beginning and end do not depart from the present thought.
Even so,
a true man has his own soaring ambition—
do not tread the path where the Tathāgata has walked.
Ascending the hall.
The Dharma has no fixed form.
Its establishment depends on people.
Suddenly taking up the staff and striking it once, he said:
This Dharma cannot be understood through conceptual thought or discrimination.
So tell me, what is it when there is no discrimination or conceptual thought?
And what is it when there is discrimination and conceptual thought?
Again striking once and giving a shout.
Raise.
Ben Yan, the two chief seats, established the monks in the hall.
Drive away the ox of the plowman.
Seize the food of the hungry.
Overturn the great sea's waters.
Punch down Mount Sumeru.
Capture tigers and rhinoceroses alive.
Seize ferocious dragons alive.
These are still not the fundamental duty of a patch-robed monk.
What then is the fundamental duty of a patch-robed monk?
Ask the two chief seats in the hall.
Ascending the hall.
Taking up the staff and striking it once, saying:
Guānyīn's wondrous power,
Can save the sufferings of the world.
A hundred flowers bloom in splendor,
Yet looking closely, there is nothing to be seen.
Then casting it down, saying:
Today is the fifth of March.
Ascending the hall.
The mind itself is Buddha, there is no other Buddha.
Buddha itself is the mind, there is no other mind.
Like a fist forming a palm, as water becomes waves.
Waves are water, the palm is the fist.
This mind belongs not to inside, outside, or in between.
This Buddha belongs not to past, future, or present.
Since it belongs not to inside, outside, or in between,
and also not to past, future, or present,
this mind and this Buddha are all provisional names.
Since they are provisional names,
then what is spoken in the entire Buddhist canon,
how could it be true?
Since it is not true,
surely Śākyamuni, the old master, did not just flap his two lips and wag his three-inch tongue in vain.
After all, what then?
Simply know to do good deeds,
and do not ask about the future.
The Master ascended the hall and cited:
One day, Línjì was attending Lì Déshān.
Déshān turned to him and said:
"This old monk is weary today."
Línjì replied:
"What is this old man babbling in his sleep?"
Déshān made to grab his staff,
but Línjì immediately overturned the meditation chair.
Yúnfēng commented:
"Two masters of the craft,
one pressing, one resisting,
slightly revealing their style—
much like holding hands to climb a high mountain.
Although it is so,
they still cannot avoid the scorn of onlookers."
The Master said:
"Old man Yúnfēng making such criticism
is much like a man from Pǔzhōu.
If Jìngshān were to see this,
he would bind them together in one bundle
and toss them into the river.
Why? Have you not heard that when the clam and snipe grapple,
both fall into the fisherman's hands?"
During the Buddha Bathing ceremony, the master addressed the assembly, saying:
Everyone splash a ladle of foul water,
To wash away the Tathāgata's pure-side defilements.
When defilements are exhausted, sentient beings' afflictions are eliminated,
And the fox then roars like a lion.
The Master ascended the hall and cited [the case]:
Yúnmén asked Cáoshān,
"What is the conduct of a śramaṇa?"
Shān said, "One who eats the monastery's grain and crops."
Mén said,
"What about going on just like this?"
Shān said,
"Can you still maintain it?"
Mén said,
"This learner can maintain it."
Shān said,
"How do you maintain it?"
Mén said,
"What's so difficult about wearing clothes and eating meals?"
Shān said,
"Why not say 'covered with hair and bearing horns'?"
Mén made a bow.
The Master said,
"These two venerable ones asking and answering like this—
they still can't avoid making a living in the wombs of donkeys and the bellies of horses.
Even so,
when a dog carries an imperial pardon, the nobles clear the way."
Entering the hall.
A monk asked,
"When it comes in the light, how is it?"
The master said,
"Large head and upturned tail, delicate."
The monk continued,
"When it comes in the dark, how is it?"
The master said,
"Wild horses neigh in the wind, hooves clattering."
The monk continued,
"Tomorrow there will be a meal at the Great Compassion Temple."
"What about that?"
The master said,
"What Xuěfēng said."
Then he said,
"When it comes in the light, strike it in the light."
"Open your eyes."
"When it comes in the dark, strike it in the dark."
"Close your eyes."
"When it comes from all directions, strike like a whirlwind."
"No lack of hesitation."
"When it comes from emptiness, strike with a flail."
"What reason is there?"
"If it doesn't come in any of these ways,"
"then it's somewhat better."
"Tomorrow there will be a meal at the Great Compassion Temple,"
"specially causing a bout of sorrow."
He added,
"The ancients spoke like this,"
"modern people bring it up like this."
"What kind of matter is accomplished in the school's teachings?"
He gave a shout.
Ascending the hall.
A monk asked,
"The past mind is unobtainable,
the present mind is unobtainable,
the future mind is unobtainable—what about this moment?"
The master said,
"Intimate words from an intimate mouth."
The monk continued,
"How should one uphold this without doubt?"
The master said,
"Just uphold it like this.
I certainly won’t deceive you."
The monk bowed.
The master then said,
"Past Buddhas
have already accomplished this gate.
Present bodhisattvas
now each enter perfect clarity.
Future practitioners
should rely on such a Dharma.
Since relying on such a Dharma,
just as the past mind is unobtainable,
the present mind is unobtainable,
the future mind is unobtainable,
and the three times are ultimately unobtainable,
how does one rely?"
If you know where to return here,
your outgoing breath does not touch the myriad conditions,
your incoming breath does not dwell in the aggregates and realms.
Constantly turning such a sutra,
hundreds of thousands of millions of volumes—
just as today, the patron invites Jìngshān’s assembly of seventeen hundred,
is what is being turned still within these hundreds of thousands of millions of volumes or not?
If it is within them,
you grasp at the characteristics of phenomena.
If it is not within them,
you grasp at the characteristics of non-phenomena.
Thus, the sutra says,
'If you grasp at the characteristics of phenomena,
you are attached to self, person, sentient being, and life span.
If you grasp at the characteristics of non-phenomena,
you are attached to self, person, sentient being, and life span.'
Right at such a moment,
is there anyone who can discern this?
If you cannot discern it,
come tomorrow, and I will tell you."
The Master ascended the hall and brought up [a case]:
A monk asked Fengxue,
"The ancient melody has no tone or rhythm—how can one harmonize with it?"
Fengxue said,
"A wooden rooster crows at midnight;
a straw dog barks at daybreak."
The Master said,
"This yellow-faced fellow from Zhèjiāng—
answering in such a way—
does not yet qualify as a descendant of Línjì.
If someone today were to ask Jìngshān,
'The ancient melody has no tone or rhythm—how can one harmonize with it?'
I would simply tell them:
'A wooden rooster crows at midnight;
a straw dog barks at daybreak.'"
The master ascended the hall and cited:
Huìchāo asked Fǎyǎn,
"What is Buddha?"
Fǎyǎn said,
"You are Huìchāo."
Xuědòu said,
"The river country's spring breeze cannot blow it awake;
The partridge calls deep within the flowers.
When waves rise high, fish transform into dragons;
Fools still bail water from the night pond."
White Cloud, our teacher-ancestor, said:
"With one big shiny coin,
I bought an oil cake,
Ate it down my belly,
And immediately was no longer hungry."
The master said:
"These two venerable elders—
One acknowledges he can hear the partridge's call,
The other knows how to buy and eat oil cakes.
But as for Huìchāo,
He still hasn't grasped the meaning of Buddha."
Upon entering the hall, hearing a sound awakens enlightenment; seeing form clarifies the mind.
Suddenly raising his staff, he said:
This is form.
Tapping it once, he said:
This is sound.
You have all seen and heard.
So which is the mind that clarifies?
Which is the Way that awakens?
Shouting once, he said:
Craving one grain of rice,
you lose half a year's provisions.
Again he tapped the staff once.
The Master ascended the hall and cited:
A monk asked Línjì,
"What is the land of the three eyes?"
Línjì said,
"I enter with you into the land of purity and wonder,
don pure garments and speak of the Dharma-body Buddha.
Again, we enter the land of non-differentiation,
don nondifferentiating garments and speak of the Reward-body Buddha.
Again, we enter the land of liberation,
don radiant garments and speak of the Transformation-body Buddha."
The Master looked around at the assembly and said:
"Do you still see old man Línjì?"
"If you haven't yet seen him,
Jìngshān will point him out for you.
Dharma-body, Reward-body, Transformation-body—
Pah! These specters and goblins!
Encounter them in the land of three eyes,
and the Man of No Rank will laugh himself to death."
The Master ascended the hall and cited [the following].
The Great Prince of Zhènfǔ asked Venerable Zhàozhōu,
"At your advanced age, how many teeth do you have left?"
Zhàozhōu said,
"Only one."
The Prince said,
"How can you eat with just one?"
Zhàozhōu said,
"Though it is only one,"
"it bites thoroughly every time."
The Master gave a shout and said,
"Enough showing off."
The master ascended the hall and cited:
A monk asked Zhàozhōu,
"What is the path without error?"
Zhàozhōu said,
"Knowing mind and seeing nature is the path without error."
The master said,
"Strike a stone man's head with a stick—
crack, crack!—discussing real matters."
Do not take it as a Chan understanding,
do not take it as a Daoist understanding.
If you want the path without error,
you must know mind and see nature to attain it.
So, which is the mind that knows?
Which is the nature that is seen?
Some, hearing such words,
then say, "Where there is water, all contain the moon;
no mountain is without clouds."
Such an understanding
is precisely like leaving Cáomén in Zhèngzhōu.
The Master ascended the hall and cited:
A monk asked Nánquán,
"Before Niútóu met the Fourth Patriarch,
why did hundred birds carry flowers in their beaks to offer him?"
Nánquán said,
"Each step treads the staircase of the Buddha."
The monk asked,
"After meeting him, why didn't they carry flowers to offer?"
Nánquán said,
"Even if they hadn't come,
they'd still be a thread's breadth better than old teacher Wáng."
Yúnmén said,
"Nánquán only understands ascending step by step to greater heights,
but doesn't understand letting go from emptiness."
The Master said,
"Although Yúnmén possesses the ability to needle the incurable and revive the paralyzed,
he still ends up treating deafness by creating muteness."
"Ascending step by step to greater heights, letting go from emptiness"—
where did this news come from?
A monk asked Yúnmén for instruction,
"What is 'ascending step by step to greater heights'?"
Yúnmén said,
"The world of Fragrant Accumulation."
The monk asked,
"What is 'letting go from emptiness'?"
Yúnmén said,
"Filling ditches and blocking gullies."
The Master said,
This only saves half.
The Master ascended the hall and cited [a case]:
Yúnmén asked the annual director,
"What did you do today?"
The director said,
"I cut thatch."
Yúnmén said,
"How many patriarchs did you cut down?"
The director said,
"Three hundred."
Yúnmén said,
"In the morning strike three thousand, in the evening strike eight hundred.
The eastern family's ladle handle is long,
the western family's ladle handle is short.
What about that?"
The director was silent.
Yúnmén picked up his staff and struck him.
The Master said:
"Though the annual director was silent,
he naturally had three hundred patriarchs to bear witness.
Though Yúnmén's order was carried out,
still, the tip of the staff has no eye."
The master ascended the hall and cited
Yúnmén's saying:
"Old Man Shakyamuni and the Emperor of Heaven
were in the central courtyard arguing vehemently over the Dharma."
The master said:
"This old fellow deserves thirty strokes of the staff.
Now, tell me, where exactly was his fault?
To accuse someone with a crime is to add that crime upon oneself."
The Master ascended the hall and cited [a case]:
Sānshèng asked Xuěfēng,
"What does the golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net feed on?"
Xuěfēng said,
"Wait until you've come out of the net, then I'll tell you."
Sānshèng said,
"A guiding teacher of fifteen hundred people,
yet you don't even understand the point of the saying."
Xuěfēng said,
"This old monk has many responsibilities in managing the monastery."
The Master [Yǎnqì] said,
"These two venerable monks—
one is as coarse as a mountain,
the other as fine as dust.
Although coarse and fine differ,
when weighed, their lightness and heaviness are just right.
Today, Jìngshān truthfully informs all of you:
Be careful not to drill tortoise shells or strike tiles [engage in futile speculation]."
The Master ascended the hall and cited [a story]:
One day the World-Honored One was walking with Ānanda.
They saw a pagoda.
The World-Honored One paid homage to it. Ānanda asked:
"Whose pagoda is this?"
The World-Honored One said:
"It is the pagoda of the buddhas of the past."
Ānanda said:
"Whose disciple is it?"
The World-Honored One said:
"It is my disciple."
Ānanda said:
"It should be thus."
The Master said:
"Ānanda's 'It should be thus' is quite good,
but unfortunately there is one move missing in between.
If you want to make the dialogue complete,
when the World-Honored One says 'It is my disciple,'
you should then say:
'You still need to bow to me three times.'
If the World-Honored One asks:
'Why do you tell me to bow to you?'
Then reply:
'It should be thus.'"
Entering the hall.
Form and mind are not two.
Self and other have no distinction.
Suddenly raising the staff, saying:
If you call this a staff,
you rub your eyes till flowers bloom.
If you do not call it a staff,
you break the home and scatter the dwelling.
After all, how should it be?
Throwing it down, saying:
The blue mountains only know how to grind away past and present;
Flowing waters—when have they ever washed away right and wrong?
The Master ascended the hall and cited [a case]:
Niàn Fǎhuá and Zhēn Yuántóu were standing in attendance by Fēngxué's side.
Fēngxué asked Zhēn:
"What is 'the World-Honored One spoke without speaking,'
and 'Kāśyapa heard without hearing'?"
Zhēn said:
"The turtledove calls from the treetop;
its intent lies in the hemp field."
Fēngxué said:
"What's the use of accumulating so much foolish merit?
Why not thoroughly investigate the words?"
He then asked Niàn:
"What about you?"
Niàn said:
"Moving expressions reveal the ancient path;
not falling into silent mechanisms."
Fēngxué said:
"Why don't you look at how Niàn Fǎhuá responds?"
The Master said:
"If this old monk had seen that old fellow speaking like this at the time,
I would have dug a deep pit
and buried them all at once.
Then led cattle to trample over it from above,
yet must let Zhēn Gōng come out ahead to be fitting."
This old monk speaking thus
is neither suppressing the strong and supporting the weak,
nor fabricating arbitrary arrangements.
If you understand,
"the turtledove calls from the treetop;
its intent lies in the hemp field,"
then you will understand "moving expressions reveal the ancient path; not falling into silent mechanisms."
These two turning phrases—
ultimately, are they one or two?
If you say they are one,
why did Fēngxué only approve of Niàn Fǎhuá
but not of Zhēn Yuántóu?
If you say they are two,
how can it be that "the setting sun and solitary duck fly together;
the autumn water and vast sky share the same color"? Ponder this.
The master ascended the hall and cited
Zhàozhōu's instruction to the assembly, saying:
"Do not pass the time idly.
Recite the Buddha, recite the Dharma, recite the Sangha."
Then a monk asked,
"What is the student's own recitation?"
Zhàozhōu said,
"Who is the one reciting?"
The monk said,
"Without companion."
Zhàozhōu scolded him, saying,
"This donkey!"
The master said,
"Although this monk is without companion,
he forms groups and bands,
clamoring enough to kill a person.
Zhàozhōu may have a fine donkey,
but it simply does not know how to eat grass."
On the anniversary of the Fifth Patriarch's passing, he ascended the platform.
Before the mountain lies a stretch of idle land.
I recall it was originally here.
Clasping hands, I earnestly inquired of the ancestral master,
only because the deed was unclear.
How many times was it sold, yet bought back by myself?
It's hard on the intermediary.
To cherish the pines and bamboos guiding the pure breeze.
Shouting once, he said:
A beggar spots petty gain.
Ascending the hall, he raised a case.
Jīnfēng addressed the assembly, saying:
"Twenty years ago, this old monk had the heart of a grandmother."
"Twenty years later, I no longer have the heart of a grandmother."
At that time, a monk came forward and asked:
"What do you mean by having the heart of a grandmother twenty years ago?"
Jīnfēng said:
"When asked about the ordinary, I answered with the ordinary."
"When asked about the sage, I answered with the sage."
The monk said:
"What do you mean by no longer having the heart of a grandmother twenty years later?"
Jīnfēng said:
"When asked about the ordinary, I do not answer with the ordinary."
"When asked about the sage, I do not answer with the sage."
The Master said:
"If Jìngshān had been there at the time,"
"I would have simply responded with our Fifth Patriarch's method."
Then raising his hand to form a turtledove's beak, he said:
"Coo-coo, coo-coo."
Ascending the hall.
At the very thought, departing from thought.
Awareness and non-awareness.
Having mind and having no mind.
Whether good or evil.
Stirred into one lump.
Taking the wrong as right.
Raising the whisk, saying:
A string pierces through the tip of the whisk.
Just go on like this.
Karmic consciousness vast and boundless, with no root to rely upon.
Now tell me, this state of karmic consciousness vast and boundless—
How far is it from old Shìjiā?
Shouting once, saying:
Almost mistakenly added a footnote.
The Master ascended the hall and cited [the case]:
Xuánshā addressed the assembly, saying:
"The venerable elders everywhere all say
they receive beings and benefit sentient beings.
But if three kinds of sick people come along,
how would you receive them?
For the blind - when you raise the gavel or hold up the whisk, they cannot see it.
For the deaf - when you speak the samādhi of words, they cannot hear it.
For the mute - when you tell them to speak, they cannot say anything.
So how would you receive them?
If you cannot receive such people,
then the Buddhadharma has no spiritual efficacy."
A monk asked Yúnmén for instruction.
Yúnmén said:
"You bow."
The monk bowed and rose.
Yúnmén poked with his staff.
The monk stepped back.
Yúnmén said:
"You are not blind."
Then he called him to come forward.
The monk came forward.
Yúnmén said:
"You are not deaf."
Then, raising his staff, he said:
"Do you understand?" The monk said: "I don't understand."
Yúnmén said:
"You are not mute."
At this, the monk attained awakening.
The Master said:
"Although this monk attained awakening,
he only understood Yúnmén's Chan.
As for Xuánshā's Chan,
he would still need to buy straw sandals [and travel more]."
The Master ascended the hall and cited [a story].
Guīshān and Yǎngshān were walking together.
Guīshān pointed to a field and said to Yǎngshān,
"This end is so high,
that end is so low."
Yǎngshān said,
"Actually, that end is high and this end is low."
Guīshān said,
"If you don't believe it,
stand in the middle of the field and look at both ends." Yǎngshān said,
"No need to stand in the middle, nor abide at either end."
Guīshān said,
"If so, look at the water - water can level things."
Yǎngshān said,
"Water also has no fixed standard.
It levels high places as high,
and low places as low."
Guīshān then ceased.
The Master said,
"Manifesting benevolence, concealing function, stirring all things,
yet not sharing the sage's worries.
How perfect is the great virtue and great enterprise!"
He gave a shout.
Ascending the hall.
A monk asked:
"Shakyamuni sealed his chamber in Magadha,
Vimalakirti remained silent in Vaishali.
Was it because deliberation remained incomplete,
or because all skills were exhausted?"
The master said:
"Deliberation remained incomplete,
all skills were exhausted."
The monk asked: "With questions and answers, elegance prevails everywhere;
without questions or answers, is there still Buddha-dharma or not?"
The master said:
"What kind of talk is this?"
The monk pressed:
"I wonder where one should practice?"
The master said:
"Practice where there is no Buddha-dharma."
Then he said:
"There are questions and answers, releasing and gathering.
There are hosts and guests, killing and enlivening.
When enlivening, there's no principle of killing;
when killing, there's no principle of enlivening.
The guest has no principle of the host;
the host has no principle of the guest.
The guest remains always guest,
the host remains always host.
Host and guest interpenetrate, pressing the sword at the gate.
Did you not see the Chan practitioner earlier ask:
'Shakyamuni sealed his chamber in Magadha,
Vimalakirti remained silent in Vaishali.
Was it because deliberation remained incomplete,
or because all skills were exhausted?'
This mountain monk answered him:
'Deliberation remained incomplete, all skills were exhausted.'
How do you all understand this?
If you can understand,
the complete guest is the host,
the complete host is the guest.
Complete gathering is releasing,
complete releasing is gathering.
Complete killing is enlivening,
complete enlivening is killing."
Then he shouted once and said:
"What kind of place is this,
to speak such words?"
He said to himself:
"Wherever there's a path to ascend,
even higher people will walk it."
The Master ascended the hall.
A monk asked,
"A sheer cliff of ten thousand fathoms—is discussion still permitted or not?"
The Master said,
"A sheer cliff of ten thousand fathoms permits no discussion."
The monk advanced and said,
"Then I know the Master's sincere heart is fully revealed."
The Master said,
"Since you know, what more are you asking?"
The monk advanced and said,
"If so, then it truly is a sheer cliff of ten thousand fathoms."
The Master said,
"While eating rice, you bit on a grain of sand."
The monk advanced and said,
"If that is the case,
then you permit this learner to advance three steps?"
The Master said,
"You don't understand—you must retreat three steps instead."
Then he said,
"The land of Magadha is still halfway there;
before Shàoshì Peak, there's not even a clue.
Discussing mysteries and speaking of wonders is like cutting good flesh to dig out a sore;
citing the ancients to illuminate the present is tossing sand and scattering soil.
How can it compare to eating when hungry, drinking when thirsty, sitting idly, and sleeping when tired?
Let the four seasons shift as they may;
none of it interferes with my affairs.
Although it is so,
one must still truly reach this realm to attain it.
But as for those who truly reach this realm,
how should they draw near?"
He shouted once and said,
"On a burn scar, you cannot apply another moxa cautery."
The Master ascended the hall and cited:
Nánquán addressed the assembly, saying:
"Mánjuśrī and Samantabhadra were fighting with each other last night at the third watch.
Each shall receive twenty blows of the stick.
Drive them out of the monastery!"
Zhàozhōu stepped forth from the assembly and asked:
"Venerable, to whom will the blows be given?"
Nánquán said:
"Where has Teacher Wáng (referring to himself) erred?"
Zhàozhōu then bowed.
The Master (speaking) said:
"Nánquán is without fault.
The mouth can bring disaster.
Zhàozhōu bowed in reverence.
The petty thieves are utterly defeated.
Jìngshān will not intervene.
The case is closed according to the record.
As for Mánjuśrī and Samantabhadra,
let them pass by for now."
The Master ascended the hall.
A monk asked,
"The present Buddha emits light,
aiding the revelation of the meaning of true reality.
What is this emitted light?"
The Master said,
"Have you eaten congee?"
The monk advanced and said,
"This student has already eaten congee."
The Master said,
"Do you still see?"
The monk advanced and said,
"I wonder if this still counts or not?"
The Master said,
"So you haven't seen after all."
Then he said,
"The present Buddha emits light,
aiding the revelation of the meaning of true reality."
Lifting his staff, he said,
"Buddhas of the past, Buddhas of the present, Buddhas of the future—
all are upon the tip of Jìngshān's staff.
Simultaneously they emit great light,
illuminating the ten-directioned dharma realms.
Directly causing mountains, rivers, the great earth, and all phenomena in their myriad forms to simultaneously bow in reverence.
What is the meaning of true reality?"
Tapping his staff once, he said,
"What follows is lengthy—we'll continue another day."
The master ascended the hall and brought up [a case]:
A monk asked Tóng'ān,
"What is the master's house style?"
Tóng'ān said,
"The golden rooster embraces its young, returning to the celestial river;
The jade rabbit conceives its offspring, heading toward the Purple Palace."
The monk said,
"If a guest suddenly arrives, how will you receive them?"
Tóng'ān said,
"The golden fruit is plucked by monkeys early in the morning;
The jade blossom is carried by phoenixes late in the evening."
The master said,
"Tóng'ān's house style is indeed extraordinary.
Jìngshān's house style, however, is not like this.
If someone were to ask,
'What is the master's house style?'
I would tell them:
'At mealtime, a bowl of mixed rice;
The rights and wrongs of Chán and the Way, I know nothing of.'
If a guest suddenly arrives, how will you receive them?
Steamed cakes and hand-pulled noodles."
Ascending the hall to conclude the summer retreat.
Taking up the staff, he said:
"One hundred and twenty days of summer,
Each day without emptiness.
The pillar displays supernatural powers,
The lantern reveals its clumsy truth.
Whether penetrating or not,
Returning instead to the staff's head to decide for you."
He struck the ground once.
Entering the hall.
A monk asked,
"When both mind and Buddha are forgotten, what then?"
The master said,
"An old woman selling fans shields her eyes from the sun with her hand."
Then he said,
"Mind and Buddha are not two.
Things and self are one suchness.
If you truly realize this one suchness,
then you won't see the names 'thing' and 'self'.
If you truly realize this non-duality,
then you won't see the forms of 'mind' and 'Buddha'.
Since you don't see the forms of mind and Buddha,
then the whole mind is Buddha,
the whole Buddha is mind.
Since you don't see the names of thing and self,
then the whole thing is self,
the whole self is thing.
If during the twenty-four hours of daily activity,
you enter realization like this,
then whether mind or Buddha,
whether self or thing,
all upside-down views,
can be fully utilized.
You'll be able to pick up a blade of grass
and make it a sixteen-foot golden body,
and take the sixteen-foot golden body
and turn it back into a blade of grass.
Even if you reach this level,
be careful not to pass under Jìngshān's gate -
I'll break your waist, don't say you weren't warned."
The Master ascended the hall and cited
the scripture, which says:
"Moreover, with extraordinary expedient means,
one aids in revealing the supreme meaning."
The Master raised his staff, struck it once, and said:
"This is the extraordinary expedient means.
What is the supreme meaning?"
He threw it down and said:
"A tiger wrapped in a paper hat—
both laughable and startling."
The Master ascended the hall and cited [the case]:
Jìngqīng asked Xuánshā,
"A student newly entering the monastic community
begs the Master to point out an entry path."
Xuánshā said,
"Do you hear the sound of Yǎnxi Brook?"
Jìngqīng said, "I hear it."
Xuánshā said,
"Enter from here."
Jìngqīng thereby gained an entry point.
The Venerable Master of the Fifth Patriarch said,
"If one truly gains entry,
one may go anywhere throughout the four directions and eight quarters.
But if not yet so,
one must not leave this place."
The Master said,
"If you wish to truly gain entry,
you must directly leave this place."
He then descended from the seat.
The lay practitioner Zhèng Yǔgōng of Twin Locusts.
Requested the ascension to the seat for Chan Master Fódēng's entombment.
Flowing ceaselessly, what is to be asked?
True illumination boundless, speaking resembles him.
Detached from form and name, people do not receive.
The sharp blade used, urgently needs grinding.
Dharma brother Chan Master Fódēng.
For twenty years wielded this sharp blade.
Enlivening the heavenly eye of people.
Detached from form and name.
Destroying falsehood and revealing truth.
Holding sideways, using upside down.
Not touching the blade's edge.
A cycle of Buddha's work already complete.
Truly surpassing before and after.
Then, looking at the assembly, said:
Today's gathering,
is precisely Chan Master Fódēng again wielding the sharp blade,
the moment for fully presenting to all, entering mud, entering water.
Is there anyone who knows gratitude?
If so, merit is not bestowed in vain.
If not yet so,
Jìngshān cannot avoid tangled vines.
Further citing an old story:
In the past, Elder Shūshān had a longevity pagoda built.
The supervisor came to report to Shūshān.
Shān asked:
How much money did you give the craftsman?
Supervisor said:
Everything is up to the Elder.
Shūshān said:
Should we give him three coins,
or two coins,
or one coin?
If you can express it,
I will personally build the pagoda.
The supervisor had no reply.
At that time, Elder Luóshān was dwelling in a hermitage at Great Ridge.
The supervisor went there.
Luóshān asked:
Where have you come from?
Supervisor said:
From Shūshān.
Luóshān said:
What words has he spoken recently?
The supervisor then recounted the previous dialogue.
Shān said:
Is there anyone who can express it?
Supervisor said:
No one has been able to express it.
Shān said:
You return and tell Shūshān:
Great Ridge, upon hearing this, says:
If you give three coins to the craftsman,
the Elder certainly will not get a pagoda in this life.
If you give two coins to the craftsman,
the Elder and the craftsman share one hand.
If you give one coin to the craftsman,
it burdens the craftsman, his eyebrows and beard will fall out.
The supervisor returned and reported this to Shūshān.
Shān then solemnly,
facing Great Ridge, bowed and sighed, saying:
Thinking there was no one,
Great Ridge has an ancient Buddha,
emitting light that shines here.
Then said to the supervisor:
You go and tell Great Ridge:
It is like a lotus in the twelfth month.
The supervisor again took these words and reported them to Luóshān.
Shān said:
Already, turtle hairs have grown several yards long.
The Master said:
Do you all know where these two elders stand?
If not yet,
today Jìngshān will mix the ancients and the moderns,
into one lump.
Shūshān's one coin, two coins, three coins,
Lay Practitioner Twin Locusts makes up two hundred thousand,
already expressing gratitude to the craftsman for Fódēng.
Avoiding making the supervisor run back and forth asking others.
A lotus in the twelfth month, one blossom is very rare.
Chan Master Fódēng collects it into the stūpa,
to serve as a model for the community.
Turtle hairs several yards long,
entrusted to Chan Master Tiānbìng,
for use as appropriate.
Dare to ask the assembly:
And say, is Jìngshān still within here or not?
After a long pause, said:
Several clear chimes beyond right and wrong,
one idle person between heaven and earth.
The Master ascended the hall.
A monk asked,
"When there is a Buddha, one cannot dwell—what about this?"
The Master said,
"To dwell is to uproot."
The monk continued,
"When there is no Buddha, one must quickly pass by—what about this?"
The Master said,
"You trouble the Ācārya."
The monk continued,
"How should a student practice?"
The Master said,
"Remove the halter and shed the horns in silence."
The monk continued,
"When meeting someone three thousand miles away, one must not make a mistaken statement—what about this?"
The Master said, "Wrong, wrong!"
The monk asked, "The 120-day summer retreat has ended, and one goes out.
If someone asks,
'What is Jìngshān's teaching?'
How should one answer?"
The Master said,
"What has Jìngshān ever said?"
The monk continued,
"But if you call it a bamboo stick, it's offensive;
if you don't call it a bamboo stick, it's contrary."
The Master said,
"How do you understand?"
The monk shouted once and said,
"Thirty years from now, many will laugh at this!"
The Master said,
"Why wait thirty years?
Even now, many are laughing at you!"
Then he said,
"I often tell you all:
If you call it a bamboo stick, it's offensive;
if you don't call it a bamboo stick, it's contrary.
Do not grasp at the moment it is raised;
do not speculate with your intellectual mind;
do not utter words;
do not remain silent.
If someone asks,
'What, after all, is it?'
Tell them,
'There is no "after all,"
nor any "what."'
At just such a moment,
the four-sided [reality] collapses to the ground, laid before you all—if your eyes are clear and your hands direct, grasp it in one leap!
Then you can encompass the three realms and uplift the four kinds of beings.
If not,
it is merely because your faculties are dull—
do not blame Jìngshān wrongly!"
The Master ascended the hall and raised [the case].
Master Zhào stated:
"For all dharmas to be non-different,
does it mean patching a duck's legs short and stretching a crane's legs long, leveling mountains and filling valleys,
only then can they be called non-different?"
Master Yúnmén declared:
"The long is naturally long,
the short is naturally short."
He further said:
"This dharma abides in its dharma position,
the appearances of the world are eternally abiding."
Then, raising his staff, he said:
"The staff is not an eternally abiding dharma."
The Master then lifted his staff, addressed the assembly, and said:
"Gouge out the pupil from your eye—
where do you see Master Zhào's dharma of non-difference?"
"Knock out the marrow from your bones—
where do you see Master Yúnmén's dharma of eternal abiding?"
He threw down the staff and said:
"See with your body divided in two places."
He then descended from the seat.
The Master ascended the hall.
A monk asked,
"Our school has no words or phrases,
and truly not a single dharma is given to others. What about this?"
The Master said,
"Five flavors drill the steelyard weight."
The monk pressed,
"Why then do you externally broadcast the family's shame?"
The Master said,
"Why is your tongue touching the ground?"
The monk continued,
"Instead, I've been led along by the Reverend."
The Master then struck him.
A question: When Qiánfēng addressed the assembly saying,
"Raise one, do not raise two.
Let go of one move and it falls into second place."
What is the meaning?
The Master said,
"Hanging a winter melon from a camel's tail."
The monk pressed,
"Is the student permitted to turn around and exhale or not?"
The Master said,
"You are permitted to turn around.
How will you exhale?"
The monk stepped forward and made a "hss" sound.
The Master said,
"This fellow playing with mud balls!"
The monk continued,
"Just as Yúnmén said,
'One comes from Tiāntāi but goes toward Jìngshān.'
What about that?"
The Master said,
"A mouse eating salt."
The monk pressed,
"If so, then one knows its flavor?"
The Master said,
"Quickly bow three times."
Then he said,
"Long rain has not cleared,
suddenly heaven and earth are pure.
The matter at the Patriarch's gate—
what need is there to further display it?"
The Master ascended the hall and cited:
A monk asked Yúnmén,
"What is the true Dharma eye?"
Yúnmén said, "Universal."
Another monk asked Fēngxué,
"What is the true Dharma eye?"
Fēngxué said, "Blind."
The Master said,
"These two venerable masters answered the same turning phrase.
Is there superiority or inferiority between them?
If you say there is superiority or inferiority,
you are truly blind.
If you say there is no superiority or inferiority,
you are truly universal.
After all, how should it be?
Clouds linger over the mountain peaks, yet not completely at leisure;
Water flows beneath the valley stream, exceedingly busy with life."
Vice Minister Zhāng arrived at the main hall.
A monk asked,
"When Dàdiān drove away the head seat for Hán Wéngōng,
what was the meaning?"
The master said,
"A catfish climbing a bamboo pole—
one day, a thousand miles."
The monk continued,
"This learner does not understand,
I beg the master to bestow compassion."
The master said,
"You want a second ladle of foul water?"
The monk continued,
"Just as the head seat also clicked his teeth three times,
where was the fault?"
The master said,
"The fault lies in clicking the teeth."
The monk continued,
"It's better not to slander the head seat."
The master said,
"What principle do you see
that makes you speak like this?"
The monk continued,
"Who knows that beyond the distant misty waves,
there are other good thoughts?"
The master said,
"You'd better not slander Jìngshān."
The monk continued,
"If today the vice minister were to ask,
'Reverend, how old are you?'
then what would you say?"
The master said,
"Tell him one hundred and twelve years old."
The monk continued,
"Can this be called slandering Jìngshān?"
The master said,
"Now you're slandering the vice minister."
Then he said,
"The ancients said,
'Our school has no phrases,
truly not a single dharma to give people.'
Speaking like this
is already being fully immersed in the latrine pit.
How much worse to step forward—what about that?"
Questioning upward and downward, the three essentials and three mysteries, snow in a silver bowl, hiding in the Big Dipper—what is the meaning?
Isn't this digging a latrine pit beside the latrine pit?
Although it is like this,
if within the latrine pit,
one knows some breath,
then one knows that all buddhas of the three times, ancestral teachers through the ages, old venerables under heaven, and all knowledgeable ones past and present
all turn the great dharma wheel within the latrine pit.
If not yet so,
be careful not to get stuck in the latrine pit.
The Master ascended the hall and cited [the case]:
Mǎzǔ was with Xītáng, Nánquán, and Bǎizhàng
enjoying the moon on the Mid-Autumn Festival.
Mǎzǔ pointed at the moon and said,
"What is it like at just such a moment?"
Xītáng said,
"It's just right for spiritual cultivation."
Bǎizhàng said,
"It's just right for making offerings."
Nánquán shook his sleeves and immediately left.
Mǎzǔ said,
"The scriptures enter the treasury, Chan returns to the sea.
Only Pǔyuàn alone transcends beyond all things."
The Master said,
"Do you know where these four elders stand?
If you still don't know,
listen to this verse:
In a prosperous nation, talented scholars are valued;
In a wealthy family, young children are pampered.
Everyone extend a hand - no quarter given between them."
The Master ascended the hall.
A monk asked,
"When ordinary people are fully endowed with the Dharma
yet remain unaware of it, what then?"
The Master said,
"Excellent news indeed!"
The monk continued,
"When saints are fully endowed with the Dharma
yet fail to comprehend it, what then?"
The Master said,
"Also excellent news!"
The monk pursued,
"Pray tell, what kind of news is this?"
The Master said,
"Seeing people, one vainly understands laughter;
Playing with objects, one knows not their names."
The monk continued,
"If one fails to obtain flowing water,
should one then cross over to another mountain?"
The Master said,
"Xiū Shānzhǔ has arrived!"
Someone asked: "When a person stands atop a solitary peak
with no path to emerge, what then?"
The Master said,
"Excellent news!"
The questioner continued,
"Venerable, why do you consistently stand like a cliff of ten thousand ren?"
The Master said,
"You try speaking a phrase from that cliff-standing position!"
The questioner said,
"Stir the long river into curdled cheese,
Transform the great earth into yellow gold."
The Master said,
"Now, take it slowly."
Then he said:
"One person on a solitary peak with no path to emerge;
Another at the crossroads with no direction to turn.
This is not Śākyamuni, nor is it Vimalakīrti.
If you can recognize their true faces here,
Then you'll understand what Xiū Shānzhǔ meant by
'Ordinary people fully endowed with the Dharma remain unaware,'
'Saints fully endowed with the Dharma fail to comprehend.'
If saints comprehend, they become ordinary people;
If ordinary people become aware, they become saints.
Is there anyone here who recognizes this?
If you recognize it,
Ordinary people, saints, solitary peaks,
And crossroads are all right here.
If you haven't recognized it yet,
Set it aside and examine it when it cools."
The Master ascended the hall and cited:
A monk asked Patriarch Wǔzǔ,
"Before Niútóu met the Fourth Patriarch,
why did hundreds of birds offer him flowers in their beaks?"
The Patriarch said,
"Wealth and honor are what people desire."
"After meeting, why didn't they offer flowers?"
The Patriarch said,
"Poverty and lowliness are what people detest."
The Master said,
"The Patriarch answering in this way,
though indeed skillfully responding to the opportunity,
how could his words avoid startling contemporary listeners?"
Jìngshān also has two turning phrases
to meet with the Patriarch:
"Before Niútóu met the Fourth Patriarch,
why did hundreds of birds offer him flowers in their beaks?"
Placing an owl-shaped ornament on a thatched hut.
"After meeting, why didn't they offer flowers?"
Digging a latrine inside the Buddha hall.
A monk asked upon entering the hall:
"When speech, silence, movement, and stillness are all irrelevant,
and even when not speech, silence, movement, or stillness are also irrelevant, what then?"
The master said:
"You reap what you sow."
The master continued:
"Even if you reach such a state, it's still irrelevant."
The master then struck him.
He then said:
"Buddhas and sentient beings originally have no different forms.
It is only due to confusion and enlightenment that there are different paths.
Although called different paths,
when confused, this very thing was never confused;
when enlightened, this very thing was never enlightened.
Therefore it is said:
'Just as the nature of empty space is not any form,
yet it does not reject the manifestation of all forms.'
If one can see in this way,
only then can one believe that:
'Before leaving Tuṣita Heaven, he had already descended to the royal palace;
before leaving his mother's womb, he had already completed the salvation of beings.'
These are true words.
These are not deceptive words.
If you can believe this, you will receive endless benefits.
If you cannot believe it, you are still within it."
Entering the hall.
Raise one, do not raise two.
Let go of the first move and it falls into the second.
If there is a patch-robed monk who knows he’s full after eating and knows he’s quenched after drinking,
there’s no need for Yúnmén to come out and beat around the bush.
Since Yúnmén is not allowed to beat around the bush,
is there anyone now who knows he’s full after eating and knows he’s quenched after drinking?
Even if there is, it’s a Huánglóng spirit.
The Master ascended the hall.
A monk asked,
"When 'empty-handed, one holds a hoe;
walking, one rides a water buffalo'—what about it?"
The Master said,
"An eel slips into an oil jar."
The monk continued,
"Thinking the barbarian's beard is red,
there's yet another with a red beard."
The Master said,
"A person crosses over the bridge;
the bridge flows, but the water does not flow."
The monk went on,
"Just as Great Master Fù used to connect with people in fish markets and wine shops,
I wonder where does the Master connect with people?"
The Master said,
"I connect with people everywhere."
The monk asked further,
"I wonder how many you have connected with?"
The Master said,
"Just you, one lacquer bucket, don't understand!"
Then he said,
"Empty-handed, one holds a hoe—
there's croton seed in the rice.
Walking, one rides a water buffalo—
stubbing one's toe.
A person crosses over the bridge—
deceiving how many people.
The bridge flows, but the water does not flow—
that's somewhat better.
If you can grasp it like this,
only then believe that
Maitreya is truly Maitreya,
dividing his body into hundreds of millions.
Constantly showing people of the time,
yet people of the time all fail to recognize him."
Striking the meditation seat, he descended.
The Master ascended the hall.
A monk asked,
"When nothing at all comes, what then?"
The Master said,
"Moving expression reveals the ancient path,
Not falling into silent mechanism."
The monk advanced and said,
"Like cutting a single strand of silk—
One cut severs all."
The Master said,
"A wealthy family's child is spoiled."
The monk advanced and said,
"When the mechanism wheel turns, even the adept is confused."
The Master said,
"Where does the mechanism wheel turn?"
The monk advanced and said,
"Where the partridge calls, a hundred flowers are fragrant."
The Master said,
"You haven't grasped it."
The monk advanced and said,
"Venerable, where do you see Pǔhuà?"
The Master said,
"Where is Pǔhuà for me to see?"
The monk advanced and said,
"The arrow pierces the red sun's shadow—
Only then is one an eagle shooter."
The Master said,
"Still, you haven't grasped it."
Then he said,
"The arrow pierces the red sun's shadow—
Only then is one an eagle shooter."
Tell me, before the arrow leaves the string, at the edge of the red sun's shadow,
Is there this message or not?"
Once the arrow has left the string,
Where does this message land?
If you know where it lands,
One arrowhead breaks three barriers,
Clearly revealing the path after the arrow.
But if not,
Then return beneath the crossbow and take shelter.
The master ascended the hall and cited:
A monk asked Bajiao,
"Without falling into all conditions,
please, Master, point directly."
Bajiao said,
"There is asking and there is answering."
The master said,
"Although Bajiao was adept at handling matters on the blade's edge,
upon careful examination,
he greatly resembles one fleeing from his shadow at noon.
He let down this monk.
If someone were to ask Jingshan today,
'Without falling into all conditions, please, Master, point directly,'
I would simply tell him,
'Although the猩猩 can speak,
after all, it is but an animal.'"
The Master ascended the hall.
A monk asked, "The mind-seal of the Patriarch—
its function resembles that of an iron ox.
Let's set that aside for now.
Just tell me, during the nine years of facing the wall,
what matter was clarified?"
The Master said,
"Standing firm across the universe,
who is the one that dares to step forward?"
The monk advanced and said,
"When he returned westward with a single sandal, was it truly authentic?"
The Master said,
"Not authentic."
The monk advanced and said,
"I also know the Reverend is accustomed to using this tactic."
The Master said,
"Yes."
The monk then shouted.
The Master also shouted.
Then he said,
"A moment ago, Shànxiū gave a shout
that shook heaven and earth.
Jìngshān followed with a shout
that was utterly baseless.
If you understand it at the point of being baseless,
you'll know how to use a broken rope
to pierce the nostrils of all under heaven.
But if you take it on at the point of shaking heaven and earth,
your own nostrils will be pierced by others with a broken rope.
Right at such a moment,
how can one avoid this fault?
Hah! Hah! Nowhere to go, nowhere to go!"
Entering the hall.
A monk asked:
Raise one, do not raise two.
Let one go and it lands on the second.
This student has come forward.
I ask the Master to raise one.
The Master said:
Six sixes are still thirty-six as before.
The monk advanced and said:
I wonder if this is real or not?
The Master said:
Only this one matter is real.
Any other two are not true.
The monk bowed.
The Master then said:
Raise one, do not raise two.
Let one go and it lands on the second.
Just like Zhènzhōu's radish head.
I wonder in Língzhào's basket.
can it be placed or not?
If you can produce a turning phrase here,
yesterday someone came from Tiāntāi,
but went to Nányuè instead.
If you cannot produce one,
this is what Xuěfēng said.
The master ascended the hall and cited:
A monk asked the Sixth Patriarch,
"Who obtained the essence of Huángméi?"
The Patriarch said,
"One who understands the Buddha-Dharma obtained it."
The monk said,
"Did you, Venerable, obtain it?"
The Patriarch said,
"I did not obtain it."
The monk said,
"Why did you not obtain it?"
The Patriarch said, "I do not understand the Buddha-Dharma."
The master addressed the assembly, saying:
"Do you see the Patriarch?"
"If you do not see him,"
"Jìngshān will point him out for you."
"Plantain, plantain, having leaves but no trunk."
"Suddenly, a fierce gust of wind arises,"
"Just like in the Great Xiàngguó Temple of Dōngjīng,"
"Under the northern corner of the eastern corridor in the thirty-six courtyards,"
"Venerable Wáng's tattered monastic robe."
"After all, how is it?"
"Return to the hall and drink tea."
Ascending the hall.
A monk asked:
The ancients said:
It is like a person climbing a tree.
With the mouth holding a branch, the hands do not grasp branches,
the feet do not step on the tree.
I wonder, is there still any opportunity to respond?
The master said:
The response is already given.
The monk said:
This student asked about the situation in the tree,
why did the venerable respond from under the tree?
The master said:
Precisely because you asked from under the tree.
The monk continued:
Can this deceive the assembly's eyes?
The master said:
Clearly, it cannot deceive.
The monk continued:
Just as when the tree has not yet grown and the message has not yet moved,
from where did Xiāngyán
obtain this topic?
The master said:
He obtained it from your lacquer bucket.
The monk continued:
Just as the venerable said:
To call it a bamboo stick is to touch,
not to call it a bamboo stick is to turn away.
Is there still a way to help people?
The master said: There is not.
The monk continued:
If so, then it becomes an empty setup.
The master said:
Empty setup.
Then he said:
It is like a person climbing a tree.
With the mouth holding a branch,
the hands do not grasp branches,
the feet do not step on the tree.
If someone under the tree asks about the meaning from the West,
to answer him would mean losing one's life,
not to answer him
would go against his question.
At that moment, as soon as Xiāngyán spoke thus,
there was one who did not agree,
called Preceptor Hǔtóu,
who came forth from the assembly and said:
I will not ask about the situation in the tree;
speak a word about under the tree.
The master said: Dangerous.
Xiāngyán laughed heartily.
The master said: Dangerous.
Here at Jìngshān,
these two dangers—
one danger is like the sky covering all,
like the earth supporting all;
one danger has nothing to do with understanding.
Is there anyone who can distinguish them?
If you can distinguish them,
not only will you personally see Xiāngyán,
but you will also leave Preceptor Hǔtóu with no place to settle his body and life.
If not,
Jìngshān will take this ready-made case
and add a footnote for all of you:
To call it a bamboo stick is to touch,
not to call it a bamboo stick is to turn away.
The master ascended the hall.
A monk asked,
"The teachings say:
This is true diligence.
This is called the true Dharma offering to the Tathāgata.
Since a dog has no Buddha-nature,
what can be called the true Dharma?"
The master said,
"Just this 'no Buddha-nature'
is the true Dharma."
The monk continued,
"According to this student's understanding,
it is not so."
The master said,
"You try to fabricate and see."
The monk bowed.
The master said,
"Just this bowing
is fabrication."
Then he said,
"This is true diligence.
This is called the true Dharma offering to the Tathāgata.
Since a dog has no Buddha-nature,
what can be called the true Dharma?"
This mountain monk says,
"Just this 'no Buddha-nature'
is the true Dharma.
Can all of you believe this?
If you can believe it,
the assembly on Vulture Peak is clearly still gathered.
If you cannot believe it,
you must wait until the future to ask Maitreya."
The master ascended the hall and cited:
A monk asked Zhàozhōu:
"I have heard that
you personally met Nánquán.
Is this true?"
Zhàozhōu said:
"Zhènzhōu produces giant radish heads."
Another monk asked, "When all phenomena return to One,
where does the One return to?"
Zhàozhōu said:
"In Qīngzhōu I made a cloth robe weighing seven jīn."
Yúnjū Shǔn the Elder said:
"Zhènzhōu radishes are large,
Qīngzhōu cloth robes are heavy.
If you wish to understand the meaning within,
the rooster crows at the fifth watch."
The master said:
"Yúnjū speaking like this
is much like being unable to forget old habits.
But if it were Jìngshān, I would not say so:
Zhènzhōu radishes have always been large,
Qīngzhōu cloth robes clearly show their weight.
When monks gather to seek the true meaning,
it's like mosquitoes and gnats biting an iron nail."
Ascending the hall.
A monk asked:
Yǎngshān said,
"Spiritual powers and playful displays are certainly not absent,
but the Venerable One's Buddha-dharma must be returned to this old monk to be complete."
I wonder, what principle does he base this on?
The master said:
"You only know how to open your mouth and laugh,
unaware that your tongue has grown long."
The monk continued:
"If so, then today I have been laughed at by the venerable master."
The master said:
"Raising your voice to stop the echo—what's the use?"
The monk continued:
"Spiritual powers and playful displays are certainly not absent,
but the Venerable One's Buddha-dharma must be returned to Jìngshān to be complete."
The master said:
"Do you still see Jìngshān?"
The monk continued:
"Stop showing off."
The master said:
"Having eyes but being like the blind."
Then he said:
"Spiritual powers and playful displays—
Yǎngshān clearly doesn't understand.
The essential wonder of Buddha-dharma—
the arhat clearly doesn't know.
Although they don't know each other,
nevertheless each lacks nothing.
Since nothing is lacking,
the long is the long dharmakāya,
the short is the short dharmakāya,
the round is the round dharmakāya,
the square is the square dharmakāya.
If you awaken in this way,
then you'll know the long is not long,
the short is not short,
the round is not round,
the square is not square.
Since none of them are,
what then do you call the dharmakāya?"
He gave a shout and said:
"Almost fitting to detain a prisoner to grow wisdom."
Ascending the hall on the Sacred Festival.
After lifting the incense,
suddenly thunder rumbled and a downpour ensued.
He then said:
"The Dharma thunder rumbles, the Dharma drum beats,
Spreading compassionate clouds and sprinkling sweet dew."
Now the Dharma thunder has rumbled,
the Dharma drum has beaten,
compassionate clouds have spread,
and sweet dew has sprinkled.
In terms of phenomena, it corresponds;
in terms of principle, it corresponds.
Since both phenomena and principle correspond,
how then should we understand this?
Descending the seat with the assembly,
they proceeded to the Great Buddha Hall,
to inaugurate the Sacred Festival of the Heavenly Dragon.
The Master ascended the hall and cited [the case]:
Dòngshān asked the abbot of Sānfēng Hermitage,
"What is your name?"
The abbot said,
"Dào Yīng."
Dòngshān said,
"Why not speak from the highest standpoint?"
The abbot said,
"If I speak from the highest standpoint,
then I would not be called Dào Yīng."
Dòngshān deeply approved of this.
The Master said,
"If Dào Yīng speaks from the highest standpoint, then he would not be called Dào Yīng.
Since he is not called Dào Yīng,
it cannot be called the highest standpoint either.
Since it is not speaking from the highest standpoint,
then how can one comprehend Dòngshān's meaning?"
After a long pause, he said,
"The wise should listen carefully and seize it swiftly—
Do not wait until the moment passes and lose your head."
Venerable Xuědòu Chí arrived at the hall for the sermon.
A monk asked,
"Yǎngshān said,
'If my uncle from Dōngsì Temple were here,
Huìjì would not suffer loneliness.'
Now that Venerable Xuědòu has finally arrived today,
I wonder how we should receive you?"
The master said,
"Ancient and modern."
The monk continued,
"If so, not only would Jìngshān not suffer loneliness,
but also the seventeen hundred assembly would have someone to rely on."
The master said,
"What principle do you see in this?"
The monk continued,
"Like two mirrors reflecting each other,
clearly without any flaw."
The master said,
"Break the mirror,
and I will meet with you."
The monk continued,
"If two mouths have no tongue,
that is our school's essential meaning.
How then should we discuss it?"
The master said,
"Holding the bridge pillar while bathing, grasping the cable while releasing the boat."
The monk continued,
"What about the essential meaning of Línjì's school?"
The master said,
"Shut your dog's mouth."
Then he said,
"Yǎngshān said,
'If my uncle from Dōngsì Temple were here,
Huìjì would not suffer loneliness.'
Yǎngshān only knew himself,
but didn't know others.
Jìngshān is not like this.
If my uncle Xuědòu were here,
all monks under heaven would not suffer loneliness.
Why? Haven't you heard ancient Xuědòu's saying:
'Holding cold wood in hand - the complete mechanism is laughable;
Wielding autumn water sideways - half raised can be extinguished.
Making those who gaze from the eight extremes not contend, seeing this person - driving the lofty stump.'"
Ascending the hall.
Today is the first day of the fourth month.
Monks lay down their staffs.
Although silent illumination is not permitted,
everyone must face the wall.
Since silent illumination is not permitted,
why then must one face the wall?
Have you not heard the words of Elder Báiyún:
"Add a little where there is too much,
subtract a little where there is too little."
Bathing the Buddha, ascending the hall.
The plantain, though earless, hears thunder and blooms.
Sunflowers, though eyeless, follow the sun as it turns.
Even Śākyamuni, the old master, is without birth,
Yet each year on this day, he is bathed once.
Since there is no birth, what is it that is being bathed?
If there is a branch, cling to the branch;
If there is no branch, cling to the precedent.
The master ascended the hall.
A monk asked,
"The Way has no fixed direction;
it is illuminated by people.
The Dharma transcends seeing and hearing;
it is discerned by wisdom.
If not a single thought arises,
is there still Buddhadharma or not?"
The master said, "There is no Buddhadharma."
The monk continued,
"Why is there no Buddhadharma?"
The master said,
"Because you dwell in that one thought."
The monk continued,
"Where does the venerable see this student's that one thought?"
The master said,
"It has arisen."
Then he said,
"Not giving rise to a single thought
is not yet the place where you all can relinquish your lives.
When a single thought just arises,
it is like a dragon obtaining water,
or a tiger leaning against a mountain.
The whole being comes thus,
the whole being abides thus.
If you simply comprehend it thus,
then you must buy one hundred twenty pairs of straw sandals and go on pilgrimage.
Why is it so?
In my king's treasury, there is no such knife."
Vice Minister Zhāng requested the master to ascend the seat.
A monk asked,
"From all directions we gather together,
Each one learning non-action.
This is the arena for selecting Buddhas,
Return with an empty mind to pass the imperial examination.
What about this moment?"
The master said,
"What does the topic say?"
The monk continued,
"Clearly evident before our eyes."
The master said,
"Meditators like hemp and millet are everywhere."
The monk continued,
"How can we all climb the immortal cassia tree together,
And pluck the foremost branch of the toad palace?"
The master said,
"This fellow today is speaking nonsense."
The monk continued,
"Even so,
This summer I'll definitely become the Chan top graduate."
Then he bowed.
Someone asked, "How does the Vice Minister's understanding compare to last year's?"
The master said,
"This year and last year are separated by only three hundred and sixty years."
The questioner continued,
"Don't slander the Vice Minister.
The Vice Minister doesn't have this message."
The master said,
"Since you don't have this message,
Why is Liǎoyīn speaking recklessly?"
The questioner continued,
"Borrowing someone's mouth to say a word or two,
What harm could there be?"
Then he bowed.
The master then said,
"What is spoken through borrowed mouths
Has nothing to do with one's own affair.
What flows from one's own heart and mind -
Bystanders with eyes are like the blind,
With mouths like the mute.
If you comprehend it just like this,
Becoming the Chan top graduate isn't difficult.
Even if you reach this point, you've only entered Jìngshān's gate,
Not yet entered Jìngshān's room.
If you enter Jìngshān's room,
Then the Chan top graduate becomes useful.
Only when the Chan top graduate becomes useful,
Does the Confucian top graduate become useless.
I dare ask the assembly,
Why is the former useful?
Why is the latter useless?"
Then looking left and right he said,
"Do you know where Jìngshān stands?"
If you know where Jìngshān stands,
Then the Chan top graduate is the Confucian top graduate,
And the Confucian top graduate is the Chan top graduate.
Now, setting aside both Chan and Confucianism,
Tell me,
What is the direct statement right before you?"
Know that the dead Instructor Zhāng
Is the living top graduate lord.
Ascending the hall for the Summer Retreat.
Mañjuśrī dwells in three places.
Master Zhìgōng is no idle monk.
When Mahākāśyapa wishes to enforce the true command,
he inevitably sees ghosts before his eyes.
Pray tell,
how should today's affairs be handled within Jìngshān's gate?
After descending the seat, all shall perform three prostrations in mutual reverence.
The master ascended the hall and cited:
A monk asked Yúnmén,
"What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma body?"
Yúnmén said,
"Hiding oneself within the Big Dipper."
The master said,
When the elder Yúnmén spoke thus,
he only answered the phrase of the Dharma body,
but did not answer the phrase that penetrates the Dharma body.
If someone today were to ask Jìngshān,
"What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharma body?"
I would immediately tell them:
"Setting up a night market in a gnat's eye,
Swinging on a tiger's tongue."
Ascending the hall.
Today is again the Dragon Boat Festival.
Mañjuśrī and Sudhana are ceaselessly busy.
The medicine to kill or revive people proves ineffective.
I add three catties of iron behind my own head.
Suddenly taking up the staff and striking it once, he said:
The wondrous power of Guānyīn’s wisdom,
Can save the sufferings of the world.
Then throwing it down, he said:
What is this iron snake burrowing into the earth?
The Master ascended the hall and cited:
Mǎzǔ ordered Zhìcáng to deliver a letter to National Unity Ancestor on the mountain.
The Ancestor opened the envelope,
saw a circle,
and immediately took a brush to put a dot in its center.
Nányáng National Preceptor Zhōng, hearing of this, remarked:
"Even Qīn Master was deluded by Master Mǎ."
The Master said:
"Master Mǎ in midwinter's bitter cold,
National Unity in early summer's growing heat—
though cold and heat differ,
neither misses their season.
Why then did National Preceptor Zhōng say,
'Even Qīn Master was deluded by Master Mǎ'?
Do you fully understand?
Lotus leaves stir without wind—
surely fish swim beneath.
He descended the seat.
Ascending the hall, he raised [the case].
National Teacher Dàoyǎn said,
"In gradual speech, one returns to the ordinary and accords with the Way;
In sudden discourse, one leaves no trace of evidence."
Yúnmén said,
"When raising the mallet, lifting the whisk, or snapping the fingers—
If one examines carefully,
It is still not without traces of evidence."
The master gave a shout and said,
"What is this dream-talk?"
Then he raised his whisk,
And again snapped his fingers, saying:
"Jìngshān now raises the whisk and snaps his fingers.
If you seek traces of evidence here,
You will fall into hell as swiftly as an arrow's flight."
The Master ascended the hall and cited:
Dàowú addressed the assembly, saying:
Loftiness is not found at the highest peak,
Wealth is not found at Fúyán,
Joy is not found in heaven,
Suffering is not found in hell.
Acquaintances fill the world,
But how many are truly known to the heart?
The Master said:
Jìngshān, however, is not so.
Loftiness is at the highest peak,
Wealth is at Fúyán,
Joy is in heaven,
Suffering is in hell.
Who knows that beneath the bamboo hat,
Lies one who was sorrowful long ago.
The Master ascended the hall and cited [a case]:
Mùzhōu asked a scholar,
"Venerable sir, what classic do you study?"
The scholar said, "I study the Yìjīng."
Mùzhōu said,
"The Yìjīng states:
'The common people use it daily but are unaware of it.'
Unaware of what?"
The scholar said,
"They are unaware of the Way."
Mùzhōu said,
"Then what is the Way?"
The scholar was silent.
Mùzhōu said,
"Indeed, you are unaware."
The Master said,
"Although the scholar was silent,
he silently understood Mùzhōu.
He was only missing the final step."
If I, Jìngshān, had seen Mùzhōu say 'Indeed, you are unaware,'
I would simply clap my hands and laugh heartily.
Surely Mùzhōu would not have been at a loss.
The Master, in the twenty-sixth year of the Shàoxīng era.
On the twenty-third day of the eleventh month.
Held an inauguration ceremony at the Bào'ēn Guāngxiào Chán Temple in Míngzhōu.
After the declaration was read, incense was offered, and prayers for the emperor concluded,
he then took his seat.
The Tiāntóng monk struck the gavel and said:
“Assembly of dragons and elephants of the Dharma feast,
contemplate the supreme meaning.”
The Master said:
“The supreme meaning—
the Tiāntóng monk has struck it into being with one blow of the gavel.
Is there anyone who knows kindness and repays kindness?”
A monk asked:
“When Bǎoshòu held his inauguration,
Sānshèng stepped forward to assist.
This student has come forth;
I wish to hear the prayer for the emperor.”
The Master said:
“Oxhide stretched over a pillar.”
The monk continued:
“Heaven’s height and earth’s depth are boundless;
the ocean of the Buddha’s merit is truly immeasurable.”
The Master said:
“The bottomless bowl passed down by a thousand sages.”
The monk advanced: “Just at such a time, how is it pecked?”
The Master said:
“If you look, you’ll have a share.”
The monk advanced:
“Is this not the matter of knowing kindness and repaying kindness?”
The Master said:
“Feel free to drill tortoiseshell and strike tiles.”
The monk advanced:
“No way to repay the virtue of the Son of Heaven;
only relying on this day’s single stick of incense.”
The Master said:
“Still somewhat close.”
A question: “The World-Honored One held up a flower, and Mahākāśyapa smiled.
The World-Honored One said:
‘I have the treasury of the true Dharma eye, the wondrous mind of Nirvāṇa,
and entrust it to Mahākāśyapa.’
What is the treasury of the true Dharma eye?”
The Master said:
“Pluck out the nail from the eye.”
The monk advanced:
“What is the wondrous mind of Nirvāṇa?”
The Master said:
“Quickly bow three times.”
The monk advanced:
“If I had not come forward to ask this,
how would I know the fully revealed mechanism of the Dharma King?”
The Master said: “Know.”
The monk advanced:
“Just as this assembly today,
how does it differ from Língshān?”
The Master said: “Universal.”
The monk advanced:
“If so, then from now on the Buddha’s sun increases in radiance,
and the wind of the Way will forever blow.”
The Master said:
“Again, foul water splashed on people.”
The monk bowed.
The Master then said:
“The essential wonder of the Buddha-Dharma
is apart from the characteristic of verbal explanation,
apart from the characteristic of written words,
apart from the characteristic of mental discrimination.
It cannot be sought with a mind,
nor attained with no-mind.
It cannot be reached through language,
nor penetrated through silence.
Like a poison-smeared drum—
hearing it, one’s brain bursts open.
Like a mass of fierce fire—
approaching it, one’s face is scorched.
Truly it is like a cliff ten thousand ren high,
cutting off saints and ordinary beings alike.
Even if one had the wisdom of Śāriputra,
or the eloquence of Vimalakīrti,
and all Buddhas of the three times appeared simultaneously,
they would still have to sink three feet into the ground. Such is its autonomy,
such is its awesome power.
Only allowed for the old barbarian to know,
not allowed for the old barbarian to understand.
How can one open one’s mouth here?
Yet, officially, not even a needle is permitted;
privately, a carriage and horse can pass.
Allowing a single thread’s passage, there is still room for discussion.” Suddenly raising his staff and striking it once, he said:
“Do you hear?
All obstacles are themselves ultimate enlightenment.
Gaining thought or losing thought are none other than liberation.
Perfecting dharmas or destroying dharmas are both called Nirvāṇa.
Wisdom and foolishness are equally prajñā.”
Striking once more, he said:
“The sun overflows the eyes;
for ten thousand li, not a single cloud hangs.
Ancient Buddhas and pillars interact;
Xīnluó and Zhānbō wrestle head to head.
That aside,
you all, just as Mǎzǔ said, ‘This very mind is Buddha’—
how do you discuss it?
Do you understand thoroughly?
Peace was originally achieved by the general;
yet the general is allowed to see peace.”
Striking once more, he cited:
“The king of Western India asked Venerable Pārthiva:
‘I wish to become a Buddha;
I do not know what is Buddha?’
The Venerable said:
‘To see nature is Buddha.’
The king said:
‘Does the master see nature?’
The Venerable said:
‘I see the Buddha-nature.’
The king said: ‘Where is nature?’
The Venerable said:
‘Nature is in functioning.’
The king said:
‘What functioning?
I do not see it now.’
The Venerable said:
‘It is functioning now,
but the king himself does not see it.’
The king said:
‘Does it exist in me?’
The Venerable said:
‘If the king functions, there is nothing that is not it.
If the king does not function, its substance is also hard to see.’
The king said:
‘When functioning,
in how many places does it appear?’
The Venerable said:
‘When it appears,
there should be eight places.’
The king said:
‘Please explain to me the eight places of Buddha-nature.’
The Venerable said:
‘In the womb, it is called body;
in the world, it is called person;
in the eye, it is called seeing;
in the ear, it is called hearing;
in the nose, it distinguishes scents;
in the tongue, it discusses;
in the hand, it grasps;
in the feet, it runs.
Fully manifesting, it encompasses all;
gathering in a grain of sand, it contains the entire world.
Those who know recognize it as Buddha-nature;
those who do not know call it spirit.’
Hearing these words, the king’s mind opened in enlightenment.”
The Master said:
“I dare ask,
the great assembly of the Dharma feast:
Tell me,
did the king of Western India realize Buddha-nature,
or did he realize spirit?
If you say he realized it in the eight places,
that is only spirit.
If apart from the eight places,
what then is called Buddha-nature?
If you can discern this here,
the emperor’s kindness and the Buddha’s kindness are both fully repaid at once.
If you cannot discern it,
today Yùwáng will add an annotation for you all.”
After a long pause, he said:
“The yuèzhuó and qílín are both auspicious;
sandalwood and campaka share the same fragrance.”
The Tiāntóng monk again struck the gavel and said:
“Carefully observe the Dharma of the Dharma King;
the Dharma of the Dharma King is thus.”
The Master addressed the assembly:
“Remember the words of the Tiāntóng monk.”
Then he descended from the seat.
Upon entering the monastery, the abbot summoned the assembly and said:
Here is the great furnace that cooks buddhas and patriarchs, forging life and death with its merciless hammer.
Do not blame the host for being faceless.
The Dharma is thus—it is not forced.
Since the Dharma is such,
and it is not forced either,
then tell me:
How about the very first phrase?
Do you fully understand?
When the fishing rod is chopped up, replant bamboos anew;
Cease when opportune, without counting efforts or time.
The master ascended the hall.
A monk asked,
"When the head is split open and the eyes bulge out,
in all directions, surging east and sinking west—
what about when Yángqí's three-legged donkey kicks up its hooves and walks?
What is the meaning?"
The master said,
"There is no meaning."
The monk continued,
"Could this be exactly where Yángqí finds his usefulness?"
The master said,
"It is exactly where Yángqí finds his usefulness."
The monk continued,
"If so, then sitting atop Yùjǐ Peak,
all people bow with folded hands."
The master said,
"Chapter One: Introductory."
The monk continued,
"I wonder where this move lands?"
The master said,
"You tell me—
where does it land?" The monk continued,
"The master is the Dharma King, free in the Dharma."
He asked,
"When one reaches the Western Heavens at dawn and returns to the Eastern Land by dusk, how is it?"
The master said,
"Hang up your straw sandals."
The monk continued,
"Thank you, Venerable, for the instruction."
The master said,
"What have you gained?"
The monk continued,
"Today I have personally met the great Chan master."
The master raised his whisk and said,
"Do you see it before the whisk,
or after the whisk?"
The monk continued,
"Both before and after are gathered at once."
The master said,
"I'll pierce your nostrils,
and swap your eyes."
The monk continued,
"Venerable, why go to such effort?"
The master gave a shout.
Then he brought up
how Venerable Nánquán, newly arrived at the monastery,
was invited by the administrators and leaders into the abbot's quarters.
A monk then asked,
"Master, upon returning to the abbot's room, what will you instruct people with?"
Nánquán said,
"Last night at the third watch, I lost my ox;
at daybreak, I lost my fire."
The master said,
"When Miàoxǐ first resided at Yùwáng,
he never lost his ox,
nor did he lose his fire.
If someone were to ask,
'Master, upon returning to the abbot's room, what will you instruct people with?'
I would just say to them,
'Hungry, eat; thirsty, drink; idle, sit; tired, sleep.'
Now tell me,
is this the same as Nánquán or different?
If you can speak to this,
I'll acknowledge you as a true monk.
If you cannot,
come back to the abbot's room in thirty years,
and I'll tell you."
With that, he descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall.
A monk asked:
Dàméi said "This very mind is Buddha."
Mǎzǔ said "Not mind, not Buddha."
Which one is correct?
The master said:
Both are correct.
Both are incorrect.
The monk continued:
Gold doesn't barter for gold.
Water doesn't wash water.
The master said:
How do you understand this?
The monk continued:
Who knows the eternal fragrance?
How far does the pure wind that fills the earth reach?
The master said:
Again blown by the wind into a different tune.
A question from the scriptures states:
Transcending verbal characteristics, transcending written characteristics, transcending mental conceptualization.
Ultimately equal and unchanging.
Please, Venerable, transcend verbal characteristics.
The master said:
Where are you now establishing yourself?
The monk continued:
With the Venerable's eyebrows intertwined.
Question and answer are complete.
The master said:
Excellent transcendence of verbal characteristics!
The monk continued:
Slanted and level, unable to grasp the theme.
Anxious and troubled, words return to emptiness.
The master said:
On the temple pole's tip, gazing at the lotus heart.
Then he said:
Today is the first day of the twelfth month.
This year's months are nearly exhausted.
Past, present, and future -
In a snap of the fingers, all simultaneously enter.
Then raising the whisk, he said:
Only this does not enter this community.
Why is it so?
Have you not heard:
It can be the master of all phenomena,
Yet does not fade with the four seasons.
Arriving at Tiāntóng, he was invited to ascend the hall.
A monk asked,
"Temporarily borrowing a question as a shadow grass—what about it?"
The Master said,
"I don't have that spare time."
The monk advanced saying,
"Is this not the Reverend's way of answering?"
The Master said, "Yes."
The monk advanced saying,
"If so, then today I've heard what was unheard before."
The Master said,
"What about the matter of hearing?"
The monk advanced saying, "Before the drum was struck,"
"I had already heard the Reverend speak."
The Master said,
"What did I say, eh?"
The monk advanced saying,
"I also know the Reverend,"
"sometimes acts thus,"
"sometimes does not act thus."
The Master said,
"Misplaced annotation."
The question: Zhàozhōu visited a hermit and said,
"Have it? Have it?"
The hermit raised his fist.
Zhàozhōu said,
"The water is shallow, not a place to moor a boat."
What is the meaning of this?
The Master said,
"A fist."
The monk advanced saying,
"He visited another hermit,"
"who also raised his fist."
Why then did Zhàozhōu say,
"There is releasing and there is seizing"?
The Master said,
"It's still just a fist."
The monk advanced saying,
"Since it's just a fist,"
"why test and discern in two places?"
The Master said,
"You just look at both places."
The monk advanced saying,
"I wonder, today as the Reverend meets with the assembly of Tiāntóng,"
"is there still a place for guiding others or not?"
The Master said, "There is."
The monk advanced saying,
"The kindness is too great to repay."
Then he bowed to the Master.
The Master then said,
"Dangle a hook ten thousand miles long,"
"Halt the black-maned steed of a thousand miles,"
"Spread a net across the heavens,"
"Strike the leaping whale."
"This is what the Old Man of Tiāntóng commonly uses."
"Today, Yùwáng, having come especially into the mountains to pay respects,"
"as a guest, submits to the host's judgment and is ordered to ascend this seat."
"Arriving here, what should one say?"
"Is it acceptable to speak of mind or nature?"
"Is it acceptable to speak of mystery, wonder, principle, or phenomena?"
"Since none are acceptable,"
"one cannot simply stop here. Since one cannot stop,"
"and cannot speak of mind, nature, mystery, wonder, principle, or phenomena,"
"is it acceptable to spread worldly truths?"
"If so, that's called setting sail with the current,"
"not the use of a patch-robed monk."
"Even so,"
"I'll briefly borrow the host's authority and light,"
"to join the assembly in meeting the season."
"Tell me,"
"what season is it now?"
"The inchworm's contraction is to seek extension."
"Shatter the蟠桃核,"
"and see the kernel within."
"Having seen the kernel within,"
"this Way transcends ordinary feeling."
"Tell me, how to phrase 'transcending ordinary feeling'?"
"Do you understand?"
"A gaze that pierces the fourfold world,"
"To preside over this Way is his alone."
He further said,
"Earlier, I received from the hall leader, the Old Man, the citation:"
"A monk asked Xiānglín,"
"'What is the matter beneath the patch-robed monk's robe?'"
"Xiānglín said,"
"'A fire on the mountain in the twelfth month.'"
The Master said,
"This is Xiānglín's saying."
"Today, the hall leader cites it; Yùwáng, following along, dares not yet agree."
"Why dare not agree?"
"If choosing the Buddha lacks such an eye,"
"What use even a thousand years?"
Ascending the hall.
Meeting without pointing it out.
Raising a thought, one immediately knows it exists.
The majestic, unmoving honored one.
Walks without lifting a foot from the ground.
Since it is the unmoving honored one,
why does it nevertheless walk?
Shouting once, he says:
Vaguely resembling a melody, just fit to listen to,
yet again blown by the wind into a different tune.
Ascending the hall.
Dānxiá burned the wooden Buddha.
The monastery director's eyebrows and beard fell off.
