Birds fly shedding feathers, fish swim muddying the water.
Shouting once, he said:
What is this?
To recognize the true qílín,
It has only one horn.
Investigate.
Ascending the hall on New Year's Day.
Three hundred sixty days in a year.
This very morning begins anew from the start.
Every person has a master within.
The water buffalo bites the mouse's tail.
Shēnshā is pleased, Nézhā is delighted.
From the Buddha hall, stepping out through the triple gate.
Rushing into the kitchen storehouse from the monks' hall.
I dare ask the assembly:
Is there still the principle of non-movement or not?
Answering himself: There is.
Then what is the principle of non-movement?
The Spring Lord executes the proper command.
Blossoms bloom on the southern branches.
Arriving at Zīfú Temple, I ascended the hall to preach.
I cited Shùn Héshàng of Xiāngchéng's verse on Huánglóng's Three Barriers, which says:
The old monk of Huánglóng
had a saying about the Three Barriers.
This mountain monk succeeds him,
and today I raise it for you.
I raise it for you—
the cat especially knows how to catch mice.
Guǎngjiàn Yīng Chánshī, upon seeing this verse, remarked:
"Good though it is,
I fear learners will take it as having no meaning."
The Master said:
"Truly, these words are correct.
Today, this mountain monk also has a verse:
Huánglóng's saying covers heaven and earth;
from the start, tightly sealed without a breath of air.
Later followers conventionally echo its sound,
all saying the cat knows how to catch bugs."
Arriving at Xuědòu, I was requested to ascend the hall.
The ordinary phrase of no-birth.
The wondrous mystery of no-self.
The essence illuminated in the inexhaustible phrase.
One arrow pierces three barriers.
In his house, there is the fundamental basis.
What then is the fundamental basis of his house?
Do not blame the former abundance of spirited determination.
His house once trod upon the highest barrier.
Again, an example is cited.
A monk asked Chán Master Míngjué,
"What is the source of all Buddhas?"
Míngjué said,
"The cold hues of a thousand peaks."
The monk said,
"I wonder, beyond this, is there still anything?"
Míngjué said,
"Raindrops on cliff blossoms."
The Master said,
"The cold hues of a thousand peaks, raindrops on cliff blossoms—"
Today, fittingly, they accord with the season and the occasion.
As for the source of all Buddhas,
it must not be disturbed.
Why must it not be disturbed?
For Xuědòu's host himself is present.
Arriving at Qǐxiá's request to ascend the hall.
Just now, I received the honor of Hall Master Dharma Uncle Chánshī citing the encounter between Línjì and Lóngguāng.
As a guest listening to the host's judgment, how dare I not follow the strict command?
I shall briefly provide an annotation for everyone.
Lóngguāng sat in his seat.
Though he remained silent,
his voice was like thunder.
Línjì said,
"This old man today has met his defeat."
Hall Master Dharma Uncle Chánshī asked,
"Where exactly was his point of defeat?"
Miàoxǐ responded,
"When the road is long and the night deep, don't hold a torch—"
"Let us all blow it out and walk in the dark."
The Master ascended the hall and cited [a case]:
One day, Yǎngshān was watching the rain with Lǎn'ān.
Ān said,
"A fine rain, Venerable."
Shān said,
"Wherein lies its fineness?"
Ān was silent.
Shān said,
"Yet I can express it."
Ān said,
"Wherein lies its fineness?"
Shān pointed his finger at the rain.
Ān then ceased.
The Master said,
"One only knew to watch the rain;
one only knew to point at the rain.
Upon careful examination,
it greatly resembles nailing a stake and rocking the oar.

Constantly dwelling within it,
Walking in meditation and sitting or lying down.
Striking the meditation seat with a whisk, he says:
All wisdom penetrates without obstruction.
Old Man Śākyamuni has arrived.
It is said that yesterday someone came from Lúshān,
Yet received news from Jiāngxī.
The alms bowl's mouth faces heaven,
The lantern hangs on the dew-washed pillar.
From all directions and eight quarters they come at once,
Truly there is no place for you to avoid.
Since there is no place to avoid,
Then how should we deliberate?
Do you fully understand?
Turning back, they further interact with one another,
If not, abide according to your position.
Bathing the Buddha Dharma Hall Assembly.
Ninety-seven marks of a great being,
Adorn the subtle and wondrous pure Dharma body.
Manifesting birth, emerging from the mother's womb,
For the sake of all beings, performing Buddha's work.
Yet what exactly is this work being performed?
After a long pause, said:
Descending the seat, together with the chief seat and the assembly,
Enter the Tathāgata's ocean of fragrant waters,
Assisting this old master in turning the great Dharma wheel.
The Master ascended the hall and raised the case of a monk asking Zhàozhōu.
"I, a student, have newly entered the monastic community.
I beg the Master for instruction."
Zhàozhōu said,
"Have you eaten your congee yet?"
The monk said,
"I have eaten the congee."
Zhàozhōu said,
"Go wash your bowl."
At these words, the monk attained awakening.
The Master said,
"Many have commented on this extensively,
and numerous annotations have been made.
Yet no one has ever clearly articulated its meaning.
Today, Miàoxǐ will clearly articulate it for you all.
After eating congee, just wash the bowl.
Now tell me,
was there any instruction given or not?
Black beans have always been good for making sauce.
A bhikṣuṇī is certainly a nun."
The Master ascended the hall and cited: One day, Zhàozhōu
was debating principles with Attendant Wényuǎn.
They competed in baseness, not in superiority.
The winner would lose a pastry.
Yuǎn said,
"Please, Venerable, establish your thesis."
Zhōu said,
"I am a donkey."
Yuǎn said,
"I am the donkey's stomach."
Zhōu said,
"I am donkey dung."
Yuǎn said,
"I am a worm in the dung."
Zhōu said,
"What are you doing in there?"
Yuǎn said,
"I am spending the summer in there."
Zhōu said,
"Bring the pastry here."
The Master said,
"Wényuǎn spent the summer in donkey dung.
A flushed face is not as good as straightforward words.
Zhàozhōu, greedy for a small gain,
won a pastry.
Upon reflection,
it's also like someone from Pǔzhōu sending a thief away.
Now, I ask, after all, how is it?
After a long pause, he said:
"The king of geese selects milk,
inherently not of the duck kind."
Ascending the hall.
When rightly speaking of knowledge and insight.
Knowledge and insight are the mind itself.
When the mind is present, there is knowledge and insight.
Knowledge and insight are the present moment.
The present moment is set aside for now.
Ancient Buddhas intertwine with dew-laden pillars.
Zhànbō contends with Xīnluó in forehead butting.
A halo of ten thousand li shines behind the crown.
Yúnmén hides within the Big Dipper.
Mùzhōu carries a plank, Zhàozhōu drinks tea.
How then shall we deliberate?
Thereupon, he gave a shout and said:
If not halted by this shout,
it might nearly disrupt the sixty-year cycle.
Descended the seat.
The Master ascended the hall and cited how Elder Dòngshān, at summer's end, addressed the assembly, saying:
"In early autumn, at summer's end,
brothers, whether you go east or west,
you must go directly to the place where for ten thousand miles there's not a blade of grass."
Those who offered interpretations before and after all failed to match it.
A monk transmitted these words to Shíshuāng.
Shuāng said:
"Why not say,
'Step outside, and there is grass'?"
When Dòngshān heard this, he deeply approved.
He remarked that in Liúyáng, an ancient Buddha had appeared in the world.
The Master said:
"Ten thousand miles without a blade of grass—
just go accordingly.
Step outside, and there is grass—
each has their own proof.
Having proof, why be constrained?
Under the clear breeze and moon, one waits by the stump;
the cool rabbit recedes, spring grass turns green."
Mid-Autumn Festival Dharma Hall Address.
People intentionally gaze at the moon.
The moon unintentionally shines upon people.
When intentional and unintentional merge into one,
Only then does true awareness arise.
Suddenly taking up the staff and striking it once, he says:
This very thing must not lack awareness.
Throwing it down, he says:
If you realize what falls is nothing other than itself,
Then you'll believe freedom unrestrained leaves no dust.
Entering the hall.
Just now it was the Mid-Autumn Festival in the eighth month,
and already it's the fifteenth of the ninth month.
Lifting his staff and striking it once, he said:
"Only this does not change."
Throwing it down, he said:
"The entire assembly hears with their ears and sees with their eyes."
Ascending the hall.
One, two, three, four, five.
Five, four, three, two, one.
Repeating it thousands of times.
Ultimately, it doesn't go beyond today.
Now, tell me, what is today's matter?
After a long pause, he said:
The frosty wind sweeps across the ground.
The Dharma body is bare bones.
The Master ascended the hall and cited:
Pánshān said:
The ultimate path—a thousand sages do not transmit it.
Címíng said:
The ultimate path—a thousand sages do not affirm it.
The Master said:
Neither transmitted nor affirmed—the ocean-mouth is hard to proclaim.
On the summit of Mount Sumeru, an iron ship sets sail.
The Master ascended the hall and cited [a case].
A monk asked Xuěfēng,
"What about the ancient gully's cold spring?"
Xuěfēng said,
"Staring, one cannot see the bottom."
"What about the one who drinks from it?"
Xuěfēng said,
"It does not enter through the mouth."
Zhàozhōu, hearing this cited,
laughed heartily and said,
"It cannot enter through the nostrils either."
The monk then asked [Zhàozhōu],
"What about the ancient gully's cold spring?"
Zhàozhōu said, "Bitter."
"What about the one who drinks from it?"
Zhàozhōu said, "Dies."
Xuěfēng, hearing of this, then said,
"Zhàozhōu is an ancient Buddha."
Thereupon, he made a distant bow and said,
"From now on, I will not answer questions."
The Master [commenting] said,
"Xuěfēng not answering questions"
"has doubtfully confounded many people."
"Zhàozhōu saying 'bitter'"
"is like a flushed face not matching straightforward speech."
"If it were Miàoxǐ, I would not be like this."
"What about the ancient gully's cold spring?"
"Reach the river and grasp the oar."
"Leave the mountain and irrigate the people's fields."
"What about the one who drinks from it?"
"Clears and cools the heart and lungs."
"This saying has two negative implications."
"If anyone can discern them,"
"I will grant that you possess the eye of true study."
Returning to the monastery and ascending the hall again.
Departure is the cause of staying.
Staying is the fruit of departure.
Departure, staying, fruit and cause -
There is nothing that must or must not be.
Shouting once, he said:
What kind of place is this?
Speaking of departure and staying,
Speaking of cause and fruit,
Speaking of what may and may not be.
Even though this is so,
Here there is actually a good point.
Tell me, where is this goodness?
After a long pause, he said:
Once more chanting old verses with continuous rhyme,
Village songs and temple dances begin anew.
A sermon on the Sacred Festival.
The mind is like the realm of emptiness.
It reveals the dharma equal to emptiness.
When emptiness is realized,
there is neither right nor wrong.
Since there is neither right dharma nor wrong dharma,
it is called the unsurpassed fruition of bodhi,
also called true suchness and buddha-nature,
and also called Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
Therefore it is said:
Prajñāpāramitā can give birth to all buddha-dharmas,
can accomplish all bodhisattva liberation dharmas,
can accomplish the king's supreme dharma,
can fulfill all sentient beings' endeavors.
It is like the wish-fulfilling jewel that embodies all virtues,
able to subdue poisonous dragons and evil spirits,
able to grant people's wishes as desired.
So what is this matter of fulfilling wishes?
Descending the seat, together with the assembly we proceed to the Great Buddha Hall,
to inaugurate the Celestial Bestowal
Sacred Festival. Respectfully announced.
The Master ascended the hall and cited [the case]:
Fǎyǎn asked Xiū Shānzhǔ:
"With the slightest difference, heaven and earth are set apart."
How do you understand this?
Xiū said:
"With the slightest difference, heaven and earth are set apart."
Fǎyǎn said:
How can understanding it this way be acceptable?
Xiū said:
I simply understand it this way.
I wonder how the Venerable understands it?
Fǎyǎn said:
"With the slightest difference, heaven and earth are set apart."
Xiū bowed in reverence.
The Master said:
Fǎyǎn and Xiū Shānzhǔ -
thread coming and thread going,
continuous and closely woven,
they upheld the Dìzàng school's style.
One could say their eyes were filled with light.
But if this were in the lineage of Déshān or Línjì,
they would have to buy straw sandals
and go on pilgrimage.
Why is this so?
With the slightest difference, heaven and earth are set apart.
Where did they get this message from?
Ascending the hall.
Today is again the fifth day of the fifth month.
Big ghosts clap hands, little ghosts dance.
Suddenly bumping into the peachwood charm spirit.
Both hands beat the chest, crying out in bitter grievance.
The mugwort figure says:
Cease your bitter cries.
Then, taking up the staff and striking it once, he says:
There is only one place fit for mutual reflection.
Mutual reflection or not reflecting mutually.
Reflecting and further interrelating.
Casting it down, he says:
If not, abide in your respective positions.
Investigate.
Ascending the hall.
This morning is again the middle of the sixth month.
I recall an old gōng'àn.
Lifting the staff and striking it once, he says:
The staff swallows the Dharmakāya.
The pillar by the side steals a glance.
Whether looking or not, he lifts up
the Qín dynasty's whip and awl.
Although it is thus,
this old gōng'àn
Miàoxǐ will judge anew for him.
Casting it down, he says:
Ten thousand differences and a thousand distinctions—
my path is unified and permeated.
Ascending the hall to mark the end of the summer retreat.
One hundred and twenty days confined within doors.
Thirty-five days wandering outside.
The iron and the tea kettle are not the same.
A clay ox unleashes the lion's roar.
Today the Dharma year has reached its completion.
Grasping the nose, yet losing the mouth.
Taking the great perfect enlightenment as the monastery.
Seven times seven remains forty-nine as before.
Ascending the hall.
When autumn rivers run clear and shallow.
White dew blends with misty isles.
How splendid is Guānshìyīn,
Whose whole body enters the wild grass.
In the wild grass, no need to search.
Why is it so?
Failing to recognize the elder brother's wife,
Only to find it was the sister-in-law all along.
Ascending the hall.
Outside the gate, spring is half gone.
The mountain retreat knows nothing of it.
Pitiful is the staff,
secretly sprouting branches in the dark.
Then, lifting the staff, he said:
This is the staff.
Which one is the sprouting branch?
Casting it down, he said:
It comes straight down—do not blink.
The Master ascended the hall and cited:
Qiánfēng instructed the assembly, saying:
"Raise one, and it cannot be grasped.
Raise two, and it is overlooked.
The first move falls into the second."
Yúnmén stepped forth from the assembly and said:
"Yesterday, someone came from Tiāntāi,
but went on to Jìngshān."
Qiánfēng then called the temple superintendent and said, "Tomorrow, there will be no communal labor."
The Master said:
"Qiánfēng washed his face and touched his nose.
Yúnmén ate his meal and bit on sand.
When the two suddenly encountered each other,
they turned out to be old adversaries.
Even so,
only the old barbarian may know it,
but the old barbarian may not understand it."
Ascending the hall.
What falls is not another thing.
Crisscrossing, it is not dust.
Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—
all reveal the Dharma King's body.
Suddenly picking up the staff and striking it once, he said:
This is the staff.
That is the Dharma King's body.
Lifting it again, he said:
This is the Dharma King's body, and that is the staff.
Then throwing it down, he said:
Since it has already fallen,
and is not another thing, what is it?
It is already adding a head on top of a head.
Shouting once, he said:
What is it even more?
Ascending the hall.
This morning is the first day of the tenth month.
For you, I shall calculate once more.
Two times five hundred coins,
originally make one string.
Those with discerning eyes at the crown of the head,
remember this kōan.
The present emperor, while still residing in his princely mansion,
dispatched a chamberlain into the mountains to make offerings to the Arhats.
After prayers for the sage emperor, he was requested to ascend the seat.
A monk asked:
"The Maitreya Buddha who is to descend in the future,
Manifests heaven and earth upon a single tip of hair.
The present Amitāyus Buddha, the World-Honored One,
Shines his great light universally over lands as numerous as the Ganges' sands.
The five hundred Arhats of Tiāntāi,
Respond everywhere according to conditions and stimuli without omission.
The old masters atop Shuāngjìng Peak—
Transcending all expedient means, how would you speak?"
The Master said:
"The Buddha of the present and the future
All share the same name."
The monk advanced, saying:
"If so, then throughout the human and celestial realms, none do not take refuge."
The Master said:
"A lion within the lion's den;
Sandalwood amidst the sandalwood grove."
The monk advanced, saying:
"It can indeed be said:
'The Dharma abides in its Dharma position,
The characteristics of the world are eternally abiding.'"
The Master said:
"Upon the summit of the temple pole, the lotus heart gazes upward."
The monk advanced, saying:
"Precisely at such a moment,
I wonder, whose 'wind and moon' (elegant realm) is this?"
The Master said:
"The Dharma abides in its Dharma position,
The characteristics of the world are eternally abiding."
The monk advanced, saying:
"[And] within the Elder's share, how then [is it]?"
The Master said:
"The celestial beings and all classes of living beings,
All receive this power of grace."
The monk advanced, saying:
"If it is thus, then:
With one body reliant, heaven and earth are vast;
Myriad affairs without care, the sun and moon are high."
The Master said:
"When the dragon obtains water, its spirit is heightened;
When the tiger meets the mountain's hue, its fierceness grows."
The monk advanced, saying:
"Having reached this point,
I can only have the troops follow the seal's turn and the generals proceed according to the tally."
The Master said:
"An astute monk turns with a single flick."
The monk advanced, saying:
"Only upon returning to a great kingdom does one realize nobility;
When water reaches Xiāo and Xiāng, it is equally clear."
The Master said, "Point."
The monk advanced, saying:
"Just as in the teachings it is said:
'Celestial beings attaining the Way take this as verification,
The Three Jewels thereby manifest in the world.
Using this wondrous Dharma to aid all living beings,
Once received, it is unwavering, eternally tranquil.'
What is the wondrous Dharma?"
The Master said:
"Cast from raw iron, forged of solid steel."
The monk advanced, saying:
"Relying solely on this true message,
The jade leaves and golden branches [endure for] myriad springs."
The Master said:
"In heaven, all stars revolve around the North;
On earth, no waters fail to flow eastward."
The monk bowed and said:
"Who would not speak thus?"
The Master then said:
"If you wish to understand the meaning of Buddha-nature,
You should observe the season and conditions.
When the season arrives, the principle naturally becomes manifest.
I venture to ask the assembly:
What is this naturally manifest principle?"
Raising his whisk, he said:
"Do you see?"
Then striking the meditation seat, he said:
"Do you hear?"
Hearing and seeing clearly—what is this?"
If you can grasp it here,
Then the emperor's grace and the Buddha's grace are both fully repaid at once.
But if not,
Jìngshān will go beat the vines.
Again raising his whisk, he said: Look! The Amitāyus Buddha, the World-Honored One, is here at Jìngshān.
Upon the tip of this whisk, he emits a great radiant light,
Illuminating unspeakable, unspeakable, and again unspeakable Buddha-lands as numerous as motes of dust in worlds.
Within all these worlds, he turns the great Dharma-wheel,
Performing immeasurable, boundless, and vast Buddha-deeds.
Among them, whether ordinary or sage,
Whether orthodox or heterodox,
Whether grass or trees,
Sentient or insentient, all that encounter this light
Attain the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
Therefore, all Buddhas hereby attain it,
Possessing the wisdom of all modes.
All great bodhisattvas hereby attain it,
Accomplishing the various pāramitās.
Pratyekabuddhas and solitary realizers hereby attain it,
Emerging in ages without Buddhas, displaying spiritual powers and light.
The various śrāvaka assemblies, including those who came last night to welcome and request,
The five hundred Arhats hereby attain it,
Gaining the eight liberations and possessing the six spiritual powers.
Celestial beings hereby attain it,
Increasing their ten good deeds.
Asuras hereby attain it,
Those in hell hereby attain it,
Suddenly transcending the ten stages.
Hungry ghosts, animals, and the four kinds of birth and nine categories,
All sentient beings hereby attain it,
Each, according to their capacity, obtains their share.
The Amitāyus Buddha, the World-Honored One, having emitted his great light and performed all Buddha-deeds,
Then with the waters of the four great oceans, poured them over the head of the World-Honored One Maitreya,
And bestowed upon him the prediction of anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi,
That he shall, in the next position, perform great Buddha-deeds.
The Amitāyus Buddha, the World-Honored One, possesses such spiritual powers,
Possesses such mastery,
Possesses such awesome might.
Having reached this point, is there still
One who knows gratitude and repays kindness?"
If there is, come forth and meet with Jìngshān, and I will affirm it for you.
If not, then listen to a verse:
The mouth of the sage throughout the ten-directional Dharma-realm,
And all within the Dharma-realm is his tongue.
Relying solely on this mouth and tongue,
We pray for our sovereign's longevity without cease.
For millions of years, pouring from the source of blessings,
Like the ocean's surge, never exhausting.
From the lion's den is born the suānní lion;
The yuèzhuó phoenix surely emerges from Dānshān's cave.
As auspicious omens, they fill the nine regions,
Grasses, trees, insects—all rejoice.
I bow to this inconceivable matter,
Likened to the multitude of stars surrounding the bright moon.
Therefore, now I proclaim this wondrous gāthā,
A true speaking within the supreme meaning.
Yù Yùgàn requests the master's presence in the hall.
Twenty years have passed since we parted.
Suddenly we meet again.
Like refined gold tempered a hundred times,
Its color remains unchanged from start to finish.
He asks me to turn the Dharma wheel,
To increase the Bodhi aspiration.
Cut off all doubt directly,
And immediately realize your original face.
Ascending the hall, he raised a case.
Venerable Yuāntōng Xiù addressed the assembly, saying:
"At Shàolín, for nine years he sat coldly,
Yet was just seen through by Shénguāng.
Now jade and stone are hard to distinguish,
So one must wrap them in hemp and paper.
This one, that one, and yet another one—
If you are a clear-eyed person,
Why must it be explained again?"
The Master said:
"Jìngshān today cannot avoid adding a dog's tail to sable,
Yet there is also something to it.
The old barbarian's nine years of words fell flat;
It's a pity they were let pass at the time.
This has led those of silent illumination
To sit year after year in a ghost cave.
This one, that one, and yet another one—
Although earnestly admonished with bitter words,
It seems like wind passing through the treetops."
Ascending the hall for the Summer Retreat.
Once a year, it is released.
Once a year, it is bound.
It is simply this matter.
Why need more words?
Without more words, one treads upon it—
A steelyard weight, hard as iron.
In the first year of the Lóngxīng era.
On the tenth day of the eighth month.
The Chán master Dàhuì Zōnggǎo
passed away in the Bright Moon Hall of Jìngshān.
The emperor, upon hearing this, sighed in regret.
He decreed that the Bright Moon Hall be renamed the Marvelous Joy Hermitage,
bestowed the posthumous title Pǔjué,
and named the pagoda Bǎoguāng,
to honor him with grandeur.
His disciples, preserving the master’s whole body,
buried it behind the hermitage.
They sent Liǎoxián to request an epitaph.
Previously, when the emperor was Prince of Pǔ'ān, he had heard of the master’s fame.
He once dispatched the palace eunuch supervisor
to visit the master at Jìngshān.
The master composed a verse to present to him,
which the emperor greatly praised.
Later, while residing in his princely establishment,
he again sent a palace reception officer
to invite the master to the mountains,
to preach the Dharma to the assembly.
He personally inscribed the characters for "Marvelous Joy Hermitage"
and composed a eulogy to send to the master.
Two years later, the emperor ascended the throne,
and first bestowed the title Chán Master Dàhuì.
The following year, he retrieved the previously bestowed imperial writings,
marked them with the imperial seal, deepening the favor, but the master had already passed away.
Reverently, the sovereign is divine, sage, heroic, and martial,
endowed with unparalleled talent,
yet he showed such grace to a man beyond worldly affairs.
For the master, among Buddhists,
was what is called outstandingly eminent in his time,
his loyalty and sincerity moved heaven’s principles.
Thus, he stirred the imperial heart,
receiving exceptional regard and understanding.
Alas, how magnificent!
Since ancient times, sages and worthies
took the transmission of the mind as their learning,
integrating sincerity and enlightenment,
from which transformation arises.
The teaching of the West
points to the emptiness of mind as ultimate liberation,
attaining oneness but not manifesting in function.
Yet the essential point of awakening
may approach what is done by those who exhaust their nature.
In later ages, the three schools flourished together,
with the Línjì lineage as the true transmission,
renowned for obtaining worthy individuals.
Transcending sound and dust,
not establishing a single dharma,
directly cutting to the root,
taking realization as the ultimate.
Radiant and shaking,
rolling and unfolding without hindrance,
like a lion’s cub,
playing freely at ease,
gaining great fearlessness.
This truly cannot be grasped by intellect or knowledge.
The Línjì lineage passed through six generations to Yángqí,
and after two generations at Yángqí,
the Chán master Yuánwù Kèqín
obtained the Dharma from Wǔzǔ Yǎn.
Honored by two reigns,
his Way flourished greatly.
The master succeeded Yuánwù,
further illuminating it.
The master’s name was Zōnggǎo,
from Níngguó County in Xuān Prefecture,
of the Xī family.
At seventeen, he became a monk,
not wishing to remain in his hometown.
Following sūtra and treatise masters,
he journeyed throughout the land.
First, he associated with elders of the Cáodòng school,
but after grasping their teachings,
he sighed and said,
"Is this truly the intent of the Buddhas and patriarchs?"
He left to visit Zhǔn Zhàntáng,
who recognized something in his expression,
and after a while told him,
"Your discourse is fluent and clear,
but it cannot yet withstand life and death.
Now that my illness is critical,
in the future, meet Chuān Qín,
who will be able to resolve your matter."
Qín was Master Yuánwù.
After Zhàntáng’s death,
the master visited Chancellor Zhāng Wújìn,
seeking an epitaph for Zhǔn.
Wújìn’s standards were high under heaven,
and he seldom approved of scholars,
but with one word, the master connected with him.
He was invited to stay,
conversing morning and night,
and Wújìn named his hermitage "Marvelous Joy,"
styled him Tánhuì,
and said, "You must see Master Yuánwù;
I will assist your journey."
Thus, he provided travel expenses to the capital,
where he met Qín at Tiāníng Monastery.
One day, as Qín ascended the hall,
the master had a sudden spiritual awakening.
He reported it to Qín,
who said,
"Not yet.
Although you have gained something,
the great Dharma is not yet clear."
Another day, Qín cited Abbot Yǎn’s phrase "having a phrase, having no phrase,"
and the master attained the great peace and joy Dharma.
Qín clapped his hands and said,
"Now you know I did not deceive you!"
From then on, he roamed freely and vigorously,
with no doubts in mind,
expounding his teachings extensively,
like the powerful debates of Sū Qín and Zhāng Yí,
or the strategies of Sūn Zǐ and Wú Qǐ,
like pouring water from a high roof or rolling a round stone down a thousand-ren slope.
The elders straightened their robes in respect,
unable to withstand his sharpness.
At that time, worthy scholars and officials
often vied to associate with him.
He was highly regarded by Vice Director of the Right Lǚ Shùntú, who petitioned
for him to be granted the purple robe and the title Master Fórì.
During the upheaval with the Nǚzhēn,
their chieftain sought ten Chán monks,
and the master was among them,
but he was later spared.
As if aided by some force, he crossed the river south.
Yuánwù was then presiding at Yúnjū,
appointing the master as first seat,
teaching the Way to the assembly,
his reputation flourishing.
Later, he left to dwell in Yúnjū Mountain,
residing at ancient Yún mén,
where learners gathered like clouds.
He then fled the turmoil to Húnán,
turned to Jiāngyòu, and entered Mǐn,
building a hermitage at Chánglè Yángyǔ.
At that time, only fifty-three followers were with him,
yet within less than fifty days,
thirteen attained the Dharma,
something unprecedented before.
Later, they all stood out prominently.
He first accepted the invitation of Supervising Secretary Jiāng Shǎomíng
to reside at the Xiǎoxī Yúnmén Hermitage.
When I, Jùn, was in Shǔ,
Qín personally entrusted the master to me, saying he truly grasped the Dharma’s essence.
When I, Jùn, came to court,
I invited him to Lín'ān Jìngshān.
The flourishing of the Way and Dharma topped the era.
People traveled great distances, with calloused feet, to attend,
fearing only to be late in bowing at his gate,
and fearing they might not see him.
The place became overcrowded,
so a large hall for a thousand monks was built to house them,
totaling over two thousand people.
His associates were all outstanding talents.
Among the famous officials of the time,
like Vice Director Zhāng Zǐsháo,
he was a close friend.
Yet, the master ultimately encountered misfortune because of this,
as those in power
feared he might criticize them and thus disliked him.
His robes were destroyed, his certificate burned,
and he was banished to Héng Prefecture,

Sānshèng said,
"When I meet someone, I bring it forth.
When I bring it forth, it is not for others."
Xìnghuà said,
"When I meet someone, I do not bring it forth.
When I bring it forth, it is precisely for others."
Venerable Zhēnjìng said,
"These two old sharp ones
Stole some of Línjì's living techniques.
Each established their own territory.
Their energy fills the universe.
Making clear-eyed people only laugh."
The master said:
Old Zhēnjìng greatly resembles one deceiving the dead.
This mountain monk is not like that.
Opening wide the path of the three essentials and three mysteries.
Sitting atop Mount Sumeru's highest peak.
Now tell me,
Does this belong to Sānshèng's share?
Or to Xìnghuà's share?
Let those with clear eyes discern.
The monk holding the whisk asked:
"Before the ancient mirror is polished, what is it like?"
The Master said:
"Fire does not wait for the sun to be hot."
The monk continued:
"After polishing, what is it like?"
The Master said:
"Wind does not wait for the moon to be cool."
The monk continued:
"What about neither polished nor unpolished?"
The Master said: Intertwined.
Question: "Who is the one not companion to all dharmas?"
"When you drink the entire West River in one gulp, I'll tell you."
What is the meaning?
The Master said:
"Nailed and glued."
Then he said:
The essential wonders of all patriarchs
are not sought through competitive debate.
They stir and resonate to crush heterodox views.
Thus Déshān would strike upon entry -
sparks from stone piercing the blue sky.
Línjì would shout upon entry -
dry thunder shaking the universe.
Not the dharma before your eyes,
nor the ultimate mechanism.
Thus or not thus,
if you can leap out,
you're still in the tangle of vines.
How then to evaluate?
How then to understand?
Don't speak of great function, great use, great liberation,
utterly naked, completely bare, nothing to grasp - then rest.
Have you attained this or not?
Don't you see what Elder Fēngxué said:
"Even if understood before words,
one remains stuck in the shell, confused by seals.
Even if mastered within phrases,
one inevitably encounters wild views everywhere.
If you're a true patch-robed monk,
understand immediately,
then you can sit atop sound and form,
lie down atop sound and form.
Mañjuśrī remains Mañjuśrī,
liberation remains liberation.
Why stick to my bowl?"
After a pause, he said:
"To startle the flock requires a heroic spirit;
to match the sage takes a lion's cub.
If choosing Buddhas lacks such eyes,
what use even a thousand years?"
He struck the meditation seat once with his whisk.
Then he brought up another case:
When Bǎizhàng visited Mǎzǔ for the second time and stood attending,
Mǎzǔ raised his whisk.
Bǎizhàng said:
"Use this way or apart from this?"
Mǎzǔ hung the whisk back in its original place.
After a pause, he said:
"When you later open your two lips,
how will you guide people?"
Bǎizhàng took the whisk and raised it.
Mǎzǔ said:
"Use this way or apart from this?"
Bǎizhàng also hung the whisk back in its original place.
Mǎzǔ then shouted.
Later, Huángbò came to Bǎizhàng.
One day he took leave, wishing to pay respects to Mǎzǔ.
Bǎizhàng said:
"Mǎzǔ has already passed away."
Huángbò said:
"I wonder what words Mǎzǔ spoke?"
Bǎizhàng then recounted the second visit incident, saying:
"At that time, Mǎzǔ's single shout
made my ears deaf for three days."
Hearing this, Huángbò unconsciously stuck out his tongue.
Bǎizhàng said:
"Will you not succeed Mǎzǔ?"
Huángbò said: "No.
Today through your account,
I've seen Mǎzǔ's great functioning.
But I never knew Mǎzǔ.
If I succeeded Mǎzǔ,
I'd lose my descendants later."
The Master said:
"Bǎizhàng, struck by the shout,
had deaf ears for three days.
Huángbò, hearing the account, unconsciously stuck out his tongue.
Bǎizhàng doubted he would succeed Mǎzǔ.
Later, when Línjì asked three times about the essence of Buddhism,
he was struck sixty blows three times,
and only then did Línjì realize, as if touched by wormwood,
venturing the three days of deafness.
I ask you all:
Since the teacher's transmission has evidence,
why are the applications different?
Do you understand?
If Cáoxī's waves were all alike,
countless ordinary people would drown."
Patrons viewing the sutras, please take up the whisk.
The Buddha's true Dharma body is like empty space.
Manifesting forms in response to beings, like the moon in water.
Raising his staff, he said:
Old Shakyamuni has arrived!
Upon the tip of Guǒ's staff,
he manifests his wondrous form body.
Universally declaring to the great assembly:
Within the Vairocana treasury there is a great sutra scroll,
measuring equal to the three thousand great thousand worlds.
Recording all affairs within the three thousand great thousand worlds,
completely and without omission.
With my pure divine eye,
I see that great sutra scroll contained within a single dust mote.
Tonight before this assembly of humans and devas,
I shall employ great skillful means,
to break open that single dust mote,
and bring forth this sutra scroll,
to benefit sentient beings!
Striking once, he called to the assembly:
The dust mote has been broken,
the great sutra scroll has emerged.
There is sudden and gradual,
expedient and ultimate,
partial and complete,
middle and extreme,
principle and phenomenon,
cause and effect.
Hundreds of thousands of Dharma gates, immeasurable profound meanings,
all dharmas of worldly and transcendental realms,
are entirely contained herein.
Do you all believe this or not?
If you believe it,
you transcend the three realms and cross the sea of suffering,
throughout the endless future, you will fully enjoy its benefits.
If you don't believe it,
Old Shakyamuni will return into the staff.
Then raising it, he said:
If you call it Old Shakyamuni,
it's still the staff.
If you call it the staff,
it's still Old Shakyamuni.
Old Shakyamuni penetrates through the staff,
the staff penetrates through Old Shakyamuni.
At just such a moment,
is it sudden or gradual?
Is it expedient or ultimate?
Is it partial or complete?
Is it middle or extreme?
Is it principle or phenomenon?
Is it cause or effect?
Is it Old Shakyamuni?
Is it the staff?
Shouting once, he said:
Sudden cannot be obtained,
gradual cannot be obtained,
expedient cannot be obtained,
ultimate cannot be obtained,
partial cannot be obtained,
complete cannot be obtained,
middle cannot be obtained,
extreme cannot be obtained,
principle cannot be obtained,
phenomenon cannot be obtained,
cause cannot be obtained,
effect cannot be obtained,
Old Shakyamuni cannot be obtained,
the staff cannot be obtained,
even a dust mote cannot be obtained,
the great sutra scroll cannot be obtained,
the present speaker of Dharma cannot be obtained,
the listeners of Dharma cannot be obtained,
even this "cannot be obtained",
also cannot be obtained.
Then drawing a line with his staff, he said:
Cutting off all entanglements!
Again raising it, he said:
At just such a moment,
what is each person's own nostrils?
After a long pause, he said:
Where have the thousand sages gone?
The sky-leaning long sword chills people to the bone.
Again striking once.
Again bringing up:
Once there was an old woman
who offered wealth requesting Zhàozhōu to expound the great treasury of sutras.
Zhàozhōu descended his meditation seat and circumambulated once, saying:
"The exposition is complete."
Someone reported this to the old woman.
The woman said:
"I requested the exposition of one treasury,
why did the venerable only expound half a treasury?"
The master said:
Some in the assembly discuss:
What is that half treasury?
Some say:
Circumambulate once more,
or snap the fingers once,
or cough once,
or shout once,
or clap once.
Such understanding
is merely shameless.
As for that half treasury,
don't say Zhàozhōu circumambulated once more—
even if he circumambulated hundreds of millions of times,
for the old woman it would still be only half a treasury.
Even if he circumambulated Mount Sumeru hundreds of millions of times,
for the old woman it would still be only half a treasury.
Even if all the venerable monks under heaven similarly circumambulated hundreds of millions of times,
for the old woman it would still be only half a treasury.
Even if mountains, rivers, and the great earth—all myriad phenomena,
every plant and tree,
each possessing the broad long tongue mark,
with different mouths but the same sound,
from today until the end of the future,
for the old woman it would still be only half a treasury.
Do you all wish to know the old woman?
After a long pause, he said:
The embroidered mandarin ducks are shown for you to see,
but the golden needle is not given away.
For Elder Gāo'ān Wù's portrait hanging.
Holding the portrait scroll, he showed the assembly and said:
On Lotus Flower Peak's summit, the true reality is spoken;
Returning from Three Pagodas, the mechanism is revealed anew.
Both paths are completely stripped away;
Every dust-mote shines with boundless radiance.
This radiance is what people know exists.
Now tell me:
Where is Elder Gāo'ān's original face?
Do you thoroughly understand?
Before living beings and buddhas existed, before the world took form—
Truly, eyebrows and eyes are clear,
Fully manifest and exposed.
If someone recognizes it here,
They may walk hand in hand with this elder,
Without grasping at name and form on the scroll.
But if not,
Yúnmén cannot avoid following convention and turning things upside down.
Then he unfurled it and said:
Do you see?
If this is it, then there are two; if this isn't it, you've missed it face-to-face.
Not missing it, there are not two;
In the ancestral hall, no positions are arranged.
In the Foolish Idleness Studio, just sit at ease.

The master asked a monk.
