If not spoken here,
where else should it be spoken?
Therefore, this matter is definitely not in words and language.
If it were in words and language,
the entire Tripitaka, the various schools and hundred philosophers, filling heaven and earth,
are they without words?
Then why did Bodhidharma need to come from the West to directly point?
After all, where is the place of direct pointing?
The moment you conceive a thought, it is already crooked.
Like the monk who asked Zhàozhōu,
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West?"
Zhōu said,
"The cypress tree in the courtyard."
This is exceedingly direct.
Also, a monk asked Dòngshān,
"What is the Buddha?"
Shān said,
"Three pounds of flax."
Also, a monk asked Yúnmén,
"What is the Buddha?"
Mén said,
"A dry piece of shit."
This is exceedingly direct.
If you try to approach it with your mind,
it becomes crooked instead.
The Dharma is originally without crookedness;
it is only because learners study with a crooked mind.
Even if they learn what is mysterious within mystery, wonderful within wonder,
in the end, they cannot overcome birth and death.
They only become those who learn phrases.
Originally, they are people without affairs,
but instead, they are afflicted by these poisonous evils in their mind-consciousness,
creating obstructions and hindrances, unable to be at ease.
Therefore, the teachings say:
The Dharma cannot be seen, heard, sensed, or known.
If you practice seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing,
that is seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing,
not seeking the Dharma.
It is like someone asking for the road into the city, from where to go?
Pointing, it is said,
"Go from here."
Hearing this, they set off—
it is already crooked.
How can this be learned with a mind that uses knowledge, views, understanding, deliberation, gain and loss, profundity, wonder, right and wrong?
If you want to truly engage in investigation,
then lay everything down,
like a great dead person.
Know nothing, understand nothing.
Suddenly, in the place of not knowing and not understanding,
if this one thought is broken through,
even the Buddha can do nothing to you.
Have you not seen the ancients say:
"Letting go at the cliff's edge, one willingly undertakes it oneself;
After death and revival, one cannot deceive the ruler."
Since you all have come to Xuěfēng to investigate Chán,
you must not take it lightly.
This is a clear-eyed master,
whom you can rely upon,
worthy of being a model of the Dharma.
Perhaps some, seeing Zhēnxiē urging people to generate the Bodhi mind,
slanderously say:
"Since he is called a Chán master,
he should have the fundamental matter of the school.
Why bother with all this fuss,
like a lecture-master?"
I ask you:
What is that fundamental matter?
Alas!
Since you yourself cannot do good,
you instead laugh at others who do good. Such people, with their birth-and-death, jealousy not eliminated,
consider themselves right.
If the Good Knowing Advisor does not urge people to generate the Bodhi mind,
should he teach people to kill and set fires instead?
This curved wooden seat
is not a place for you to seek fame, seek profit, be jealous, or engage in birth-and-death.
Viewed with the Dharma-eye,
it is like a boiling cauldron, a fiery furnace, a forest of swords, a mountain of blades.
Once the Dharma drum is struck,
all heavenly dragons and spirits assemble.
If your Dharma-eye is not clear,
the heavenly dragons and spirits see you spewing black smoke from your mouth;
how could they not be terrified?
Have you not seen it said in the teachings:
Those who have not attained but claim to have attained,
this is arrogance,
slandering the great Prajñā.
It cannot be repented.
It is like a poor man falsely calling himself an emperor, bringing about his own execution.
How much more so for the Dharma King?
How can one falsely steal it?
If the cause is not true,
the result will be twisted.
One must be genuine to attain it.
Those called Good Knowing Advisors
guide all living beings,
enabling them to see the Buddha-nature.
They must observe the roots and set up teachings, match the sickness and administer the medicine.
One cannot speak to people from a three-family village,
saying, "The staff goes to the Western Heaven in the morning and returns to the Eastern Land in the evening;
the fan leaps up to the Heaven of the Thirty-Three,
tapping Indra's nose; the eastern sea carp gets one strike, and rain pours down like basins."
Although these are fundamental statements,
how can they comprehend them?
This old fellow, even you Chán practitioners still cannot find his cracks,
let alone ordinary people, dwelling in the dust-net, with active ignorance.
If there is no skillful means to guide them, to make them ripe,
how can they immediately understand?
This assembly consists entirely of those who have left their homes from ten or twenty stages away,
one person joining the community, generating the mind, turning the multitude towards goodness.
How could there be no benefit?
This is the fundamental duty that a Good Knowing Advisor ought to perform.
How could it be forced?
This summer, Yúnmén was at Guǎngyīn,
opening a shop selling lamp wicks and soap pods.
According to the family's means, rich or poor,
he spoke some coarse Chán.
In the room, he questioned the learners with one phrase.
If, without thinking or deliberating,
they could naturally and innocently utter a phrase,
he would press them further.
If they hesitated and could not respond,
he would strike them on the back with a stick.
There were no subtleties.
If suddenly one or half a person were awakened,
he would then send them up to Xuěfēng,
to the great furnace and bellows,
as matters belong to the same family.

Earlier, Zhēnxiē cited the World-Honored One entering Śrāvastī, the great city, to beg for food. After eating, putting away the robe and bowl, washing his feet, he sat down on the seat. Subhūti came forth, paid homage, and said, "How rare, World-Honored One!"
Zhēnxiē said,
"Old Śākyamuni was pitiable enough; when Subhūti came out and said 'How rare,'
immediately, it was like ice melting and tiles crumbling."
Good assembly!
Old Śākyamuni had not spoken a single word;
what did Subhūti see that he said "How rare"?
Do you all want to understand?
Just look at the place where Zhēnxiē said "ice melting and tiles crumbling."
If suddenly you can see through it,
your lifelong task of study and practice is completed.
Just like Zhēnxiē,
ordinarily when he sees learners,
they often recognize the present mirror-awareness,
seek knowledge and views, look for understanding,
without any time of rest.
Having no alternative, he teaches people to undertake it beyond the kalpa.
Speaking based on reality,
this one phrase is already too much.
This is a temporary expedient,
like pointing at the moon to show someone.
One should look at the moon,
not recognize the finger.
People nowadays cannot comprehend this;
they think there really is such a matter.
As the Patriarch said, "Mistakenly recognizing, how could they understand expedient means?"
Since they do not recognize expedient speech,
they then sit inside the belly of Dipaṃkara Buddha,

in the ghost cave under the black mountain, sitting motionless until their buttocks grow calluses, their mouths drooling, their bellies still pitch-black—will they ever see it, even in a donkey's year?
Yúnmén tonight, before the assembly of humans and gods, joins the speech of the sages.
Each of you, remember this.
Many words lead the Way further away.
Earlier, Zhēnxiē had a case left unfinished;
Yúnmén will conclude it for him.
Once, an old monk visited Línjì.
As soon as they met, he lifted his sitting mat and said,
"Is it bowing?
Or is it not bowing?"
Línjì shouted.
The old monk then bowed.
Jì said,
"This thief!"
The old monk said,
"Thief, thief!" and left.
Jì said,
"Don't say nothing is good."
The head seat was standing in attendance.
Jì said,
"Is there any fault or not?"
The seat said, "There is."
Jì said,
"Does the guest have fault?
Or does the host have fault?"
The seat said,
"Both have fault."
Jì said,
"Where is the fault?"
The seat then left.
Jì said,
"Don't say nothing is good."
The master said:
Línjì lost one move in the dark,
but won one play in the light.
Although there is losing and winning, light and dark,
how unbecoming it is for the bystander!
Now, I ask you,
who is the bystander?
After a long pause, he said:
If you go to other places,
do not cite this incorrectly.
Master Dìngguāng requested a general discourse.
A monk asked:
"If a single dharma exists,
Vairocana falls into the state of an ordinary person.
If all dharmas are nonexistent,
Samantabhadra loses his realm.
Apart from these two paths,
please, Master, quickly speak."
The Master said:
"A shell-less turtle flies up to heaven."
The monk continued:
"I've intimately received the Master's instruction;
One phrase selflessly benefits sentient beings."
The Master said:
"What is this intimate place?"
The monk continued:
"Last night, a clear breeze arose in the eight directions;
This morning, flowing waters swell the front stream."
The Master said:
"You almost didn't ask properly."
Then he said:
"All Buddhas originally never emerged in the world,
Nor did they enter parinirvana.
Through their inherently free great vow power,
They manifest boundless rare dharmas.
These dharmas cannot be ultimately grasped through thought,
They are not where the mind operates.
Since they're not where the mind operates,
They are not rare dharmas.
Since they're not rare dharmas,
These dharmas have neither reality nor emptiness.
Since they lack reality and emptiness,
Calling them existent won't do,
Calling them nonexistent won't do,
Calling them both existent and nonexistent won't do,
Calling them neither existent nor nonexistent won't do,
Calling them not nonexistent and not not nonexistent won't do either.
Didn't you see the Chan guest's question earlier:
'If a single dharma exists,
Vairocana falls into the state of an ordinary person.
If all dharmas are nonexistent, Samantabhadra loses his realm.
Apart from these two paths, please, Master, quickly speak.'
Yúnmén answered him:
'A shell-less turtle flies up to heaven.'
Everyone, how would you discern this?
Is it existence or nonexistence?
Is it emptiness or reality?
Try to come out and speak!
If not,
I'll add some more complications.
Thus the ancient sage said:
Sometimes first illuminate then apply,
Sometimes first apply then illuminate,
Sometimes illuminate and apply simultaneously,
Sometimes illuminate and apply at different times.
If you first illuminate then apply,
You blind everyone's eyes.
If you first apply then illuminate,
You open everyone's eyes.
If you illuminate and apply simultaneously,
Then half-blind and half-open.
If you illuminate and apply at different times,
Then fully open or fully blind.
Among these four statements,
One has guest but no host,
One has host but no guest,
One has neither guest nor host,
One fully possesses both guest and host.
Now in this assembly,
If there's someone who won't be deceived, come forth and say:
What kind of place is this?
Speaking of existence and nonexistence,
Speaking of emptiness and reality,
Speaking of illumination and application,
Speaking of guest and host -
Grab me by the chest,
Pull me from the Chan seat,
Beat me to pulp with the mallet -
I wouldn't blame you.
Is there such a person?
If not,
The ladle handle remains in Yúnmén's hands.
Whether releasing or restraining,
Speaking of existence and nonexistence,
Speaking of emptiness and reality,
Speaking of illumination and application,
Speaking of guest and host -
All originates from here.
Tell me, should we release now,
Or restrain?
After a long pause, he said:
"Opening people's eyes, blinding people's eyes,
One hand pushes, one hand pulls.
Not the three essentials or three mysteries,
Nor the fourfold selection.
After all, what is it?"
Raising his whisk, he said:
"Xuěfēng rolls the ball, Mùzhōu carries the plank."
Then he said:
"Everyone always says
They come here to practice Chan.
Let me ask you:
How do you practice Chan?
Since impermanence is swift and the matter of birth and death is great,
With your own affair unclear, you seek a master's decision,
Wanting to understand yourself and attain peace of mind -
This isn't child's play.
Yet nowadays everyone says:
'I fear death, so I practice Chan.'
Practicing and practicing,
As days and months accumulate,
They fall into a nest of complications,
Only gaining smooth talk,
Adding more confusion to their own share,
Actually worse off than before joining the assembly when they had fewer troubles.
This is fundamentally a mistake from the start,
Not meeting true people,
Passing down errors repeatedly,
Leading to this state.
Recently, the Dharma is lamentable,
Demons are strong, Dharma is weak.
Chan practitioners
Each have a bellyful of Chan,
Everywhere competing like herb-gathering contests -
When will they ever rest?
I often tell you all:
The Patriarch coming from the West
Only served as a witness,
Nor did he transmit any Chan way to people.
If there were a Chan way to transmit,
Then each should transmit it to their parents,
Transmit it to their six relatives!
Since there's nothing to transmit, one must awaken by oneself.
If you intend to seek awakening,
You're already mistaken.
How much more so with much knowledge and understanding,
Recklessly speaking nonsense?
He was extremely intelligent and sharp,
Yet for years couldn't grasp Chan -
Precisely because of much knowledge and understanding.
After Bǎizhàng passed away, he went to Wéishān.
Wéishān said: 'I hear
When you were with my late teacher Bǎizhàng,
You answered ten when asked one,
Answered a hundred when asked ten.
This is your intelligence and sharpness -
Conceptual understanding and intellectual thinking,
The root of birth and death.
Before your parents gave birth to you,
Try to speak a phrase!'
Xiāngyán, questioned by Wéishān,
Became completely bewildered.
Returning to his quarters,
He checked all the texts he'd previously studied
From beginning to end,
Seeking one phrase to respond with -
But couldn't find any.
Then he sighed to himself:
'A painted cake cannot satisfy hunger.'
Repeatedly going to the hall,
He begged Wéishān to explain it.
Wéishān said:
'If I explain it to you,
Later you'll curse me.
What I say is mine,
Ultimately not your concern.'
Xiāngyán could do nothing,
His mind filled with frustration,
Resenting Wéishān for not explaining.
So he gathered all his collected writings
And burned them, saying:
'Enough, enough!
In this life I won't study Buddha-dharma anymore.
I'll just be a long-term congee-eating monk,
Sparing mental effort.'
From then on, he completely let go -
Not thinking of Chan,
Not thinking of the Way,
Not thinking of good,
Not thinking of evil,
Not thinking of before parents' birth,
Not thinking of the present either.
With all four sides grounded, everything released,
He bid farewell to Wéishān and went directly to Nányáng to see National Teacher Zhōng's traces.
There he rested and built a hut.
One day while clearing weeds,
As he tossed away tiles and stones,
Suddenly hitting a bamboo, it made a sound -
Unknowingly striking the nostril of before parents' birth.
In that moment, like a sick person finding medicine,
Like darkness finding light,
Like poverty finding treasure,
Like a child finding its mother,
His joy was boundless.
Then he bathed, burned incense,
Bowed toward Wéishān from afar, sighing:
'The Venerable's great compassion
Surpasses even parents' kindness.
Had you explained it to me then,
How could this have happened today?'
Then he composed a verse:
'One strike - all knowing gone.'
See how those who attain
Naturally speak differently.
When he first heard the bamboo's sound,
Suddenly great awakening -
The awakened mind completely ceased messages,
Like Maitreya snapping fingers, the pavilion gate opens,
Summoning Sudhana to enter.
Sudhana's mind rejoiced,
Entered, then it closed again.
This is the principle: Xiāngyán's awakening completely ceased messages,
The matter before parents' birth instantly appeared.
Only then composing a verse
Provided skillful means for helping others.
Below he annotated:
'No further cultivation needed.
Movement and expression reveal the ancient path,
Not falling into silent mechanism - everywhere no traces,
Beyond sound and form, dignified demeanor.
All directions' way-attainers
All say supreme capacity.'
Often seeing Chan practitioners
Love to everywhere ask elders -
When elders have no place to put words, they explain for them.
Are you afraid Xiāngyán didn't speak clearly enough,
Needing further annotation?
There are also those who say:
'Through striking something making sound,
I had an awakening.'
If asked, 'Try to explain!'
They strike something making sound, saying:
'How clear!'
What connection does this have?
Much like scratching an itch through boots with a fist -
How can you reach comfort?
Haven't you heard
In ancient times, when Jùzhī lived in his hut,
A nun wearing a bamboo hat
Came directly, circled his seat once, saying:
'If you can speak, I'll remove the hat.'
Jùzhī couldn't speak at that time.
The nun flicked her sleeves and left.
Jùzhī said:
'Why not stay awhile?'
The nun said:
'If you can speak, I'll stay.'
Jùzhī again had no words.
After the nun left,
Jùzhī sighed to himself:
'Though I'm a man,
I'm inferior to a woman.'
He prepared to burn his hut and descend the mountain.
Suddenly that night he dreamed a deity said:
'Venerable, don't descend the mountain.
Wait -
A great being in the flesh will come explain Dharma for you.'
After several days, indeed Tiānlóng arrived.
Jùzhī told him the previous incident.
Tiānlóng said:
'You ask me,
I'll speak for you.'
Jùzhī said:
'If you can speak, remove the hat.'
Tiānlóng simply raised one finger.
Jùzhī suddenly experienced great awakening.
Afterwards, whenever questioned,
He only raised one finger.
He often said:
'I obtained Tiānlóng's one-finger Chan,
A lifetime's use不完.'
Lángyé Jué once composed a verse:
'Jùzhī's one finger lets you know -
Morning-born hawk soars skyward.
Without strength to lift tripods and move mountains,
The black steed won't be easily ridden even for a thousand miles.'
See this verse -
This understands the one-finger Chan clearly.
How can this be learned?
Jùzhī had a serving boy
Who whenever seeing people ask questions,
Also learned to raise a finger in response.
Someone told Jùzhī:
'Venerable, this boy shouldn't be underestimated -
He also understands Buddha-dharma.
Whenever anyone asks him,
He raises his finger like you.'
Hearing this, Jùzhī
One day secretly hid a knife in his sleeve,
Called the boy forward:
'I hear you also understand Buddha-dharma -
Is this true?'
The boy said yes. Jùzhī said:
'What is Buddha?'
The boy immediately raised his finger - Jùzhī grabbed it
And cut it off with the knife.
The boy screamed and ran out.
Jùzhī then called the boy,
The boy turned his head.
Jùzhī said:
'What is Buddha?'
The boy unconsciously raised his hand -
Saw no finger,
Suddenly experienced great awakening.
Wonderful!
Truly knowing Buddha-dharma cannot be transmitted or learned -
Jùzhī's attainment wasn't in the finger,
Xiāngyán's awakening wasn't in striking bamboo. Tell me:
Where was it?
I've explained everything at once - does everyone understand?
This matter is neither difficult nor easy -
A hair's breadth deviation means missing by a thousand miles.
I urge everyone:
Step back and look for yourselves -
Everything is readily available.
Please directly accept it right now,
No need to exert effort.
If you intend to move even a hair's breadth,
You're already a thousand miles away -
No connection at all.
Since you're all here,
You should feel shame,
Not passing time casually.
If not sincere,
What in prajñā will consume the faithful offerings?
Haven't you heard Fényáng Wúyè say:
'Look at ancient virtue practitioners -
After attaining meaning,
Thatched huts and stone rooms,
Cooking meals in broken-legged pots,
Eating for twenty-thirty years,
Not concerned with fame and gain,
Not mindful of wealth and treasures,
Greatly forgetting human affairs,
Hiding traces in rocky cliffs,
Not coming when kings command,
Not attending when lords invite -
How different from us coveting fame, loving profit, drowning in worldly paths,
Like petty merchants with small desires forgetting great fruits!'
Clearly, brothers, already then such words existed.
Had they seen our current actions,
How shameful it would be!
Brothers,
Time is precious,
It waits for no one.
Each should arouse your spirits thoroughly,
Not vainly receiving Buddha's protection,
Not betraying your lifelong aspiration for the Way.
Recently, Dharma Master came from Xuěfēng,
Simply because impermanence is swift and the matter of birth and death is great.
My own affairs are not yet clear, and I wish to beg for your guidance.
Thereupon, I cited Mǎzǔ's "not mind, not Buddha, not a thing."
Instructed him to contemplate it.
Further gave him another round of annotation.
Do not grasp it through reasoning.
Do not grasp it as having nothing to do.
Do not grasp it like striking flint's spark or lightning's flash.
Do not speculate under the intellect.
Do not accept it at the point of raising.
"Not mind, not Buddha, not a thing."
How should it be understood?
He then became doubtful.
And dared not open his mouth again.
Today, however, he comes to burn incense and pay respects, saying:
"Miàodào studies Prajñā,
often encountering demonic obstacles.
I wish to request that tonight, before the assembly of devas and humans,
you expound Prajñā to serve as repentance.
May all sentient beings in the Dharma realm instantly realize the profound Prajñā,
and together repay the Buddha's kindness." Yúnmén said:
"The ancient sages have said,
'Fearful mind is hard to arise,
good mind is hard to stir.'
Without having attained liberation oneself,
yet seeking to liberate others first—
this is the Bodhisattva's resolve.
Since you know to fear sin,
and turn your mind toward the Way,
this is indeed rare." Thus, he granted the request,
to perform repentance for him.
Moreover, the nature of sin is not inside, outside, or in between;
then what is used to repent?
Yet there are no saints who possess sin,
nor ordinary beings without sin.
When ordinary beings commit sins,
they all arise from deluded thoughts of the mind,
entirely without real substance.
Although without real substance,
when receiving retribution, one must still deludedly receive it.
Like a shadow following the form,
it cannot be escaped.
Although deludedly receiving retribution,
it also has no real substance.
Therefore it is said,
if the nature of sin had substance,
then the entire realm of empty space could not contain it.
Why?
Because ordinary beings who commit sins are many.
Now, this venerable has aroused a single thought of mind,
wishing to directly attain the unsurpassed Buddha-fruit Bodhi.
Once this mind is aroused,
the sins committed, like piled dry grass as high as Mount Sumeru,
and the mind aroused, like a mustard seed's worth of fire,
can all be completely burned without any remainder.
Can you believe this?
Once this single thought of mind is aroused,
at that moment, Buddhahood is already accomplished.
Throughout the future, it will never regress or be lost.
What serves as proof?
Have you not seen in the teachings where Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Bodhisattva Dharmaprajñā:
"Son of the Buddha,
when a Bodhisattva first arouses the mind of Bodhi,
how much is the measure of merit obtained?"
The Bodhisattva Dharmaprajñā said:
"This meaning is very profound,
hard to speak, hard to know,
hard to differentiate, hard to believe and understand,
hard to realize, hard to practice,
hard to penetrate, hard to contemplate,
hard to measure, hard to enter.
Nevertheless, I shall rely on the Buddha's majestic power,
and speak for you.
Suppose there is a person,
using all kinds of joyful provisions,
makes offerings to all sentient beings in the eastern asaṃkhyeya worlds,
for a full kalpa,
then teaches them all to uphold the five precepts.
The south, west, north, four intermediate directions, above and below are likewise.
What do you think?
Is this person's merit
not very great?"
Śakra Devānām Indra said:
"Only the Buddha can know this person's merit;
all others are incapable of measuring it."
Dharmaprajñā said:
"This person's merit,
compared to the merit of a Bodhisattva's initial arousal of mind,
does not reach one percent,
not one thousandth,
not one hundred-thousandth.
Thus, one hundred-millionth, one hundred-hundred-millionth, one thousand-hundred-millionth, one hundred-thousand-hundred-millionth,
up to an asaṃkhyeya part,
countless, immeasurable, boundless, unspeakable parts, unspeakable unspeakable parts,
still do not reach one.
Successively guiding sentient beings,
according to their desires, pleasures, limits, and various faculties' differences,
from ten to a hundred,
from a hundred to a thousand,
from a thousand to ten thousand,
from ten thousand to a hundred million,
from a hundred million to unspeakable unspeakable asaṃkhyeya numbers of sentient beings,
all enabling them to uphold the five precepts and ten good deeds,
further to a second person again doubling the number of the previous person,辗转 up to a hundred people,
each person doubling the number of the previous person,
all enabling them to realize the fruits of Srota-āpanna, Sakṛdāgāmin, Anāgāmin, Arhat, and Pratyekabuddha,
the merit obtained compared to the merit of a Bodhisattva's initial arousal of mind,
does not reach one percent,
even up to unspeakable calculations and analogies also cannot compare.
Exhausting all analogies, there is no place for comparison. Why?
Because this single thought of mind is equal to the Buddhas of the three times, without two, without difference.
The Sanskrit 'kṣama',
here means 'repentance of faults',
called severing the continuous mind.
Once repented, never again created.
This mind once aroused never regresses or is lost.
If one can directly be without mind,
the merit of initial arousal of mind,
compared to the merit of no-mind,
does not reach one percent, one thousandth, one hundred-thousandth, one hundred-thousand-ten-thousand-hundred-millionth,
even up to unspeakable unspeakable asaṃkhyeya parts by calculation and analogy,
still do not reach one.
Why?
At the initial arousal of mind,
it is equal to the Buddhas of the three times.
This mind does not even have the Buddhas of the three times;
where then can one grope?
Therefore, the merit of a single thought of no-mind,
again has no place for comparison.
If so, then there is no birth nor death,
no sage nor ordinary being,
no person nor self,
no Buddha nor Dharma.
If one can see thus,
this is true repentance.
This venerable,既然 possessing the aspiration of a great hero,
is determined to practice Chan.
Just practice thus.
You must suddenly awaken,
directly without mind,
then attain peace and bliss.
If not awakened,
merely verbally speaking a few 'not's,
and citing some ancient's sayings about 'nothing',
mistakenly taking evidence, then saying,
'I have attained rest.'
I ask you, have you really rested or not?
This is using mind to be without mind.
If using mind to be without mind,
the mind instead becomes existent.
How can you forcibly make it nothing?
The ancient sages scolded this as heretics falling into empty annihilation,
dead people whose souls haven't dispersed,
slandering the great Prajñā, beyond repentance.
Although with good causes, they incur evil results.
Such views,
like killing hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands of rice plants, hemp, bamboo, or reeds,
what sin is there?
Such ones surely have a belly full of doubts.
If oneself is without doubt,
then one has expedient means
to resolve others' doubts.
If oneself has doubts,
how can one remove others' doubts?
Attempting to remove others' doubts,
only adds another layer of doubt for them.
As said, 'My eye was originally correct;
because of the teacher, it became skewed.'
Everyone, do you wish to know: being without doubt oneself, can one remove others' doubts?
Once the World-Honored One was expounding the Dharma at the Vulture Peak assembly,
there were five hundred bhikṣus
who had attained the four dhyānas and possessed the five supernatural powers,
but had not attained the patience of the non-arising of dharmas.
Using their past-life knowledge supernatural power,
each saw in their past lives
having killed fathers, harmed mothers, and other heavy sins.
Within their own minds, each harbored doubts,
unable to realize the very profound Dharma.
At that time, Mañjuśrī, knowing the assembly's doubts and fears,
relying on the Buddha's power,
then grasped a sharp sword,
held it threateningly toward the Tathāgata.
The World-Honored One then said to Mañjuśrī:
"Stop, stop!
Do not commit such transgression, do not harm me.
I must be harmed;
being harmed for good.
Mañjuśrī,
from the very beginning,
there is no self or person.
But due to the inner mind perceiving self and person,
when the inner mind arises, 'I' must be harmed,
that is called harm."
Thereupon, the five hundred bhikṣus,
awakened to their original mind as like a dream, like an illusion,
in the dream-illusion, there is no self or person,
even up to the parents who gave birth and were born from.
Then the five hundred bhikṣus,
in unison spoke a verse praising Mañjuśrī:
"Mañjuśrī, great wise one,
deeply reached the source of Dharma.
Holding a sharp sword himself,
threatened the Tathāgata's body.
As the sword, so the Buddha likewise,
one mark, not two.
No mark, nothing born,
in this, how can there be killing?"
Assembly,
although Mañjuśrī resolved the assembly's doubts,
he expended no small effort.
Today, Yúnmén resolves this venerable's doubts,
and doesn't even use a sharp sword,
only have this 'not mind, not Buddha, not a thing.'
If here your doubt is shed,
you'll roam freely under heaven.
If not,
listen to this annotation:
One cut severs the path of birth and death; the Mohī's true eye opens at the crown.
Boundless karmic obstacles all vanish.
After all, how?
Hánshān and Shídé are on Tiāntāi.
Striking the meditation seat once with the whisk,
shouted once and descended the seat.
Huáng Déyòng requested a universal discourse.
The Master said:
Huáng Duānfū of Shàowǔ, a noble scholar,
believed in the Buddhist vehicle and knew of this matter.
He donated family wealth to build a hermitage,
naming it after Yuánwù.
Repeatedly he sent letters begging
to transplant a branch of Yángqí's Dharma there,
to greatly benefit sentient beings.
Yúnmén did not dare lightly agree.
He also entrusted Scholar Wú Yuánzhāo
to plead again and again,
yet still did not dare grant it easily.
Unfortunately, Duānfū suddenly passed away.
It is said when arranging his passing,
he called his two sons
and repeatedly instructed them:
"If for my sake you can from Yúnmén
invite a genuine resident for the hermitage,
then I shall die without regret."
Having spoken, he departed forever.
The two sons, not forgetting his final instruction,
sought Scholar Yuánzhāo
to draft a petition and send a special envoy
to invite Chán person Mí Guāng as hermitage head.
Seeing their utmost sincerity,
he finally accepted the mission.
Now Déyòng and his brothers
specially come to this hermitage, spending gold to prepare offerings and requesting this mountain monk's universal discourse,
to expound the essential doctrine,
repaying the grace of all saints' blessings.
But what is called the essential doctrine?
And how is the essential doctrine to be expounded?
Modern Dharma is truly lamentable.
False teachers expounding Dharma
are as numerous as Ganges' sands.
Each establishes their own school, each speaks of uniqueness,
continually fabricating, misleading later generations
beyond counting.
Chán practitioners lack the discerning Dharma eye,
while teachers also lack clear insight,
thus leading to this state.
Yúnmén initially didn't know Yuánzhāo,
but recently in Jiāngxī saw his colophon on the donated Huáyán "Brahma Conduct" chapter,
where he claimed understanding through the Brahma Conduct chapter,
not doubting all teachers' tongues.
Already then I grasped the essential point,
and told the brothers:
This person only understands "no Brahma conduct,"
already having his face stamped by false teachers.
If Yúnmén sees him,
I must try my utmost to save him.
When we met in Chánglè,
he came inquiring and entered the room.
Immediately I cut off his understanding with just two phrases:
"What you've understood
is what Yǒngjiā called 'empty openness denying cause and effect,'
vast and boundless, inviting calamity.'"
Further showing him mistaken evidence from the Brahma Conduct chapter:
"No grasping at the body,
no attachment to practice,
no abiding in dharmas.
Past already extinguished,
future not yet arrived,
present empty and still.
No doer of actions,
no receiver of results.
This world doesn't move,
that world doesn't change.
Here, what dharma is called Brahma conduct?
Where does Brahma conduct come from?
Who possesses it?
Whose essence is it?
By whom is it made?
Is it existent or non-existent?
Is it form or non-form?
Is it feeling or non-feeling?
Is it perception or non-perception?
Is it volition or non-volition?
Is it consciousness or non-consciousness?
Thus observing,
the Brahma conduct dharma is ungraspable."
If relying on this to claim no Brahma conduct
is true Brahma conduct,
this slanders the great prajñā,
entering hell like an arrow shot.
Further telling him:
"Nowadays various false teachers
each claim themselves
to have attained unsurpassed bodhi,
each speaking heterodox views,
deceiving and misleading people.
They misinterpret ancient enlightenment stories,
arbitrarily forcing interpretations.
Some take silence and wordlessness
as matters before the empty kalpa,
teaching people to cease and rest,
rest until like earth, wood, tile, or stone.
Then fear others say they sit in dark mountain ghost caves, subsequently citing ancestral testimony:
'Clearly constantly knowing,'
'Words cannot reach it.'
When resting like earth, wood, tile, or stone,
it's not dark unknowing,
but clearly aware and distinct,
walking, standing, sitting, lying,
constantly maintaining,
just practicing like this,
long time naturally merging with original mind."
Some take discarding emotional dust, not establishing fixed positions as their gate,
whenever ancient cases are raised,
immediately understanding.
If the master asks "Not mind, not Buddha, not thing,"
"How do you understand?"
They say:
"Master, quite aware!"
Or:
"Where has the master been?"
Or:
"Don't add point to arrow!"
Or:
"How many people deceived!"
Or repeating:
"Not mind, not Buddha, not thing."
Whenever asked about ancient causes,
they immediately grasp at the raising,
understanding at spark-strike lightning-flash moment,
raising equals understanding.
Whatever asked, all rejected,
called free and easy, attaining great joy.
Some take "three realms only mind, all dharmas only consciousness" as essential,
citing similar ancient passages as proof,
taking eye-seeing ear-hearing as attainment points.
All entry points
come from seeing things and awakening,
come from hearing sounds and awakening.
All their methods
imitate ancient similarities.
When someone asks,
they stick fixed to the question and answer,
called "wordless immediate unborn,"
like Fúzhōu people hemming cloth,
called "continuous without falling into emotion-dust."
Like a monk asking an ancient virtue:
"How to escape the three realms?"
Said: "Bring the three realms, I'll escape them for you."
Or: "What are the three realms?"
Or:
"Understand this monk's question,
escaping three realms isn't hard."
Like a monk asking Fǎyǎn:
"What is Cáoyuán's single drop of water?"
Answered:
"Is Cáoyuán's single drop of water."
Huì Chāo asked the master:
"What is Buddha?"
Answered:
"You are Huì Chāo."
Citing such examples as proof,
completely right yet completely wrong.
Again discussing Yàoshān's evening address:
"I have one phrase,
wait until bull bears calf,
then tell you."
A monk came forth:
"Bull already bore calf,
only master doesn't speak."
Yàoshān said:
"Light the lamp."
The monk returned to assembly.
Later Fǎdēng commented:
"Tell me,
was it male calf or female calf?"
Answering himself:
"Twins."
Discussing this as wordless unborn understanding.
Yàoshān said:
"I have one phrase,
'wait until bull bears calf' already spoke it."
So this monk understood and came forth:
"Bull already bore calf,
only master doesn't speak."
Truly continuous without exposing edge.
Fǎdēng tested: "Tell me,
was it male calf or female calf?"
Again answering himself:
"Twins."
Also taken as wordless unborn understanding:
He asked male/female calf,
then answered himself:
"Twins,"
without slightest remainder,
Buddha's eye cannot see.
Taking such words
as precise breakthrough without exposure, effortless understanding.
Again like ancients pointing to a stone asking learners:
"This stone,
inside mind or outside mind?"
Answering:
"Inside mind."
Ancient virtue said:
"Why so desperately urgent?
Mind containing a stone?"
Assembly discussions said:
"Shouldn't answer inside/outside; if inside/outside answered,
then dharma has remainder."
Speaking:
"Fine stone indeed!"
Or:
"Deeply understand the question,"
Or:
"What is called a stone?"
Or:
"Yes, yes,"
Or:
"Before the Dharma hall,"
Or:
"Thanks for pointing,"
Or:
"Master, still know shame?"
Or:
"Extremely dull,"
All such answers
wrapped in one phrase,
called "continuous,"
called "not straying,"
such views
very common in communities.
Some say all language irrelevant,
when raising awareness first stare wide-eyed like children seeing ghosts,
grasping at staring frowning glaring moments,
mistakenly citing ancient evidence:
"Raising without looking differs,"
"Thinking when will awaken?"
Raising must gaze with eyes,
just repeating ancient phrases,
called "not in words,"
like "cypress tree," "wash bowl," "three pounds hemp" etc.
If passing one such,
others passed easily,
without effort.
Such types
compared to spark-strike lightning-flash types
only add staring frowning glaring,
each claiming ancestral authenticity.
Don't slander ancients!
Like raising monk asking Yúnmén:
"What penetrates Dharma body?"
Yúnmén said:
"Hide in Big Dipper."
How do you understand?
Learner stares wide-eyed:
"Hide in Big Dipper."
Master may temporarily suppress learner,
repeating several times:
"Hide in Big Dipper,
Hide in Big Dipper,"
thinking firmly established, self-mastered,
not turned by calling,
master cannot handle,
called "genuine,"
then asking meaning,
answers:
"Buddha's eye cannot see,"
Or:
"Look beyond heaven,"
Or asking:
"What's ancestral meaning from West?"
"Court cypress tree,"
answers:
"Branch south, branch north,"
Or:
"Can host all phenomena,
not fading with seasons."
All this in staring frowning glaring repetition,
then giving matching phrases,
considered extraordinary.
Fool!
Not that staring frowning glaring has Chán,
not staring frowning glaring lacks Chán.
Not that repeating has Chán,
not repeating lacks Chán.
Some hearing Yúnmén say this
mistakenly think:
"Repeating is right,
not repeating is right,
no difference,"
such people
truly unsavable.
Some ignore completely, hearing Buddhism mentioned,
hearing awakening mentioned,
go mad,
mistakenly citing ancients:
"Originally no deluded awakened person,
only need today finish."
All ancient causes
called expedient means,
also called establishing genuine,
only where no Buddhist discussion occurs,
all questions answered
simply according to reality,
ordinary nothing-special,
heaven heaven, earth earth,
pillar wood,
guardian clay,
hungry eat, sleepy sleep,
what else matters?
Haven't you heard
Zhēnjìng master say:
"Don't use nothing-special understanding,
nothing-special traps people's minds."
Often those poisoned by nothing-special
reject this saying.
Some seeing ancient cases
cannot reason logically,
use irrelevant phrases
responding everywhere,
called mysterious, called beyond meaning,
called immediate penetration.
Like monk asking Zhàozhōu:
"All dharmas return to one, where does one return?"
Zhàozhōu said:
"I made a cloth gown in Qīngzhōu weighing seven pounds" etc.
Many mistakenly discuss:
This monk's question extraordinary,
if Zhàozhōu lacked escape route
couldn't handle it.
"All dharmas return to one,
one returns nowhere.
If somewhere to return,
then existent dharma,
so Zhàozhōu saw through,
immediate wondrous function,
directly responding:
'I made cloth gown weighing seven pounds,'
how extraordinary!"
Some discuss:
"All dharmas return to one, where does one return?
If one returns nowhere,
falls into emptiness,
so Zhàozhōu said:
'I made cloth gown weighing seven pounds,'
Zhàozhōu's turning phrase
truly extraordinary,
not falling existence/non-existence,
answered perfectly."
Some say:
Yúnmén speaking thus
only fears people clinging,
if not clinging,
that's ancestral mind.
What is essential is simply the matter at hand.
Do not cling to freedom or naturalness.
It is not apart from the true that a standpoint is established.
Where a standpoint is established, there is the true.
What further matter could there be?
Some ask, "Before your parents were born, what was your original face?"
Then they say,
"The attendant has no reply for the venerable monk."
Taking this deluded consciousness as the fundamental destiny.
Such kinds
are all madmen running outside.
There is another type
who themselves know their Dharma-eye is not clear,
their Chan cannot gain people's trust,
and they have no means to instruct learners.
They themselves have never studied the teachings,
yet hastily become petty dealers with lecture masters,
snatching a phrase or half-sentence to flatter the deaf masses.
Venerable Linji said:
"There are certain blind bald-headed fellows
who take meanings from the teachings and sutras to deliberate,
forming them into phrases and meanings,
like taking a piece of excrement in their mouth and then spitting it out to others.
This is truly unbearable."
Yuánzhāo initially heard this said,
and though doubtful in mind,
his words were very stubborn,
even sneering at this mountain monk.
That evening in the room, I just asked him the phrase about the dog having no Buddha-nature,
and he couldn't proceed, only then realizing that practicing Chan requires awakening.
He stayed in Chánglè for ten days,
coming to the room twenty times,
exhausting all his tricks yet unable to manage.
Only then did he start to feel anxious.
This mountain monk truly told him:
"You don't need to display tricks.
You must directly break through completely and cleanly to confront life and death.
What end is there in displaying tricks?"
Still I told him:
"You don't need to rush.
If you cannot realize it in this life, realize it in the next."
Then he became convinced and took his leave.
After more than ten days, he suddenly sent a letter,
along with ten ancient verses,
all about causes and conditions this mountain monk asked him in the room.
The letter said:
"On the road to Yánpíng,
I suddenly had an insight.
I ultimately dare not deceive myself.
Only then do I believe this matter
is not obtained from others."
One of the verses said:
Not mind, not Buddha, not things,
The whole body is a string of golden bones.
Zhàozhōu visited old Nánquán,
And understood he said Zhènzhōu produces radishes.
This mountain monk was quite doubtful.
Then Guāng Chán asked,
"According to this verse, can it resolve life and death or not?"
Yúnmén told him:
"It can resolve it, yet it cannot resolve it.
You should go ask Yuánzhāo."
When I received Guāng Chán's letter, it said:
"When the scholar official met me,
it was exactly as the venerable monk said."
Everyone, tell me,
what was said?
Ah!
It puzzles everyone under heaven.
Those with discerning eyes, distinguish for yourselves.
Those who practice Chan nowadays,
do not ask whether they can resolve life and death or not,
but only seek quick results,
and want to understand Chan.
There is not one who does not speak of principles.
Like the donor official,
seeing that he loved discussing principles,
I thus showed him a causeless condition without principle,
for him to see.
A monk asked Yúnmén,
"What is Buddha?"
Yúnmén said,
"A dry shit-stick."
Fearing he would understand it as a principle,
I first told him not to say
that the Way is in piss and shit,
the Way is in weeds,
the Way is in tiles and pebbles,
clarifying mind through form,
manifesting principle through things,
or say that everywhere is true, every speck is the original person, and such.
He looked at this saying,
but couldn't handle it,
using all his strength to look,
yet ultimately couldn't see through.
Suddenly one day he understood this matter
cannot be penetrated through principles,
and said, "I have an awakening."
Then he composed several verses consecutively to present his understanding.
One said: The vast void is forced to have a name,
Even Sēngyóu could not paint it.
Why seek the source and ask the exact point?
There is not a single dharma that can grasp it.
Another said:
Upon arriving home, why speak of the journey?
In spring, ten thousand trees naturally flourish.
If meeting upstream to ask each other,
The sun wheel rises east of Fúsāng.
Another said:
After the age of fifty, cease pursuing,
The wonderful secret emptily transmitted at Shàolín.
Leisurely plucking a tune without strings,
Clear breeze and bright moon both know the melody.
Another said:
Letting go at the cliff's edge, truly without falsehood,
Sense faculties and objects instantly exhausted, with nothing left.
Only then know the Buddha-dharma hasn't much to offer,
Seeking outwardly only shows greater distance.
This mountain monk told him:
"Composing verses is fine,
speaking principles is also fine,
but you are only going farther from the Way."
He was not convinced,
and composed another verse:
Avoid discussing mystery and speaking subtleties,
How can one follow sounds and pursue forms?
Sweep away this lump altogether,
Everyone has no insight at all.
He also sent a letter saying:
"Looking at this saying,
directly the path of speech is cut off, the place of mental activity ceases,
no words to speak,
no principle to express,
not arising the slightest mind of cultivation or learning,
knowing nothing, understanding nothing,
not involved in thought, not entering reasoning,
truly peaceful and happy."
This mountain monk again told him:
"This is an exceptional principle.
If the dry shit-stick saying
can be expressed like this, then like sawing through a steelyard weight,
'three pounds of flax,'
'the dog has no Buddha-nature,'
'one mouth drinking all the water of the Western River,'
'not mind, not Buddha, not things,'
'having phrases, no phrases, like a vine relying on a tree,'
the sayings 'mind is Buddha,'
all can be expressed like this.
Since it cannot be like this,
you must awaken to attain it.
Awakened, matters are of one family;
unawakened, they are thousands of differences.
A hair's breadth difference misses by a thousand miles.
You must be extremely careful.
Even if people say Yúnmén treats the donor disrespectfully,
my heart does not betray others, my face shows no shame."
He saw this mountain monk advising him with such utmost sincerity,
and only then knew the Buddha-dharma has no human sentiment.
Then he became convinced. Since he was convinced,
I just taught him to look: "What is Buddha? A dry shit-stick."
I only wanted him to break through completely and cleanly.
If because he, as an official, gave up wealth to build a hermitage,
established fields to support the community,
and even supported this mountain monk,
one then considers it correct,
then all the poor people in the whole world
would have no share in practicing Chan.
Not only would it lose the wise teacher's discerning eye,
it would also cheat him for hundreds of kalpas and thousands of lifetimes.
This is no small matter.
This summer, several more monks,
unwilling to put effort into the effortless place,
only busily rushing about,
also came to present their understanding,
composing ancient verses.
Yúnmén told them:
"This is not the principle."
They said, "You are blocking
and not letting them go."
I ask you,
have you yourselves let go or not?
Zhàozhōu said:
"Other places are hard to see, easy to recognize;
here it is easy to see, hard to recognize."
Yúnmén usually asks practitioners:
"Call it a bamboo stick, you're stuck;
don't call it a bamboo stick, you turn away.
You cannot speak,
you cannot be silent."
Out of ten, five have blind eyes.
Even if there are those acting clever, presenting understanding,
using all their strength to say the word 'lift,'
some snatch the bamboo stick from my hand,
some flick their sleeves and leave.
Other wrong understandings are too numerous to count.
Not one has blood under their skin.
An ancient virtue said:
"This matter is like an eighty-year-old man entering the examination hall;
it's no child's play.
If it could be molded together,
millions would have been molded already.
Since it cannot be molded,
one must awaken to attain it.
Besides this, there is no other principle.
If you truly have an awakening,
and the teacher deliberately says it's not,
the karmic consequences are also not small."
Today, because of the feast offering and celebration, I present this to everyone.
It was because Huáng Duānfū came to know of Yúnmén
through Yuánzhāo initially.
Guāng Chán went to stay at his hermitage
also because of Yuánzhāo.
Duānfū's two sons today set up this feast, inviting this mountain monk for this universal discourse, also because of Yuánzhāo.
Yúnmén speaking all this tangled talk is also because of Yuánzhāo.
Since it is so,
tell me,
what, after all, is Yuánzhāo's matter?
After a long pause, he said:
"Wait until he personally comes to Yúnmén this winter,
then I will explain it to everyone."
He struck the Chan seat and descended the platform.
The State of Qín's Grand Lady requested a universal discourse.
A monk asked:
The Sūtra of Perfect Enlightenment says, for instance, a pure mani pearl reflects the five colors.
Before the colors appear, where is the pearl? The Master said:
How does the Sūtra of Perfect Enlightenment ever say it like that?
The monk continued:
I'm not sure how to understand it.
The Master said:
The Sūtra of Perfect Enlightenment never said it like that.
What else is there to understand?
The monk continued:
After all, how is it?
The Master said:
In stillness, svāhā.
Question: I won't ask about Hú Zhāngsān or Hēi Lǐsì,
but how long is the nose of the Great Statue in Jiāzhōu?
The Master said:
It's over two hundred zhǎng long.
The monk continued:
How can it be so sloppy?
The Master said:
You, a monk from Chuān, ought to know.
The monk continued:
Why was it swallowed by the iron ox of Shǎn Prefecture?
The Master said:
Who said that?
The monk continued:
Viewed from high up, it's not enough; from low down, it's more than level.
The Master said:
Try speaking from neither high nor low.
The monk said: Dangerous.
The Master said:
That's still from a place of high and low.
The monk continued:
When there's spirit, add spirit.
The Master said:
The grass bandits are utterly defeated.
Then he said:
Today is the birthday celebration of the State of Qín's Grand Lady, Madame Jì,
Dharma True.
She reverently offered pure wealth,
traveled far to this mountain to set up a pure vegetarian feast for the Chan assembly,
and still commanded this mountain wild one
to ascend this seat,
to give a universal discourse for the assembly,
expounding prajñā.
May she progress on the path without demons,
her physical body safe and well.
This is the intention of the State of Qín's Grand Lady.
This old woman's lifelong conduct,
every monk from Chuān knows it.
Only the monks from Lǔ do not yet know.
Today, because of the feast, celebrating and praising, I'll present it to the great assembly.
I've heard that when this old woman was around thirty years old,
the former Grand Master passed away, and Huīyóu
and the Minister were still young.
She stood firm and independent,
sternly with an air that could not be offended.
East and west neighbors, seeing her demeanor, knew to be in awe.
She strictly taught her two sons to study,
handling affairs with great family discipline.
Normally, when Huīyóu
and the Minister attended to her left and right,
if not told to sit, they dared not sit.
Such was her strictness.
The Minister often said:
His official position today
is all due to his old mother's education in the past.
Beyond daily household meals,
the old mother gave all the rest as alms to support monks,
to pray for the longevity of our sovereign.
He often felt ashamed of receiving emoluments without merit.
Hearing that the former Master returned to Shǔ,
he received much support from her,
only she did not yet know Chan meditation.
Huīyóu and the Minister,
however, each had their awakening at the former Master's place.
When Qiān Chán was at their home,
Huīyóu and the Minister
personally told Qiān:
Our old mother has practiced for forty years,
only lacking this one step.
You have long attended Jìngshān和尚,
hearing and seeing much.
Please stay to accompany her morning and evening in conversation,
for in the relationship between us brothers and our mother, it's hard to speak.
It's said that every day when gathering with Qiān,
he solely encouraged this matter.
One day she asked Qiān:
How does Jìngshān和尚 usually teach people?
Qiān said:
The和尚 only teaches people to contemplate the phrase "Does a dog have Buddha-nature?"
and the bamboo stick phrase.
Just don't use words,
don't think about it, don't try to understand it where it's raised,
don't grasp it at the opening of the mouth.
"Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not?"
"No."
Just so, he teaches people to contemplate.
She then deeply believed,
investigating day and night.
She always loved reading sūtras and worshiping Buddha.
Qiān said:
The和尚 usually says,
to accomplish this matter,
one must stop reading sūtras, worshiping Buddha, reciting mantras, and such,
and instead rest the mind in investigation,
not letting the effort be interrupted.
If one always clings to reading sūtras and worshiping Buddha, seeking merit,
that becomes an obstruction to the path.
Wait until one thought corresponds,
then again read sūtras and worship Buddha.
Even one incense, one flower, one glance, one bow,
all actions are not in vain;
they are all the wonderful function of Buddha.
It's also practicing based on the root.
Just trust and listen; it certainly won't mislead you.
Hearing Qiān's words,
she immediately put it all down,
focusing solely on sitting in meditation,
contemplating the phrase "Does a dog have Buddha-nature?"
It's heard that last winter, one night she suddenly woke from sleep, got up in high spirits to sit in meditation and raise the phrase,
and abruptly had a point of joy.
Recently, Qiān returned to the State of Qín,
bringing a personal letter and several verses to present to this mountain monk.
One of the verses says:
Every day reading the sūtra text,
it's like meeting an old acquaintance.
Don't say there are frequent obstacles,
each raising brings something new.
This mountain monk often tells the brothers,
after realizing Chan,
whenever reading scriptural texts,
it's like walking once through your own home.
It's also like meeting an old acquaintance.
Now this verse by the State of Qín
covertly matches Sūn and Wú's strategies.
Look at her, a woman,
yet truly having the actions of a great man,
able to accomplish the affairs of a great man.
Qiān Chán came up yesterday to tell this mountain monk,
to carefully explain some Chan sicknesses,
and to form a prajñā connection with the State of Qín and the great assembly.
This mountain monk said to him:
What sickness does Chan have to speak of?
Chan has never had a headache,
never had foot pain,
never been deaf,
never been blind.
It's just that people who meditate on Chan
meditate differently,
realize differently,
apply their minds differently, rely on teachers differently.
Because of these differences,
it's called sickness.
It's not that Chan has sickness.
What is Buddha?
The mind itself is Buddha.
What sickness is there?
"Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not?"
"No."
What sickness is there?
Call it a bamboo stick and you're attached;
don't call it a bamboo stick and you're contrary.
What sickness is there?
What is Buddha?
Three pounds of flax.
What sickness is there?
What is Buddha?
A dried shit stick.
What sickness is there?
If you don't penetrate it,
and just make rationalizations, trying to penetrate it, you're a thousand miles away, unrelated.
Trying to approach it with the mind,
trying to think about it with the mind,
grasping it where it's raised,
understanding it at the spark from struck stone or flash of lightning—
this is what is called sickness.
Worldly doctors can only fold their hands.
Yet ultimately, it's not Chan's affair.
Zhàozhōu said:
If you want to be a disciple of the King of Emptiness,
don't let the sickness of the mind be hardest to cure.
I remember Śāriputra asked the Moon Maiden:
You now,
what vehicle do you practice?
Do you practice the Śrāvaka vehicle,
the Pratyekabuddha vehicle,
or the Mahāyāna?
The Moon Maiden replied:
Śāriputra,
since you ask me what vehicle I practice,
I now ask you in return:
Śāriputra,
please answer me as you wish.
As for the Dharma you have realized,
do you practice the Śrāvaka vehicle,
the Pratyekabuddha vehicle,
or the Mahāyāna?
Śāriputra said:
No.
Moon Maiden,
why?
Because that Dharma
cannot be differentiated,
cannot be spoken of,
neither different nor one,
nor many.
The Moon Maiden said:
Śāriputra,
therefore, one should not differentiate the one appearance or different appearances of all dharmas, nor appearance without difference.
Among all appearances, there is nothing to abide in.
The Master said:
Śāriputra asked like this,
the Moon Maiden answered like this.
Tell me,
how far is it from the Dharma realized by the State of Qín's Grand Lady?
Is there anyone who can judge?
Try coming out to judge.
If not,
then try to recognize it within the entanglements.
Therefore, it is said:
Those who study meditation
must study the living phrase,
not the dead phrase.
If you recognize under the living phrase,
you'll never forget it for eternity.
If you recognize under the dead phrase,
you can't even save yourself.
You all,
every day going up and down,
in the quarters drinking tea and soup,
at the estate carrying salt and flour,
in the monks' hall walking and benefiting,
under the long corridor selecting vegetables,
in the back garden carrying manure,
below the millhouse turning the millstone.
At such times,
even the Buddha's eye doesn't see you.
Tell me,
is it a dead phrase, a living phrase, or a neither-dead-nor-living phrase?
Try to determine it. Even if you can determine it,
you're still within the three phrases.
Haven't you heard?
A monk asked Nánquán和尚:
"The mind itself is Buddha" doesn't work,
"Not mind, not Buddha" doesn't work either.
What is your intention?
Nánquán said:
You just believe that the mind itself is Buddha, that's all.
Why talk about whether it works or not?
It's like you, Virtuous One, having eaten,
go from the east corridor to the west corridor.
You can't always ask people whether it works or not.
Here, if you recognize Nánquán,
then you won't be used by the three phrases,
but will be able to use the three phrases.
Once you can use the three phrases,
then you'll share the same eyes with Nánquán,
the same ears,
the same nose to smell,
the same tongue to taste,
the same body to perceive,
the same mind,
with no difference at all.
It's just because you mistake the medicine for the sickness,
the old sickness not yet removed,
new sickness arises again.
Instead, you're turned upside down
by the dead and living phrases.
You twist the ancient ones' direct path
all at once.
So, what is the ancient ones' direct path?
I'll cite one or two examples for you.
For instance, Nánquán said:
Lead the cow to the east of the stream to graze,
it will inevitably eat the king's water and grass there.
Lead the cow to the west of the stream to graze,
it will inevitably eat the king's water and grass there.
Better to just accept a little as it comes.
Many people misunderstand this gōng'àn.
How many misjudge it?
What is the principle of "accepting a little"?
They say:
Wearing clothes and eating meals, what's so difficult?
Making a living before donkeys and behind horses.
Don't slander Nánquán.
Since you misunderstand this one,
you'll surely misunderstand the next.
Huángbò said:
All of you
are just eaters of wine dregs.
Going on pilgrimage like this,
how could you have today?
Do you know there are no Chan masters in the land of the Great Táng?
Then a monk came forth and said:
What about those in various places who guide disciples and lead assemblies?
How about that?
Huángbò said:
I don't say there's no Chan,
only that there are no teachers.
This saying
is a source of trouble.
Don't say those who haven't awakened misunderstand it;
even if awakened thoroughly from head to tail,
if the great Dharma is not clear,
they still don't see Huángbò.
For instance, Huángbò said:
"I don't say there's no Chan, only that there are no teachers."
How do you understand this?
Some in the assembly discuss it, saying:
In everyone's own share, who is not a true man?
Why rely on a teacher's transmission?
Eating wine dregs means biting on words and speech.
Words and speech are the dregs of the ancients.
But that's irrelevant.
If you wish not to incur uninterrupted karma, do not slander the Tathāgata's true Dharma wheel.
Haven't you heard?
Wéishān brought up this saying and asked Yǎngshān:
What is Huángbò's meaning?
Yǎngshān said:
The goose king selects milk,
it's never been of the duck's kind.
Wéishān said:
This is truly hard to discern.
Now, with Wéishān and Yǎngshān asking and answering like this,
how do you discuss it?
Here, one must be a true person to understand.
Since you don't understand this one,
you take the cypress tree in the courtyard, three pounds of flax, the dried shit stick, the sawed scale weight, and such,
all as dregs.
Since you misunderstand this one, you'll surely misunderstand the next.
Dòngshān asked Chán the Head Seat:
The Buddha's true Dharma body is like empty space,
responding to things and appearing in forms, like the moon in water.
How do you speak of the principle of responding? Chán said:
Like a donkey looking into a well.
Dòngshān said:
You've spoken greatly,
but only eighty percent.
Chán said:
How about you,和尚?
Dòngshān said:
Like the well looking at the donkey.
Various places discuss it, saying:
"Like a donkey looking into a well" has traces;
"Like the well looking at the donkey" is traceless.
It's also called forgetting feelings and wiping away traces.
But that's irrelevant.
And it's not this principle.
Having misunderstood this point, they further misunderstand.
Monk Nányuè said:
It is like an ox pulling a cart.
If the cart does not move,
should you strike the cart,
or strike the ox?
Upon hearing this, Mǎzǔ suddenly attained great enlightenment.
Nowadays, Zen practitioners
explain it as:
The ox symbolizes the mind, the cart symbolizes the Dharma.
Simply illuminate the mind, and the Dharma will naturally be clear.
Just strike the ox,
and the cart will move by itself.
But this is completely missing the point.
If it were like that,
Mǎzǔ would never have attained enlightenment even in a donkey's year.
This old fellow
initially thought
that Buddhahood could be attained by sitting,
and Zen could be realized by sitting in meditation.
He persistently sat waiting.
Monk Nányuè, knowing he was no ordinary person,
therefore took a brick and ground it in front of his hut.
Mǎzǔ asked:
"Reverend, what are you grinding the brick for?"
Nányuè replied:
"To make a mirror."
Mǎzǔ said:
"How can grinding a brick make a mirror?"
Nányuè responded:
"If grinding a brick cannot make a mirror,
how can sitting in meditation make a Buddha?"
Mǎzǔ, stirred by this,
felt anxious in his heart,
and asked:
"What then should be done?"
Right here, the nose-ring rope
was already in Monk Nányuè's hand.
Therefore it is said:
"To understand the meaning of Buddha-nature,
observe the timing and conditions."
Monk Nányuè knew his time had come,
and said to him:
"Are you learning to sit in meditation, or learning to sit as a Buddha?
If learning to sit in meditation,
Zen is not sitting or lying.
If learning to sit as a Buddha,
Buddha has no fixed form.
In the dharma of non-abiding,
one should not grasp or reject.
If you sit as a Buddha,
you are killing the Buddha.
If you cling to the form of sitting,
you have not reached its principle."
At once, he confiscated all his possessions,
yet still demanded he pay tribute,
leaving him with nowhere to turn,
until he was willing to give up his life,
seeking a place to die.
Once his life was relinquished,
he then understood to ask:
"How should the mind be applied to accord with formless samādhi?"
Nányuè said:
"Your learning the Dharma-gate of the mind-ground
is like sowing seeds.
My expounding the essential Dharma
is like the rain from heaven.
Your conditions being ripe, you shall see the Way."
He asked further:
"The Way is without form;
how can it be seen?"
Nányuè said:
"The Dharma-eye of the mind-ground can see the Way;
formless samādhi is also like this."
Mǎzǔ asked:
"Does it have creation and destruction?"
Nányuè replied:
"If one sees the Way in terms of creation, destruction, aggregation, and dispersion, that is incorrect."
Thereupon, Mǎzǔ's doubts melted away; as the saying goes, "If you do not enter the tiger's den,
you cannot catch the tiger's cub."
Even if enlightened, without meeting a true teacher, ten out of five pairs will concoct interpretations,
and certainly cannot guide others.
Do you all wish to recognize one who, having attained enlightenment, met a true teacher?
This very Mǎzǔ
is the example.
After Mǎzǔ attained the Dharma,
he went directly to Jiāngxī and established his teaching.
One day, Monk Nányuè said:
"Dàoyī is expounding the Dharma in Jiāngxī,
but we haven't received any news from him."
He then instructed a monk, saying:
"You go, and when he ascends the hall, ask him:
'What is this?'
Observe what he says,
and remember it to report back."
The monk followed the instruction.
Seeing Mǎzǔ ascend the hall, he came forth and asked:
"What is this?"
Mǎzǔ said:
"Since the turmoil thirty years ago,
I've never lacked salt or sauce." The Master addressed the assembly, saying:
"Those under the Patriarch's school who have their noses pierced
all come from this one phrase."
You tell me,
this one phrase,
where does it come from?
It comes from striking the ox and striking the cart.
If you understand this,
you will also understand the old woman on the road to Táishān.
Whenever a monk asked,
"Which way to Táishān?"
The old woman would say:
"Go straight ahead."
As soon as the monk started walking,
the old woman would say:
"A fine master, yet he goes off like that!"
Zhàozhōu, hearing of this, said:
"I'll go and test this old woman."
Zhàozhōu went to see the old woman and asked the same question.
The old woman gave the same answer.
Returning, he said to the assembly:
"The old woman on the road to Táishān
has been seen through by this old monk."
Do you all understand?
The emperor's decree within the realm;
the general's order beyond the borders.
Just look at it like this.
In earlier years, I could not comprehend this,
and once sought instruction from a presumptuous elder,
who explained it to me thus:
"As soon as this monk asked, 'Which way to Táishān?'
he was already seen through by the old woman.
The old woman said,
'Go straight ahead.'
The monk then walked.
Precisely following sound and chasing form—
how could he not be seen through?"
He also said:
"The moment he opened his mouth, he was seen through."
Thinking about it now,
it is truly unbearable.
I will explain it clearly for you:
If you understand Zhàozhōu saying, "The old woman on the road to Táishān has been seen through by this old monk,"
then you will understand the old woman saying, "A fine master, yet he goes off like that!"
I once composed a verse:
"All under heaven's Zen practitioners speak of seeing through;
Who knows Zhàozhōu's words had already fallen?
Leading descendants to be less than stalwart;
Each cleverer, lying down in a cold place."
This verse is very clear;
you must not misunderstand it.
Having misunderstood this point, they further misunderstand.
Mùzhōu called to a monk, "Virtuous one!"
The monk turned his head.
Mùzhōu said:
"Carrying-plank fellow!"
There was once a Zen head
who brought up this story and asked a monk,

As soon as the monk opened his mouth, he said:
"Indeed, a carrying-plank fellow!"
But this is completely missing the point.
Xuědòu, raising the case, said:
"Mùzhōu only has one eye.
Since this monk turned his head when called,
why did he become a carrying-plank fellow?"
Huìtáng said:
"Xuědòu also only has one eye.
This monk turned his head as soon as called;
why wasn't he a carrying-plank fellow?"
These two old fellows
could walk hand in hand with Mùzhōu.
If it were a sharp fellow,
upon hearing this brought up,
his eyes would be like bronze bells—
he would never dally here.
Having failed to understand this point, they further misunderstand.
The story of Bǎizhàng's wild fox:
they then say,
"Not falling is also it,
not obscuring is also it.
It's just that when answering this question at that time,
he shouldn't have harbored doubt,
hence he fell into the wild fox state,
because wild foxes are inherently doubtful."
But this is completely missing the point.
Having misunderstood this point, they further misunderstand.
The Patriarch said:
"It is not the wind that moves, not the banner that moves;
it is your mind that moves."
I once sought instruction from an elder,
asking what the meaning was.
The elder waved his sleeve in the gesture of wind moving and said:
"What is this?"
How pitiful! How pitiful!
Shameful and mortifying!
Stupefying and confounding!
Some say:
"Not the wind moving, not the banner moving,
it must be the mind moving."
I often ask students:
"Not the wind moving,
not the banner moving,
not the mind moving—
what then?"
Here, how can blinking be tolerated?
Having misunderstood this point, they further misunderstand.
Wénshū is the teacher of the seven Buddhas;

Why could Wǎngmíng Bodhisattva bring her out?
Among the assembly, some discuss it, saying:
"The ladle handle was in the woman's hand."
But this is completely missing the point.
Having misunderstood this point, they further misunderstand.
Xuěfēng said:
"At Wàngzhōu Pavilion, I have met with you;
at Wūshí Ridge, I have met with you;
in front of the monks' hall, I have met with you."
Nowadays, various places discuss it, saying:
"What is the meeting place at Wàngzhōu Pavilion?"
They then say:
"Buying cheap in the south, selling dear in the north."
"What is the meaning of meeting at Wūshí Ridge?"
They then say:

They then say:
"Return to the hall and have some tea."
But this is completely missing the point.
As for other erroneous interpretations,
they are too numerous to count.
I often ask students as well:
"At Wàngzhōu Pavilion, I have met with you;
at Wūshí Ridge, I have met with you;
in front of the monks' hall, I have met with you—
what then?"
This is precisely the diamond hoop and the chestnut-vine burr;
how will you swallow it, how will you penetrate it?
Do you wish to know one who can swallow and penetrate?
Have you not heard?
Bǎofú asked Éhú:
"Setting aside the monks' hall for now,
where did you meet at Wàngzhōu Pavilion and Wūshí Ridge?" Éhú swiftly walked back to the abbot's room.
Bǎofú then entered the monks' hall.
Monk Fényáng composed a verse, saying:
"Wàngzhōu, Wūshí, and before the hall;
Meetings and understandings, how many thousands?
Only Éhú and Bǎofú—
At this moment, their understanding shifted."
This verse has clearly spoken for you.
Having failed to understand this point, they further misunderstand.
Xuánshā said:
"Everywhere it is said
we should receive beings and benefit them.
But if three kinds of sick people come,
how should we receive them?
For the blind, raising the hammer or whisk, they do not see;
for the deaf, speaking the samādhi of language, they do not hear;
for the mute, telling them to speak, they cannot speak.
If we cannot receive such people,
the Buddha-Dharma has no efficacy."
The Master looked at the assembly and said:
"Do you wish to know Xuánshā?
His whole life, heart and gall laid bare to others;
acquainted yet as if unacquainted."
At that time, Monk Dìzàng was in the assembly;
he came forth and said:
"I have a mouth and am not mute;
have eyes and am not blind;
have ears and am not deaf—
how will you receive me, Reverend?"
The Master said:
"Not from the father, the son is not born."
Xuánshā laughed heartily.
The Master said:
"There is a knife within the laughter."
I sometimes bring up this story and ask students;
some come imitating like drawing a gourd from a model,
also saying:
"I have a mouth, ears, and eyes—
how will you receive me, Reverend?"
I say to them:
"Biting a piece of shit-stick—
not a good dog."
Yet they still cannot get past it.
Having misunderstood this point, they further misunderstand.
Xiāngyán said:

The Master said:

In earlier years, I sought instruction from a venerable,

He then put the handle of his whisk in his mouth,

The Master snapped his fingers and said:

the rest, with their bizarre actions, go without saying.
Do you wish to understand?
Just regard it as a single phrase.
I will first tell you:
Do not think that regarding it as a single phrase means understanding it at the moment of raising it.
Thinking that once raised, it is understood—
that is not the principle here.
What then is the principle?
"Like a person climbing a tree,
mouth holding a branch,

Below the tree, someone asks about the meaning of the West.
Not answering fails the questioner;
if answering, one loses body and life." How, in this place where there is not even a hair's breadth of room,

The Master said:

The Master said:

Later, Xuědòu, raising the case, said:

This old monk has also climbed the tree; bring me a question."
Though Xuědòu gave support to head monk Hǔtóu,

What is the meaning of the Patriarch's coming from the West?
The cypress tree in the courtyard.
And what harm is there?
You might as well understand it well.
Have you not seen the verse of Monk Fényáng?
Xiāngyán held a tree in his mouth to show many people,
Wanting to guide his fellow monks to realize the fundamental truth.
The Master said:
Confess according to the truth.
If you deliberate and seek within words,

The Master said:

The Master said:
Idle talk.
Even so,

Bǎizhàng asked Guīshān, Wǔfēng, and Yúnyán:

Guīshān said:

Bǎizhàng said:

Bǎizhàng said:

Among the assembly, it is discussed:

The three responding like this,
everyone runs into the wild grass."
Fortunately, it's irrelevant.
I tell you,
this matter certainly does not lie in words.
Since it is not in words,
at such a time, what should be done?
I have already told you.
Since you misunderstand this one,

Déshān said:

Yuánmíng said:

Fortunately, it's irrelevant.

Here is the sword that should cut but doesn't, to avoid chaos.
Therefore, Xuědòu said:

Fortunately, it's irrelevant.
If Chán is understood in this way,

The clever and sharp-witted immediately generate understanding from words,
interpret and annotate, and that's it.
I ask you:

when life and death arrive, how will you handle it?
Now I clearly tell you:
These idle words and lengthy speeches,
are the path to transcend life and death.
Do not plant thorns or dig latrines on this path.
If perhaps a monk comes out and says,
'Master, right here,
you are planting thorns and digging latrines,'
if not, how should one respond?
This mountain monk has an excuse.
And how is that excuse?
Listen to a verse:
Among women, there is a great hero,
Manifesting her body to teach her kind.
With precepts, meditation, wisdom, and liberation,
She tames their greed, anger, and delusion.
Though dwelling among them, performing Buddha's work,
Like wind traversing the sky, with nothing to rely on.
Past, future, and present,
Buddhas and bodhisattvas as numerous as sands, with different mouths but the same voice, utter these words:
'Excellent, extraordinary, rare in the world,
The source of mind is pure, without worry or joy,
Not making thoughts of no joy and no worry.
Engaging as appropriate, following worldly conditions,
Yet unattached to worldly conditions.'
The fiery clouds of June burn the azure sky,
Suddenly, thunder shakes the three thousand realms.
Dispelling heat and affliction, obtaining cool clarity,
That is the season of that hero's birth.
I speak this verse to aid the light,
Universally bestowing it upon all women in the Dharma realm.
*Shouts once.*
Qián Jìyì requested a universal discourse.
A monk asked:
In the past, a monk asked Monk Yángqí:
"What is Buddha?"
He replied:
"A three-legged donkey kicking up its hooves as it walks."
I am uncertain of the intended meaning.
The Master said:
"No trace exists throughout heaven and earth."
The monk advanced:
"Just as before King Wēiyīn,
who was it that rode?"
The Master said:
"After King Wēiyīn,
who was it that rode?"
As the monk hesitated,
the Master gave a shout.
Then he said:
"Before King Wēiyīn,
the three-legged donkey leaped and pranced."
After King Wēiyīn,
Old Man Yángqí cut off all traces."
Since all traces are cut off,
why then does the three-legged donkey leap and prance?"
If you can understand this,
then you'll know the three-legged donkey before King Wēiyīn indeed leaped and pranced."
If you cannot understand,
Old Man Yángqí has been wronged his whole life."
Right at such a moment,
what is the phrase that clears this wrong?"
Shouting once, he said:
"Almost certainly playing with danger."
He continued:
"Venerable Yùnwén,
today representing Zǐxū,
has come to request a universal discourse for the assembly."
This old man said:
"What should I speak about?"
Yùnwén said:
"Please, Venerable, bring out Yángqí's diamond circle and chestnut-bramble ball,
to bestow upon the assembly."
He also said:
"Like National Teacher Zhōng and Great Pearl Monk's way of expounding the Dharma,
many in various places greatly doubt it,
saying it drags through mud and brings along water,
not directly cutting through to expound the meaning of principle in Chán.
I wish the Venerable would clarify true and false,
resolving the assembly's doubts."
This too is the intention of the donor requesting the universal discourse.
This old man said:
"Very well. Thus the Great Awakened World-Honored One, first realizing this matter,
for twenty-one days in Magadha had no place to open his mouth,
saying himself:
'I'd rather not expound the Dharma,
but quickly enter nirvana.'"
Truly knowing the difficulty of expounding the Dharma,
how could it be considered easy?
Recalling the expedient means practiced by past buddhas,
he then rose from the Bodhi tree and went to the Deer Park,
according to the capacities of beings' roots,
expounded the great store of teachings.
Finally, gathering the causes and completing the result,
he nonetheless said:
"From the beginning at the Deer Park,
to the end at the Ajiravati River,
during this interval between the two,
not a single word was spoken."
This very thing is what Yángqí called the diamond circle and chestnut-bramble ball.
Truly it is hard to swallow, hard to penetrate.
If right here you can directly undertake and realize it,
the great Dharma not yet clarified,
still nothing can be done about it.
I dare ask all of you,
what is named the great Dharma?
How then to penetrate the diamond circle?

Have you not heard Yántóu say:

All buddhas appear in the world, patriarchs come from the west,

Thus a patriarch said:

Affairs and principle are both without obstruction,

If you understand these four lines,

Up to the differing intentions and circumstances of the ancients,
the profundity of mind and nature,

With a gentle pull, it moves.
One must raise one and understand three, discerning the slightest opportunity,

As soon as it's raised, it becomes clear.
Nowadays, various places have several

If the great Dharma is clarified,

become your own useful tools.
Some prefer the spark from struck stone, the lightning flash,
