Much speaking and many words

A thousand explanations, ten thousand explanations—

Suddenly, on the word "no," life is cut off,
and these principles too are flowers in the eye.
This matter is like the blue sky and bright sun.
Luminous and pure.
Unchanging and unmoving.
Neither decreasing nor increasing.
In each person's daily interactions and responses,
it is clear in every instance,
manifest in every thing.
Try to grasp it, but you cannot obtain it;

Vast and unobstructed,
clearly empty.
Like a gourd floating on water:
you cannot restrain it,
you cannot entangle it.
Throughout history, those who have attained the Way

emerging and submerging,
fully experiencing it as a whole,

They do not see any appearance of birth, death, or worldly troubles.

what then constitutes birth, death, and worldly troubles?
From where do birth, death, and worldly troubles arise?

Since there is no place to rest,
then Buddha is illusory, the Dharma is illusory.
The three realms, the twenty-five existences, the twelve sense bases, and the eighteen elements are all empty and vast.

even the word "Buddha" has no place to rest.

but only seek knowledge and understanding
in the ancient cases.

those with such views

The weak means the place of deviation is light,

Since you have already known of this great cause and condition,

constantly probing deeply beneath your own feet.
Probing back and forth,

Bare and naked, clean and free—there is nothing to grasp.

Proceeding in this way,

throughout future eons, one still cannot know the limits of the seas of lands within a single pore—their sequences, their treasuries, their distinctions, their universal interpenetration, their formation, their dissolution, and their adornments.

Holy names and ordinary labels are all empty sounds;

Such words strike stone men on the head—

People know the principle that worldly conditioned phenomena are illusory and unreal.

When everywhere there is attachment, then suffering is taken as pleasure.
Therefore Śākyamuni said to Maudgalyāyana:
"You take form and emptiness as opposing and contending within the Tathāgatagarbha,
yet the Tathāgatagarbha follows along as form and emptiness pervading the dharma realm."
Thus within it, wind moves, sky clears, sun shines, clouds darken.
Sentient beings are confused and dull, turning away from enlightenment to join with dust.
Therefore they generate defilements and have worldly appearances.
This is being deluded about the power of the Way
and being overcome by karmic power.
Śākyamuni also said:
"I, with wondrous illumination neither ceasing nor arising, unite with the Tathāgatagarbha,
and the Tathāgatagarbha is only wondrous awareness illuminating perfectly the dharma realm."
Thus within it, one becomes innumerable, innumerable become one.
The small manifests the great, the great manifests the small.
The unmoving site of enlightenment pervades the ten directions.
The body contains the ten directions' endless emptiness.
On a single tip of hair manifests a jeweled king's land.
Sitting within a minute dust particle turns the great dharma wheel.
This is the present activity
of not being deluded about the power of the Way and overcoming karmic power.
However, both places ultimately return to emptiness and illusion.
If abandoning karmic power yet grasping the power of the Way,
then I say such a person does not understand the Buddhas' expedient means of teaching according to circumstances.
Why?
Do you not see Śākyamuni said:
"If grasping dharma characteristics,
then one is attached to self, person, sentient being, and life span.
If grasping non-dharma characteristics,
then one is attached to self, person, sentient being, and life span."
Therefore one should not grasp dharma,
nor should one grasp non-dharma.
As previously stated: the power of the Way and karmic power fundamentally have no fixed measure.
If one is a wise man,
using the power of the Way as a weapon,
to expel karmic power,
when karmic power is eliminated, the Way is also illusory.
Therefore it is said:
"Only using provisional names,
to guide sentient beings."
Before recognizing and breaking through,
it is extremely difficult.
After recognizing and breaking through, what difficulty or ease remains?
Layman Páng said:
"Ordinary people's wisdom is narrow,
falsely speaking of difficulty and ease.
Departing from characteristics is like empty space,
completely realizing all Buddhas' wisdom.
Precept characteristics are also like space,
deluded people themselves create and uphold.
The root of sickness unwilling to pull out,
only playing with flowers and branches."
Want to know the root of sickness? It's nothing else,
just this grasping difficulty and ease, falsely producing acceptance and rejection.
If this root of sickness is not completely pulled out,
floating and sinking in the sea of birth and death,
truly there is no time of emergence.
Formerly, Scholar Zhāng Zhuō, just when the venerable pointed out his sickness source,
then understood and said:
"Cutting off afflictions doubly increases sickness,
heading toward true suchness is also deviation.
Following worldly conditions without obstruction,
nirvāṇa and birth-death are empty flowers."
To be direct without doubting the patriarchs and Buddhas, without doubting life and death,
just constantly let the mind be empty and open, when things come then deal with them accordingly,
like water's stillness, like a mirror's clarity.
Good and bad, beautiful and ugly arrive,
not a hair's breadth can escape.
Truly know the inconceivable realm of natural no-mind.
Recent monasteries have a kind of false Chán,
taking sickness as medicine.
They themselves have never had realization,
yet use enlightenment as establishment, use enlightenment as guiding words,
use enlightenment as falling into secondary importance,
use enlightenment as branch and leaf matters.
Since they themselves have never had realization,
they also don't believe others have realization.
Entirely with empty stillness stubbornly ignorant,
calling it the matter before the empty eon beyond Vairocana's sound,
daily just consuming two meals,
not attending to matters.
Always with drooping lips sitting meditation,
calling it 'cease and desist',
just involving language then calling it falling into present time,
also calling it descendants' matters.
Taking this black mountain ghost cave as the ultimate principle,
also saying 'the ancestor never left home',
using one's own foolishness to make others foolish.
Śākyamuni so-called:
"For example, someone plugs their own ears,
loudly shouting seeking others not to hear,
these people are called pitiable ones."
There is a kind of scholar-official,
initially having such poison enter their mind consciousness,
even if encountering true good knowing advisors,
speaking fundamental words,
instead consider it wrong.
These people are just like what the world calls tiger ghosts:
not only having their lives taken by them,
but also instead being used by them,
completely unaware.
Unless having past vow power,
constantly taking these two matters: living not knowing where from, dying not knowing where to,
stick them on the tip of the nose.
In tea, in meals, in quiet places, in noisy places,
thought after thought diligently, always like owing someone
millions in money debt with no way to pay,
heart and mind troubled, no way to avoid,
cannot seek life, cannot seek death.
At such time,
the paths of good and evil successively cut off.
When feeling like this,
exactly when to exert effort.
Just here look at a critical phrase:
A monk asked Zhàozhōu,
"Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not?"
Zhàozhōu said, "No."
When looking, don't use reasoning,
don't use explanation,
don't seek understanding,
don't accept at the opening,
don't make principles at the raising,
don't fall into empty stillness,
don't use mind waiting for enlightenment,
don't comprehend at the master's speaking,
don't fall into the armor of nothing-to-do.
Just while walking, standing, sitting, lying, constantly investigate:
"Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not?"
"No." When investigation becomes ripe,
verbal discussion and mental thought cannot reach,
within the mind seven up eight down,
like biting a raw iron stake with no flavor,
absolutely don't retreat in aspiration.
When reaching such time,
this is good news.
Don't you see ancient virtue said:
"The Buddha spoke all dharmas,
to save all minds.
I have no mind,
what use all dharmas?"
Not only in the patriarch's school like this,
the Buddha's entire canon,
entirely is this principle.
Sentient beings' evil karmic obstructions heavy,
daily getting out of bed,
then mind consciousness scattered, thinking of fame and profit,
carrying self and others,
deluded thoughts upside down,
from morning till night,
like interlocking chains continuously unbroken,
never tiring of it.
Suddenly arising one thought,
toward this gate putting intention considering,
then wanting to understand,
when mind consciousness cannot arrange,
then producing affliction,
early wanting to quit,
saying 'what's the point?'
Such people are countless.
Friend Shùnyuán is not like this.
Since knowing the various illusions in the deficient realm,
single-mindedly toward one's own footsteps investigate.
"Where does life come from?
Where does death go to?"
Since not knowing where from,
also not knowing where to,
presently clearly solitary awareness,
that distinguishes right and wrong, good and bad for people,
definitely is it existent or non-existent?
Is it real or illusory?
Straight until like drinking water, knowing for oneself cold or warm,
not receiving instruction from others' words, suddenly with a burst,
reaching the ultimate peaceful bliss, great rest great cessation place,
only then willing oneself.
With this scroll coming seeking instruction,
taking brush casually writing,
then completing this section of entanglements.
However, things don't arise alone,
arising necessarily has cause.
If always understanding as entanglements, how can one attain?
Don't you see formerly Master Zǐhú said:
"The patriarch coming from the west is just winter cold summer heat,
night dark day bright.
Only because you followers without intention create intention,
without matters produce matters,
without inside-outside forcibly make inside-outside,
without east-west recklessly speak east-west.
Therefore śamatha cannot be clear,
until sense bases and objects cannot be free."
By this measure,
Shùnyuán never came to Miàoxǐ seeking dharma words,
Miàoxǐ originally never wrote one word.
Winter cold summer heat, night dark day bright,
inside outside middle, east west south north,
originally never moved, changed, increased, decreased even slightly.
Why?
Our school has no verbal statements,
also has no dharma to give people.
Since having no dharma to give people,
then what is this presently written?
Winter cold summer heat, inside outside middle,
what is this?
East west south north never moving slightly,
what is this? Existent also cannot be obtained,
non-existent also cannot be obtained.
Winter cold summer heat also cannot be obtained,
inside outside middle also cannot be obtained,
one speaking thus also cannot be obtained,
one receiving thus also cannot be obtained,
one slight bit also cannot be obtained,
Shùnyuán also cannot be obtained,
Miàoxǐ also cannot be obtained,
cannot obtain also cannot be obtained.
Within cannot obtain, just thus obtain.
Shùnyuán arriving here, how should one investigate?
Just this 'how should one investigate' also has no place to stand.
Then this speech also not accepted,
this speech since not accepted,
Miàoxǐ definitely has no speaking,
Shùnyuán definitely has no hearing.
No speaking place is true speaking,
no hearing place is true hearing.
Thus then Miàoxǐ is Shùnyuán,
Shùnyuán is Miàoxǐ,
Miàoxǐ Shùnyuán not two, not divided,
not separate, not cut off.
Jiāzhōu's great statue eats huánglián,
Shǎnfǔ's iron cow full mouth bitter.
Bitter not bitter clearly,
look see nothing to see.
Kuàirán Jūshì Luó Zōngyuē,
in the late spring of the Shaoxing era's dīngchǒu year,
deliberately came to Màoshān to visit Miàoxǐ.
Wishing to thoroughly investigate this great matter of causation,
he repeatedly followed the assembly into the hall,
displaying his skills and flaunting his understanding.
All were dismissed.
Suddenly one day, Miàoxǐ saw from his expression that he
was peeking at a leopard through a tube—
turning his body and moving his brain,
he already had a verse in his sleeve.
Although it had not yet been presented,
Miàoxǐ immediately turned the pivot for him.
Though he had not yet leapt out of the entangling vines bare-boned,
he did come to know that rice makes meals and wheat makes noodles.
Just as he was at the point where effort was most needed,
he abruptly came to bid farewell, saying:
"I must urgently return to marry off my daughter."
With this scroll,
he begged for the principles of practice.
In the past, Layman Páng had said:
"Have a son but do not wed him,
have a daughter but do not marry her off.
Let us all gather round
and speak the wordless talk."
Later, during the Yuánfēng era,
there was a scholar
known as Layman Wúwéi,
surnamed Yáng, named Jié, courtesy name Cìgōng,
who had once studied under elders
and gained true attainment in the Chan school.
He once responded to Layman Páng's verse with this:
"A grown son must wed,
a grown daughter must marry.
What time is there for effort,
still speaking the wordless talk?"
These two worldly fellows,
taking this eternal field of the ten directions,
without obtaining the official seal,
each divided boundaries and claimed, "I know it exists,"
yet constantly honored themselves where no Buddha exists.
At that time, there was also one who was dissatisfied,
known as Chán Master Hǎiyìn Xìn,
then residing at Sūzhōu's Dìnghuì Temple.
Upon seeing Wúwéi's verse,
he too had a verse, saying:
"I have no son to wed,
nor daughter to marry off.
When tired, I simply sleep—
who cares for wordless talk?"
These three old men, with their three verses—
Kuàirán Jūshì, whether eyes open or closed,
or neither open nor closed,
is caught.
Miàoxǐ can only watch from the sidelines.
Watching is not nothing,
but after all, where is Kuàirán Jūshì caught—in the open-eyed state,
the closed-eyed state,
or the neither-open-nor-closed state?
If caught in the open-eyed state,
he falls into Layman Páng's trap.
If caught in the closed-eyed state,
he falls into Yáng Wúwéi's trap.
If caught in the neither-open-nor-closed state,
he falls into Chán Master Hǎiyìn's trap.
Hearing this, Kuàirán is sure to say,
"None of these!"
But if none of these,
he falls into Miàoxǐ's trap.
To escape the three elders' traps is easy;
to escape Miàoxǐ's trap is hard.
How, after all, can Kuàirán break free?
Wait until you return to Yánpíng and marry off your daughter,
then come back slowly,
and I will explain it for you.
Recalling an ancient virtue's verse,
I write it here as well,
hoping Kuàirán will not falter midway,
such is the earnestness of this grandmotherly heart.
The verse says:
"Learning the Way is like drilling for fire;
when smoke appears, do not stop.
Wait until the golden spark flashes—
then returning home, you reach the end."
One more question:
where, after all, is the home to which Kuàirán returns?
If you penetrate this question,
son's wedding and daughter's marriage are both within it.
If you do not yet know this home,
then with karmic consciousness vast and vague, you wander outside.
Nor can you blame Miàoxǐ.
Determined to thoroughly investigate this matter,
one should discard all previous clever explanations and reasoning,
memorization from texts and words,
and calculations and measurements within the mind-consciousness.
Cast them far away to other worlds,
not allowing even a speck to remain in the chest, sweeping everything completely clean.
Then, where thoughts and ideas cannot reach,
try taking a step forward to see.
If one can take this step,
it is like the youth Shàncáitóngzǐ in Pǔxián's pore-realms,
taking one step across innumerable, unspeakable Buddha-land dust-particle worlds.
Proceeding like this,
even through endless future kalpas, one still cannot know
the sequential realm-oceans within a single pore, the realm-ocean treasury,
the realm-ocean distinctions, the realm-ocean universal entry,
the realm-ocean formation and realm-ocean destruction,
the realm-ocean adornments and all their boundaries.
Nor can one know
the Buddha-ocean sequence, the Buddha-ocean treasury,
the Buddha-ocean distinctions, the Buddha-ocean universal entry,
the Buddha-ocean arising and Buddha-ocean cessation,
all their boundaries also unknowable.
The Bodhisattva assembly ocean sequence,
the Bodhisattva assembly ocean treasury,
the Bodhisattva assembly ocean distinctions,
the Bodhisattva assembly ocean universal entry,
the Bodhisattva assembly ocean gathering,
the Bodhisattva assembly ocean dispersion,
all their boundaries also unknowable.
Entering the realms of sentient beings and ghosts, sentient beings' faculties,
the wisdom that teaches and tames all sentient beings,
the profound freedom in which Bodhisattvas dwell,
the stages and paths Bodhisattvas enter,
all such oceans' boundaries
are believed to be known through no-thought and non-action.
There is such merit and virtue.
Although this step is said to be difficult to take,
if one has previously planted good roots and seeds,
simply look where faith reaches.
Looking and looking, internally nothing abides, externally nothing is clung to,
unaware and unknowing, the burden is lost.
At such a time,
one then knows what layman Páng Jūshì said:
"The thought-free cool monastery,
the empty-accumulation true Wǔtái.
Facing objects, the mind is undefiled;
encountering situations, the mind is like dead ashes.
Subtle truth manifests within;
Udumbara flowers bloom in emptiness.
The truth-eye seeks nothing;
free from characteristics, that is Thus-Come.
If you can learn like this,
unmoving, you transcend the three calamities."
These are true words, real words, neither deceptive nor false.
Yet even so,
do not think that because it's said this way,
you should go to the place of non-action and non-doing,
close your eyes and make a dead appearance,
calling it "silent yet constantly illuminating."
Forcibly grabbing the monkey's rope,
fearing it might jump around—
ancient masters called this the scattered soul of the nihilistic heretic, a dead person.
Truly wanting to end mental birth-and-death, wash mental defilements, cut through mental thickets—
one must beat this monkey to death with a single blow.
If you always tightly
hold the rope end,
subduing the mind,
I say this person
grasps it improperly,
truly pitiable.
Viewed with the true eye,
all are celestial demons, heretics, ghosts, and spirits,
not our kin.
This matter requires bearing it like solid steel forged, cast iron made.
If you intentionally bear it,
then you miss it again.
The ancients,不得已,
seeing you lost your way,
merely acted as guides pointing the way.
There is no Chan Way or Buddha-dharma to transmit.
If you say there is transmission and reception,
that is deviant dharma.
Why?
Don't you see the Diamond Sūtra says:
"If you say the Thus-Come One has spoken Dharma,
you slander the Buddha.
That person does not understand my meaning."
It also says:
"Dharma should be relinquished,
how much more non-dharma."
Truly speaking,
speaking of thusness and Buddha-nature,
speaking of bodhi and nirvana,
speaking of principle and phenomena,
speaking of deviant and correct—
all are non-dharma.
How can one further speak of mysteries and subtleties that can be transmitted and received?
Don't you see an earlier master said:
"Speaking of 'studying the Way'
is already just guiding words.
When did it ever tell you to create models and patterns,
specially seeking outside?"
Therefore it is said:
"Intending to study the profound with mind and thought,
is like heading west while facing east."
Línjì said:
"Just cease your thought-chasing mind,
then you're no different from Śākyamuni."
Seventh-ground Bodhisattvas' mind seeking Buddha-wisdom not yet ceased
is called affliction of dharma-dust.
Since you have determined resolve,
there must be a time when you attain entry.
So what is that time of attaining entry?
When suddenly the breath of mind-consciousness is extinguished—that is Buddha.
In principle, sudden awakening—with awakening, all is eliminated;
in phenomena, not suddenly removed—through sequence, gradually exhausted.
To understand these principles,
is like Shàncáitóngzǐ hearing Mílè's snap,
the tower gate opening,
Shàncáitóngzǐ's mind rejoicing,
entering, then it closes again.
Xiāngyán heard bamboo struck,
suddenly awakened,
then understood and said:
"One strike, all knowing gone;
no further need for cultivation.
Moving, expressing the ancient path;
not falling into silent mechanism"—this kind.
One's own awakening place, one's own peaceful joy place,
one's own strength place—others don't know.
Cannot pick it out to show people.
Except for those already awakened, already peaceful, already strong,
upon seeing, silently resonate.
If doubt not yet resolved,
just look at an ancient's entry phrase,
transferring the daily mind that makes fantasies
to the phrase—then all activity ceases.
A monk asked Zhàozhōu:
"Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not?"
Zhōu said: "No."
Just this one word
is the knife that severs the path of birth-and-death.
When false thoughts arise,
just raise "No."
Raising it and raising it,
suddenly all traces cut off—
that is returning home and sitting securely.
Beyond this, nothing special.
The previously mentioned difficult step
unexpectedly, suddenly, is passed.
Since knowing impermanence is swift and the matter of birth and death is great,
one must resolve to draw near to a good spiritual guide.
Diligently and tirelessly, without abandoning day or night,
always take the two words "birth and death"
and paste them on your forehead.
In tea and in meals, while sitting and while lying down,
when directing servants,
when handling household affairs,
when happy and when angry,
when walking and when staying,
when entertaining guests,
do not let them go.
Always as if there is one urgent, unfinished matter blocking your heart,
resolved to remove and sweep it away completely,
only then will there be some correspondence.
If only when hearing the ancestral teacher speak
do you then become anxious,
and when not speaking
you relax again,
then you lack a determined will.
To wish to sever the root of birth and death
will then be impossible.
This matter does not depend on male or female, monastic or lay.
If under the ancestral teacher's single word,
it breaks abruptly and severs explosively,
that is the point of thorough penetration.
The Buddha's parable of the burning house
truly opens the expedient gate for sentient beings and reveals the true reality.
Pointedly and precisely,
within it, it is said:
This house has only one door,
and moreover it is narrow and small.
The children are young,
and have no understanding.
This means sentient beings' faculties are narrow and inferior,
lacking determined resolve,
attached to birth, death, and worldly toils,
in worldly toils, heads emerging and heads submerging,
unable to leave the burning house of the three realms.
Therefore, he sets up various expedient means
to make sentient beings abandon expedients
and directly exit the burning house to sit in the open ground.
This is old man Shakyamuni's thoroughly compassionate heart.
Whenever reading sutras or the stories of ancient virtuous ones entering the Way,
one should see the moon and forget the finger;
absolutely must not get stuck in the words.
If seeking mystery and subtlety in the phrases,
seeking the extraordinary in the speech,
and practicing effort in such a place,
then one loses the expedient means.
Miàoxǐ has never had any real dharma to give people;
he simply settles the case according to the facts.
Taking what he has realized in his life,
he opens his mouth and reveals his guts,
clearly and directly speaking to people.
Those who can believe it
follow and practice it.
Although upon first hearing it,
it may seem hard to accept,
if the person has planted prajñā seeds since beginningless time,
as soon as it is mentioned,
their eyebrows stand upright,
and their eyes become fixed and moving.
When this old monk first dwelled on this mountain,
there was a laywoman named Wúzhe from the Xǔ family in Chángzhōu,
her dharma name Miàozǒng.
At thirty years old, she became firm,
cultivated practice, and widely visited various venerable masters,
all receiving their seal of approval.
However, because she truly feared the suffering of birth and death,
she wanted to truly understand the original destiny and final destination,
and specially came to the mountain for summer retreat.
At that time, there were seventeen hundred monastics sharing the summer retreat.
Féng Jìchuān, the junior minister,
was also at this mountain in the Unmoving Pavilion, following the assembly.
One day, because this old monk ascended the seat,
he brought up the story of Venerable Yàoshān first visiting Shítóu, asking Shítóu:
"The three vehicles and twelve divisions of teachings,
I have roughly studied and investigated.
I have heard that in the south there is direct pointing to the human mind, seeing nature and becoming a Buddha.
I truly do not understand it clearly.
I beg the teacher to instruct me."
Shítóu said:
"Thus is not right,
not thus is not right,
thus and not thus are both not right."
Yàoshān did not understand.
Shítóu said:
"You go to Jiāngxī and ask Great Master Mǎ."
Yàoshān followed the instruction and went to Great Master Mǎ's place,
asking as before.
Great Master Mǎ said:
"Sometimes I have him raise his eyebrows and blink his eyes,
sometimes I do not have him raise his eyebrows and blink his eyes,
sometimes having him raise his eyebrows and blink his eyes is right,
sometimes having him raise his eyebrows and blink his eyes is wrong."
Yàoshān under these words greatly awakened,
and had no more tricks to present,
but only bowed his head and paid homage.
Great Master Mǎ said:
"What principle have you seen that you pay homage?"
Yàoshān said:
"At Venerable Shítóu's place,
it was like a mosquito on an iron ox."
Great Master Mǎ affirmed him.
At that time, ascending the seat and just bringing it up again,
Wúzhe under the words suddenly understood.
After descending, she did not come to report.
At that time, Féng Jìchuān followed this old monk to the abbot's quarters and said:
"I understand."
The old monk asked him:
"How does the layman understand?"
Jìchuān said:
"Thus is not right,
sulu suopohe.
Not thus is not right,
xili suopohe.
Thus and not thus are both not right,
sulu xili suopohe."
The old monk neither told him it was right,
nor told him it was wrong.
Instead, he repeated Jìchuān's words to Wúzhe.
Wúzhe said:
"I have seen Guō Xiàng's commentary on Zhuāngzǐ.
Those who know say:
it is rather Zhuāngzǐ commenting on Guō Xiàng."
The old monk saw her words were unusual,
but did not ask her.
Instead, he brought up the story of Yántóu and the old woman and asked her.
Wúzhe then composed a verse saying:
"A single leaf boat floats on the vast expanse,
presenting oars and dancing paddles, apart from the musical notes.
Cloudy mountains and sea moon are all cast away,
gaining Zhuāng Zhōu's long butterfly dream."
The old monk also let it rest.
A year later, Jìchuān doubted her attainment was not real,
and specially went from Píngjiāng to summon Wúzhe,
asking her on his boat:
"The old woman gave birth to seven sons, six did not meet a connoisseur,
only this one is also unnecessary,"
and then abandoned it in the river.
"The teacher said
the laywoman understood.
How did you understand it?"
Wúzhe said:
"The above confession is entirely according to the facts."
Jìchuān was greatly astonished.
Also, once she came to the room,
the old monk asked her:
"The ancients did not leave the abbot's quarters;
why then did they go to the village to eat oily cakes?"
Wúzhe said:
"If the venerable lets Miàozǒng pass,
then Miàozǒng dares to communicate."
The old monk said to her:
"I let you pass;
you try to speak."
Wúzhe said:
"Miàozǒng also lets the venerable pass."
The old monk said:
"But what about the oily cakes?"
Wúzhe gave a shout and went out.
At that time, the whole assembly heard her reply like this.
See how with just one drop of water,
she could stir up waves.
Because she had severed worldly conditions early,
and early believed in this essential point,
and although once her face was sealed by a false teacher,
she was able to step back,
know it was not decisive,
and take awakening as the standard.
Therefore, as soon as she saw the good spiritual guide bringing it up,
under the words, a thousand understandings and a hundred correspondences.
The Lady of Yǒngníng Commandery, Cáo Shì Shànyīn,
intelligent, sharp, and wise,
knows there is this great matter of fundamental importance,
decisively capable of transcending birth and death,
not entangled by worldly toils.
Although in wealth and honor,
she is not trapped by wealth and honor.
She also wishes to step back and draw near to a good spiritual guide,
to resolve the great matter of birth and death.
But she has not yet met a true knowledgeable one to stimulate her.
Recently in the city,
because the festival commissioner invited me to her cloister garden to speak the Dharma,
Shànyīn heard this old monk bringing up this great matter of fundamental importance,
thus her innate nature was ignited,
and immediately her body and mind became peaceful and settled.
Although not yet fully ten parts penetrated and freed,
she has already recognized the many false and unreal matters within the burning house of worldly toils.
When the thirtieth day of the twelfth month arrives,
love and affection will be of no use,
power and influence will be of no use,
wealth and treasures will be of no use,
temperament will be of no use,
official position will be of no use,
wealth and honor will be of no use.
When the light of the eyes falls to the ground,
only the two paths of good and evil created in ordinary times
will appear one by one before you.
If evil is much and good is little,
then you will drift along following the evil karma.
If evil is little and good is much,
then you will be born into human or heavenly families of the ten goodnesses following the good karma.
Since you know these two paths are both illusory,
then generate a courageous, vigorous, steadfast, and unwavering mind,
resolved to transcend emotions, leave views, and penetrate birth and death.
On the thirtieth day of the twelfth month,
the two paths of good and evil
cannot constrain me.
Since you know there is such a supreme matter,
fearing you cannot attain it while in the burning house,
always draw near to a good spiritual guide.
Therefore, she specially came to Jìngshān to stay for ten days,
following the assembly to listen to the Dharma,
soaking in good conditions,
generating great vows,
never regressing.
Before leaving, she requested instruction with this scroll,
